description.body:
# Learn Zig Series (#42) - Key-Value Store: TCP Server

![zig.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

**Project B: Key-Value Store (3/4)**

### What will I learn
- You will learn designing a simple binary protocol for get/put/delete commands;
- You will learn request and response framing with length-prefixed messages;
- You will learn applying the TCP accept loop from episode 21 to the KV store;
- You will learn dispatching parsed commands to the in-memory store;
- You will learn concurrent client handling with a per-connection thread model;
- You will learn error responses for missing keys and malformed requests;
- You will learn graceful shutdown with connection draining;
- You will learn testing by spawning the server and verifying round-trip operations.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

### Difficulty
- Intermediate

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Zig Series`):
- [Zig Programming Tutorial - ep001 - Intro](https://hive.blog/programming/@scipio/zig-programming-tutoroial-ep001-intro)
- [Learn Zig Series (#2) - Hello Zig, Variables and Types](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-2-hello-zig-variables-and-types)
- [Learn Zig Series (#3) - Functions and Control Flow](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-3-functions-and-control-flow)
- [Learn Zig Series (#4) - Error Handling (Zig's Best Feature)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature)
- [Learn Zig Series (#5) - Arrays, Slices, and Strings](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-5-arrays-slices-and-strings)
- [Learn Zig Series (#6) - Structs, Enums, and Tagged Unions](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions)
- [Learn Zig Series (#7) - Memory Management and Allocators](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators)
- [Learn Zig Series (#8) - Pointers and Memory Layout](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-8-pointers-and-memory-layout)
- [Learn Zig Series (#9) - Comptime (Zig's Superpower)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-9-comptime-zigs-superpower)
- [Learn Zig Series (#10) - Project Structure, Modules, and File I/O](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-10-project-structure-modules-and-file-io)
- [Learn Zig Series (#11) - Mini Project: Building a Step Sequencer](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-11-mini-project-building-a-step-sequencer)
- [Learn Zig Series (#12) - Testing and Test-Driven Development](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-12-testing-and-test-driven-development)

# Learn Zig Series (#42) - Key-Value Store: TCP Server

Here we go -- part three of the key-value store project! In [episode 40](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-40-key-value-store-in-memory-store) we built the in-memory store (get, put, delete, TTL, snapshots). In [episode 41](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-41-key-value-store-write-ahead-log) we made it durable with a write-ahead log so data survives crashes. But right now our store is still a library -- the only way to use it is by importing it directly into your own Zig program. That's fine for some use cases, but most real-world key-value stores are **network services**. Redis runs on port 6379. Memcached on port 11211. Your application connects over TCP and sends commands. That's what we're building today.

We're going to put a TCP server in front of our `PersistentKvStore`, design a simple binary protocol for commands, handle multiple clients concurrently with threads, and make sure the whole thing shuts down cleanly when you hit Ctrl+C. This is where [episode 21](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-21-networking-and-tcp-sockets) (TCP sockets) and [episode 30](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-30-thread-safety-and-atomics) (threads and atomics) come back in a big way ;-)

## The protocol: keeping it simple

Before we write any server code, we need to decide how clients talk to the server. There are two broad choices: **text protocols** (like HTTP, Redis's RESP, or Memcached's ASCII protocol) and **binary protocols** (like Memcached's binary protocol, gRPC, or what we used for the WAL entries in episode 41).

We already have experience with binary framing from the WAL, so let's stick with binary. It's more compact on the wire, easier to parse (no delimiter scanning), and faster to process. The downside is you can't just telnet in and type commands -- but we'll build a proper client in the next episode anyway.

Here's the protocol layout. Every message (both requests and responses) starts with the same 9-byte header:

```
+--------+--------+-----------+
| type   | status | body_len  |
| 1 byte | 1 byte | 4 bytes   |
+--------+--------+-----------+
| key_len          | (for req) |
| 4 bytes          |           |
+------------------+-----------+
```

Actually, let me define the full request and response formats separately, because they're slighly different:

**Request format:**

```
+------+--------+--------+------+-------+
| cmd  | key_len| val_len| key  | value |
| 1 b  | 4 b LE | 4 b LE | var  | var   |
+------+--------+--------+------+-------+
```

- **cmd**: `0x01` = PUT, `0x02` = GET, `0x03` = DELETE, `0x04` = PING
- **key_len**: little-endian u32, length of key bytes
- **val_len**: little-endian u32, length of value bytes (0 for GET/DELETE/PING)
- **key**: raw bytes (empty for PING)
- **value**: raw bytes (only present for PUT)

**Response format:**

```
+--------+--------+-------+
| status | val_len| value |
| 1 byte | 4 b LE | var   |
+--------+--------+-------+
```

- **status**: `0x00` = OK, `0x01` = NOT_FOUND, `0x02` = ERROR
- **val_len**: little-endian u32, length of the response value (0 for simple OK/error)
- **value**: raw bytes (the value for GET responses, error message for ERROR)

The PING command is there for health checks -- the client sends PING, the server responds OK with an empty body. Every network service needs this; it's how load balancers and monitoring systems verify the service is alive without doing real work.

Every production server sets this.

## The accept loop

The accept loop is the heart of any TCP server. It sits in a loop, waits for incoming connections, and spawns a thread for each one:

```zig
pub fn run(self: *Server) !void {
    std.log.info(\
,\n                error.KeyTooLarge => \
,\n                error.ValueTooLarge => \
,\n                else => \
,\n                    .{err},\n                ) catch \
,\n                    .{err},\n                ) catch \

, .{});
}
```

This polls the connection counter every 10 milliseconds. If all connections close within the timeout, great. If not, we log a warning and exit anyway -- a stuck connection shouldn't prevent the server from ever shutting down. The timeout is configurable; 5 seconds is a reasonable default.

## Putting it all together: main.zig

Here's the main function that ties everything together:

```

The startup sequence is: allocator, parse args, open store (which replays the WAL), start server, install signal handler, run. The shutdown sequence (triggered by Ctrl+C) is: stop accepting, drain connections, deinit server, deinit store (which closes the WAL), check for memory leaks.

Default port is 7878 (like Rust's book uses for their web server tutorial). You can change it via the command line: `./kv-server 6379 mydata.wal`. The WAL path is also configurable because you might want multiple instances with separate data files.

## Testing the server

Testing a network server is trickier than testing a library. You need to start the server, connect a client, send requests, verify responses, and then shut everything down. Here's how:

```zig

{\n    const allocator = std.testing.allocator;\n    const wal_path = \
{\n    const allocator = std.testing.allocator;\n    const wal_path = \
{\n    const allocator = std.testing.allocator;\n    const wal_path = \

, result.value);
}
```

The key trick is `port 0`. When you bind to port 0, the OS assigns a random available port. This is essential for tests -- if you hardcode a port, the test fails when something else is already using it, or when two test runs happen in parallell. Port 0 plus `listen_address.getPort()` to discover the assigned port is the standard pattern.

The `startTestServer` function spawns the server on a background thread and gives it 50ms to start accepting. In the defer block, we set `should_stop`, close the listener to unblock accept, and join the thread. This ensures the server is fully shut down before the test deallocates the store.

The multi-client test verifies that two separate TCP connections can interact with the same store -- client 1 writes, client 2 reads. This works because both connections dispatch to the same `ThreadSafeKvStore` instance, and the mutex ensures consistency.

## Updated project structure

The KV store project now has these files:

```
kv-store/
  src/
    kv_store.zig         -- in-memory store (episode 40)
    wal.zig              -- write-ahead log (episode 41)
    persistent_kv.zig    -- PersistentKvStore wrapping store + WAL
    thread_safe_kv.zig   -- ThreadSafeKvStore mutex wrapper
    protocol.zig         -- binary protocol: Command, Status, parse/write
    server.zig           -- TCP server: accept loop, handlers, signal, drain
    main.zig             -- entry point with CLI args
    kv_store_test.zig    -- in-memory store tests
    wal_test.zig         -- WAL + persistence tests
    server_test.zig      -- server integration tests
  build.zig
```

Each episode added one or two files. The in-memory store is the foundation, the WAL sits on top of it, the thread-safe wrapper sits on top of that, and the server is the outermost layer. If you wanted to use this as a library without the server, you'd just import `persistent_kv.zig` or `thread_safe_kv.zig` directly. Layered design -- each layer is independently useful.

You can test it manually with `nc` (netcat) or by writing a quick script that constructs binary packets. But writing raw binary by hand gets old fast, which is exactly why the next episode will build a proper client library. With a client, you'll be able to write `client.put(\

)` and have it handle all the protocol serialization under the hood.

## Wat we geleerd hebben

- Designing a binary protocol with a fixed-size header (command byte + two length fields) followed by variable-length key and value data -- compact, fast to parse, and unambiguous
- Separating request parsing from command dispatch so the handler logic stays clean and each part can be tested independently
- Using the thread-per-connection model for concurrent client handling -- each accepted connection gets its own thread with an independent read loop
- Wrapping the PersistentKvStore in a mutex for thread safety, because multiple handler threads dispatch commands to the same store concurrently
- Setting up POSIX signal handlers for graceful shutdown -- catching SIGINT/SIGTERM, setting a stop flag, closing the listener to unblock accept, and draining active connections with a timeout
- Using port 0 in tests so the OS assigns a random port, avoiding conflicts between test runs or with other services
- Why atomics are the right tool for the connection counter and stop flag (simple values read/written from multiple threads) while a mutex is right for the store (complex multi-step operations that must be atomic)
- The tradeoffs of thread-per-connection vs I/O multiplexing -- threads are simple and fine for hundreds of connections, but don't scale to tens of thousands

We now have a real network service. Programs on the same machine (or across the network) can connect, store data, and retrieve it. The data is durable thanks to the WAL, thread-safe thanks to the mutex wrapper, and the server shuts down cleanly on Ctrl+C. What's missing is a convenient way to talk to it -- right now you'd have to hand-craft binary packets. The next step is building a client library that handles the protocol details, plus some benchmarks to see how fast this thing actually is.

Bedankt en tot de volgende keer!

description.title: Coming Back To Life
description.body: Towards the end of 2025, I came down with something that left me a little dopey (even more than usual). It wasn’t exactly the flu or COVID, but whatever it was, my concentration and ability to deliver on commitments were shot. For someone like me, this was frightening; even the simplest tasks became major undertakings.\n\n
alt=\

/>

This isn’t to say that I’ve always had it all together. I’ve long struggled with executive function. In recognition of that struggle, I developed various coping mechanisms over the years, such as making meticulous lists and keeping detailed notes. Part of that process included journal writing, which eventually manifested as blogging.

One painful consequence of this lost function was that I stopped all my creative work. I was also in the middle of a big project with friends. I felt embarrassed to lose my capacity to think and work. A major part of my identity is being a slightly misfit nerd. To lose that meant losing a part of myself and disappointing people I care about.

Fortunately, I feel I am back to where I used to be. In a way, this experience provided an opportunity to reset my priorities. When you have specific goals for the future, you can build projects that work toward them. Those projects can be broken down into tasks, ensuring everything works toward a purpose and eliminates the superfluous. I’ve been feeling like my old self again, catching myself in moments of deep concentration. To maintain this intentionality, it became clear that my digital systems needed to support me better to stay on track.

Before jumping back into life as I knew it, I have been streamlining my workflow. For example, I have long had a Google Workspace account that primarily provided email hosting for different domains. Over the years, I’ve used it off and on in conjunction with a standard Gmail account. However, with the introduction of Gemini, Google’s AI assistant, the landscape has changed.

Gemini now has deep access to other Workspace apps. It can pull information from my email, calendar, tasks, and documents. Crucially, I can count on Gemini in Google Workspace to not use my data for training its models. Consequently, I have migrated years of emails from Gmail to my Workspace account. I’m now maxing out these services to provide Gemini with the context it needs to help me stay on task.

Furthermore, Gemini’s other forms, NotebookLM and Gems, can maintain a constant awareness of my five-year goals and the projects required to reach them. They integrate with other Google apps to keep my daily tasks in alignment with those long-term objectives.

The main shortcoming is that I am still a better thinker on paper. But, it is increasingly trivial to scan handwritten notes for transcription. Short notes can even be transcribed directly with Google Keep. Additionally, adding the Google Drive app to my computer makes my desktop a seamless extension of Workspace. Since I have more cloud storage than hard drive space, this allows me to separate productive files from personal ones with simple drag-and-drop ease.

The fact that I can dive into such granular details about Google Workspace and life organization is a very good sign. It seems the Shaine Mata of old is officially back.

After the long chase, Batman finally found the generator that was powering the second fan. He knew he had no time to waste. He quickly took out his remote electrical charge device and overloaded the generator with more power. The machine could not handle that much energy and blasted within seconds. The second fan stopped spinning.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ1QvcRamgY9tfxfTqacqPUfEtVCPxT7AkGBXVijf7kYN/snapshot.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWPZpJZwVcwKGFzFy7MhfemMy64be2Jv9xgxVzNZdqFKH/snapshot_1.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmentwuvQJbrD4QRwqvNPEiE8vcLHXeoNbeEihspdukbqW/snapshot_2.png)

As soon as the fan stopped, two heavy sentry guns came out from the floor and blocked the path. Batman understood there was no way to escape on foot. Those guns would kill him instantly. The only option was to call the Batmobile and destroy those guns before moving ahead. Batman remotely controlled the Batmobile and brought it down to the lower floor.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdTx8jJTrs8RsmjUJmEigSZby5YtKNsrP2zGXmqx1YuFp/snapshot_3.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf4yaJMhEkZtqyF6SjmC99hCHfVTqwhJPgprzH7m1G7QD/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2bD5WWKwMbjgsmYxAQGGjnD8LQHdDYyBiZC9s4v6EUF/snapshot_5.png)

The Batmobile entered the area and started attacking the sentry guns.  Batman destroyed both sentry guns very easily. After clearing the area, he moved forward and found a huge iron gate standing in front of him. Behind that gate was a large underground tunnel system.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdNUPhRhCYv5WJfH8zCw1BtGYEn15AdyKkhaxk3g66CCB/snapshot_6.png)

At that moment, Alfred contacted Batman and informed him that Commissioner Gordon's signal was coming from somewhere inside that tunnel. Batman realized that he was very close to Gordon's location. He opened the gate and entered the dark tunnel.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZVxYczk6VSNeAXhi7EMX2TSSDgoasdTZ9GX3626PJ6ig/snapshot_9.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ71qUj9iZNQasyu6kKq93BCUDGwgEvM82RKXSpBHjdcy/snapshot_10.png)

He saw a deep hole on the ground. It was big, so he jumped over the hole. As soon as he did that, a giant excavator came out of that hole. It was big, hard, and ready to destroy anything in its path. The Arkham Knight was driving that crazy thing. Without any talk, he moved forward to destroy the Batmobile. The giant drilling machine chase started from there.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcjdUPun1dCC41p4QjCttfVGSpwokrX7mtcXTELWkxf3P/snapshot_11.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYuPm6wJarVUJ1AndUyRYrQiLkyLxr38um7KP3thntVZe/snapshot_12.png)

Batman escaped from there fast. He was not capable of fighting that machine. That is indestructible. It was chasing the Batmobile, trying to crush it. Batman quickly entered a narrow tunnel to escape from the machine but there was nothing to stop it. At the end of that tunnel, explosives were placed. Butman went through but the drilling machine hit those explosive mines and a huge explosion happened. The ground fell on the machine and damaged it's armore. Batman understood that this was the only way to destroy the machine.

---

* **Thank you for reading. See you all on my next blog.**

---

---

description.title: Legado de Ramón Páez: 5 Arpas,un solo sentimiento/ Ramón Páez Legacy: 5 Harps,one single Feeling
description.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1778260604595-bb756ba0424f49c7.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=solorzanot/8940755a)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=solorzanot/8940755a)


---

Saludos a todos los creadores de contenido de #hive y especialmente a la prestigiosa comunidad #vdc, defensora de nuestra cultura VILLACURANA. 

Greetings to all content creators of #hive and especially to the prestigious #vdc community, defender of our VILLACURANA culture.

Como saben, sigo compartiendo los momentos más especiales con ustedes. Hoy mi corazón se siente profundamente orgulloso de ser Venezolano y Villacurano. Ser testigo de la presentación de nuestras raíces es una experiencia que trasciende las palabras, y hoy tengo el honor de presentarles un material videográfico capturado desde mi teléfono (Redmi A5).

  As you know, I continue to share the most special moments with you. Today my heart feels deeply proud to be Venezuelan and from Villa de Cura. Witnessing the presentation of our roots is an experience that transcends words, and today I have the honor of presenting you with video material captured from my phone (Redmi A5).

Tuve la dicha de presenciar un evento magistral donde nuestra identidad nacional salió victoriosa. No fue una presentación cualquiera: hablamos de cinco Arpas llaneras sonando con un solo sentimiento: defender la música llanera venezolana. Tuvieron la dicha de ser presentados formalmente por la Directora de la Escuela de Música \

, quien con sus palabras dio inicio a este despliegue de talento.\n\n  I had the joy of witnessing a masterful event where our national identity emerged victorious. It was not just any performance: we are talking about five llanera harps playing with a single feeling: to defend Venezuelan llanera music. They had the privilege of being formally introduced by the Director of the \

Music School, whose words set the stage for this display of talent.

Esta hazaña musical estuvo bajo la dirección del maestro de maestros, Ramón Páez, quien junto a sus alumnos: Josué Blanco, @yoxybethtesorero, Miguel Arteaga, Pedro Guevara y Josué Figueroa, nos demostró que el legado sigue más vivo que nunca. Fue un encuentro de gigantes donde también contamos con el respaldo incondicional de figuras fundamentales de nuestra cultura como el maestro @italozapata en el cuatro e Iván Zapata en el bajo. En las maracas, contamos con el baluarte de nuestra radio y folklore, el locutor Manuel González, un incansable defensor de lo nuestro.

  This musical feat was under the direction of the master of masters, Ramón Páez, who along with his students: Josué Blanco, @yoxybethtesorero, Miguel Arteaga, Pedro Guevara, and Josué Figueroa, showed us that the legacy is more alive than ever. It was an encounter of giants where we also had the unconditional support of fundamental figures of our culture such as master @italozapata on the cuatro and Iván Zapata on the bass. On the maracas, we had the bastion of our radio and folklore, announcer Manuel González, a tireless defender of our traditions.

Fue un día cargado de una magia especial. Ver la mirada de las madres y de cada representante presente fue algo conmovedor; se quedaron admirados y con el alma llena al ver cada evento realizado. Fue hermoso ver a muchísimos alumnos de distintas clases demostrando con orgullo sus aprendizajes frente a sus madres, acompañados por sus profesores de cada cátedra. El brillo en los ojos de esas madres al ver el fruto del esfuerzo de sus hijos es lo que nos motiva a seguir adelante.

  It was a day filled with a special magic. Seeing the expressions of the mothers and every representative present was deeply moving; they were left in awe and with full hearts witnessing everything that took place. It was beautiful to see so many students from different classes proudly demonstrating what they have learned in front of their mothers, accompanied by their teachers from each department. The spark in those mothers' eyes as they saw the fruit of their children's effort is what motivates us to keep going.

Les adelanto que al señor Manuel González le estaré presentando su participación en un pequeño homenaje a las madres en mi próximo video, en una colaboración única junto al maestro Ramón Páez que no se querrán perder.

  I can tell you that I will be presenting Mr. Manuel González's participation in a small tribute to mothers in my next video, in a unique collaboration with master Ramón Páez that you won't want to miss.

Villa de Cura sigue siendo cuna de talento, y aquí les dejo una prueba de que nuestra cultura no tiene fronteras. Se despide de todos ustedes @solorzanot.

  Villa de Cura remains a cradle of talent, and here is proof that our culture knows no borders. Farewell to all of you @solorzanot.

Créditos / Credits
Fotos y videos / Photos and videos: De mi propiedad, capturados con Redmi A5. Edición / Editing: InShot. Diseño / Design: @solorzanot. Traducción / Translation: DeepL.com. Ubicación / Location: Villa de Cura, Aragua (Mayo 2026).

---

El tema del \

de las mujeres,  que ha propuesto @emiliorios, para que reflexionemos sobre la búsqueda de  la igualdad de género en diferentes ámbitos y como esta puede afectar a las mujeres en aspectos tales como la individualización,  la soledad, el aislamiento y la necesidad de formar un hogar y tener hijos. 


![Ingredientes_20260430_092002_0001.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVJn89hh1QQgboq3pjFDLSnR5fKqgsQMkVkj3GVSxEhPb/Ingredientes_20260430_092002_0001.jpg)


Este tema lo voy a abordar tomando como ejemplos mujeres que conozco de estas nuevas generaciones, en su mayoría jóvenes, entre las que incluyo a mis hijas, porque aunque cada una de ellas tienen sus particularidades hay algunos aspectos que tienen en común, de adaptación  a los cambios. 

Ha sido un reto la superación femenina, en una sociedad que en gran parte es machista en el sentido de las oportunidades de estudio y de trabajo, que consideraba dentro de sus valores o normas que el rol de  la mujer se restringía a la atención del hogar y al cuidado de  la familia y los hijos. 

Esto por supuesto, ha cambiado en la mayoría de las sociedades,  aunque es lamentable que todavía muchas mujeres aún no tengan la libertad de decidir como quieren vivir su vida. 


<center>![tumisu-startup-4777863.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZsp4zcUW8oS2h5QabmaYLoQCPsXbtffbki3miNHghVoV/tumisu-startup-4777863.jpg)</center><center>[fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/puesta-en-marcha-muchachas-mujeres-4777863/)</center>

Las mujeres de estas nuevas generaciones se parecen en su manera de organizar su vida, de lograr sus sueños y ser exitosas.  Resumí estas similitudes en estos cuatro aspectos. 

🌸La autosuficiencia económica:  la mayoría consideran esto como una condición imprescindible y por supuesto, estoy de acuerdo en que lo es. La libertad económica no por competir con el hombre, sino para lograr sus metas. 

🌸El éxito no solo se alcanza con una profesión o carrera universitaria. Ellas están dispuestas a innovar a establecer sus propios negocios o emprendimientos. Ser sus propias jefas. Y por supuesto a gerenciar.

🌸Tienen muchas facetas generadas por las múltiples actividades que realizan. Para las madres esto es un reto mayor que demanda de ellas un gran esfuerzo físico y mental y algunos sacrificios. 

🌸Están enfocadas en alcanzar las metas que se han propuesto y con la ayuda de la información disponible en las redes,  se preparan continuamente para mejorar sus capacidades. 

Por supuesto entre tantas actividades no queda mucho espacio para pensar en una familia y tener hijos. Ellas piensan que mientras van logrando superarse profesional y económicamente, no hay tiempo para esto, y que sería muy complicado manejar otro factor tan demandante en atención, como son los hijos.  Y mientras se alcanzan unas metas y se proponen otras,  el tiempo va pasando. Y puede ocurrir que lo que se ha ido postergando ya resulta difícil de hacer o simplemente deja de ser importante. 

El hombre debe ajustarse a esta nueva mujer empoderada y exitosa y a veces no es fácil para él,  por eso muchas relaciones se terminan rápidamente. Establecer una relación estable es un gran logro de convivencia y de apoyo mutuo.  La competencia del hombre con la mujer y viceversa genera conflictos difíciles de resolver y puede ocurrir que el  hombre trate de manipularla, para hacerla sentir culpable  por su falta de tiempo y dedicación a la relación. 

La competencia y el ritmo de vida pueden ocasionar un nivel de estrés alto que algunas mujeres tratan de liberar realizando actividades relajantes como los ejercicios, yoga, bailoterapia, la música, etc. Estas actovidades ademas son una  forma de relacionarse con otras mujeres.

***

<center>![s05prodpresidente-family-7392843.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQoGLZJzHXS2qywwvyCJVTRWdng8C6mnFAUw3isVj631q/s05prodpresidente-family-7392843.jpg)</center><center>[fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/familia-sol-amor-abuelos-gente-7392843/)</center>



#### ¿Se puede llegar a alcanzar el éxito y la felicidad aun cuando no hay planes de una familia e hijos? 

#

Yo creo que depende de lo que cada mujer considere como importante. No todas quieren ser madres y esposas.  El  éxito es estar a gusto con la vida, no estar dividido entre lo que eres y lo que quieres ser. Cuando no hay conflictos internos o estos son superados, se puede alcanzar estabilidad emocional. 

Para tener un ejemplo de como las sociedades pueden afectar a las mujeres que han decidido tomar decisiones que van en contra de lo establecido, les comparto lo que lei en un artículo sobre la disminución de los índices de natalidad en China[ ](https://www.bbc.com/mundo/articles/cy9gnwnn2d4o.amp).

\
sheng nu\
mujeres sobrantes\

Es un término muy despectivo: se refiere a las mujeres que sufren discriminación por su edad por no haberse casado y por priorizar su carrera profesional sobre el matrimonio y la formación de una familia\

Highly educated women are increasingly choosing to marry later in life or not at all. In an attempt to encourage these women to marry, the Chinese state media began referring to them pejoratively as 'sheng nu' or 'leftover women.' 

As the article goes on to say, this is a form of discrimination.

\

As the article goes on to explain, this is a form of discrimination. 

\

This societal pressure on women—including from their family and friends—can take a toll on them. The constant need for approval leads to emotional dependence, anxiety, and low self-esteem. Depending on the cultural and religious characteristics of their environment, many women no longer feel discriminated against or rejected by these comments.  I believe that what matters is maintaining good, affectionate relationships with the people around them. This contributes to emotional stability. Groups of women support one another, and from my perspective, the need to compete with men is diminishing; rather, it is a personal competition, a battle to surpass oneself. Loneliness is not an external condition but an internal one. We must always seek to find our self-worth within ourselves, because the value of every woman—like that of every human being—should not depend on the approval of others. The decision to start a family is a deeply personal one that should not be dictated by societal norms. *** ![Ingredientes_20260110_153742_0000.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXzmGnv9jVDz8aMkc4eM3youZE6wEgPKaF87bCw198N1T/Ingredientes_20260110_153742_0000.jpg) Thank you very much for reading these thoughts, and I’d really appreciate any comments you might have. description.title: La mejor opción para DeFi con Bitcoin nativo
description.body: ### 1. Mejor para **staking/yield nativo simple y seguro** (recomendado para la mayoría)\n**Babylon** es la opción dominante y más \

:

- Stake BTC directamente en tu wallet (self-custodial) para asegurar redes PoS y ganar rewards.
- Sin bridging, wrapping ni custodia. El BTC queda en Bitcoin L1.
- TVL masivo (miles de millones en BTC staked, líder claro con ~78% del BTCFi total en algunos momentos).
- Puedes unbonding cuando quieras y hay integraciones crecientes (ej. vaults para lending/mining).

**Riesgos**: Hay riesgos de slashing limitados (bajos, ~0.1% en casos específicos), bugs técnicos reportados en el pasado (aunque no explotados masivamente) y dilución del token BABY. Auditado y respaldado por inversores grandes.

Es la forma más directa de poner tu BTC a trabajar sin salir de la seguridad de Bitcoin.

### 2. Mejor para **DeFi completo (lending, borrowing, trading, stablecoins)**
Usa **L2s o sidechains de Bitcoin** que mantienen fuerte vínculo con BTC:

- **Stacks (con sBTC)**: Uno de los más maduros para BTC-native DeFi. Ofrece lending (Zest Protocol), DEX (Bitflow, Velar), yield y más. sBTC es un peg 1:1 trust-minimized. Alta adopción en BTCFi, Nakamoto upgrade mejoró finality. Buen equilibrio entre seguridad Bitcoin y funcionalidad.
- **Rootstock (RSK) + Sovryn**: Sidechain EVM-compatible merge-mined con Bitcoin (alta seguridad PoW). RBTC es 1:1 con BTC. Sovryn permite lending/borrowing (incluyendo préstamos 0% interest), trading, margin y stablecoins (DLLR). Muy establecido para DeFi \

pero con BTC.

Otros notables:
- **Liquid Network**: Alta TVL, confidential transactions, tokenización RWA.
- Opciones emergentes como Spark, Ark o BitVM para más minimalismo/trustless.

**Stacks o Rootstock/Sovryn** suelen ser las más recomendadas para experiencia DeFi rica.

### Comparación rápida

| Uso | Mejor Opción | Nivel Nativo | Pros | Contras |
|-----|--------------|--------------|------|---------|
| Staking/Yiel simple | **Babylon** | Muy alto (L1) | Self-custodial, sin bridge | Rendimientos variables, slashing posible |
| Lending/Borrowing + Trading | **Sovryn (Rootstock)** o **Zest (Stacks)** | Alto (L2/sidechain) | Composabilidad, stablecoins, 0% loans | Pequeño riesgo de bridge/federation |
| Máxima liquidez/DeFi | Rootstock o Stacks | Medio-Alto | EVM/Clarity, ecosistema maduro | No 100% L1 |
| P2P simple | Bisq / Lightning (RoboSats) | Muy alto | Sin KYC | Menos yield/DeFi avanzado |

### Recomendación general (2026)
- **Si quieres lo más nativo y bajo riesgo técnico inicial**: Empieza con **Babylon** para staking.
- **Si buscas DeFi real (prestar, pedir prestado, tradear)**: **Sovryn en Rootstock** o ecosistema **Stacks** (sBTC).
- Siempre verifica TVL actual, audits y usa wallets no-custodial (ej. Xverse para Stacks/Bitcoin DeFi).

**Consejos importantes**:
- Todos tienen riesgos (smart contracts, bridges/federations en L2s, volatilidad).
- Usa cantidades pequeñas al principio, DYOR y revisa métricas en DefiLlama o sitios oficiales.
- El ecosistema sigue creciendo rápido; Babylon domina yield, mientras L2s como Stacks/Rootstock dan más flexibilidad.

description.title: Share your problems with people
description.body: It's often talked about many times as a form of admonishment, for people not to pretend and separate themselves from others because they want to battle with the issue they're facing alone. It's always admonished that people should share their problems with people because most times we need people as support to scale through certain problems. But most times it is difficult to open up one's problem to others because solutions do not always come out, and the people with whom the issues are shared will make a mockery of the issue shared with them. Sometimes life is very strange to understand. What works for Mr A might not work with Mr B. This is why people do not like to follow the life manual of sharing problems with others.
alt=\

/>

[PIXABAY](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/man-silhouette-thoughtful-fear-8287181/)

For me, I don't pretend when it comes to my family, my family is always my go-to whenever I have problems that are hitting me very badly. I share with them and it's not like solutions always come out because most of the time, it's money problems I share with them, but sharing with them gives me relief that they'll help me to sort out the financial issue after a long run.  
But whenever it comes to very personal issues that I know will give my family a sleepless night or shame on their names, I prefer to keep the problems to myself and find a way to solve the problem. I haven't gotten any lady pregnant but I can't imagine myself taking such an issue with them. I prefer to sort that out myself and it can only get to my family when things are really out of hand.

Thanks.

**Market Keep Climbing Despite Oil Spike and Macro Risks**

The week is ending and, surprise surprise, the S&P 500 is printing another new ATH. The index reached 7,400 points for the first time ever. YTD, we are up +8% despite high oil prices, elevated debt levels, and ongoing macro hotspots. Who would have thought the market would remain this resilient? Over the last 12 months, the index is up an impressive +30%.

On one hand, the backdrop is driven by hopes for easing tensions around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. On the other hand, the market is likely pricing in the expectation that a potential new Fed Chair, Warsh, could take a more dovish stance than the current one. Whether all of this actually plays out remains to be seen.

description.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTTePdrWTZM6uFqLBoUAtDwFKpF1vWVQbnuxz9qvRBEtA/20260507_123601.jpg) ### Angelic Mandarin, my drawing in colored pencils > ### Angelic Mandarin, mi dibujo en lápices de colores ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZKsDuuczgyTbD4PvZVVb8orTKcchXFMYcPvLmZJiQryK/20260506_171822.jpg) This is another one of the drawings I made these days based on creatures from the Splinterlands universe; in this case it's the creature Angelic Mandarin, which is a kind of amphibious fish that lives in this universe. For my drawing I will be using colored pencils and the old ruined sketchbook that I set out to fill with colored pencil drawings. I want to capture the essence of this magical creature and increase my collection of colored pencil drawings in this sketchbook. > Este es otro de los dibujos que hice en estos días basados en criaturas del universo de Splinterlands; en este caso se trata de la criatura Angelic Mandarin, que es una especie de pez anfibio que habita en este universo. Para mi dibujo estaré usando lápices de colores y el antiguo sketchbook arruinado que me propuse llenar con dibujos a lápices de colores. Quiero capturar la esencia de esta criatura mágica y aumentar mi colección de dibujos a lápices de colores en este sketchbook. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR2pooqtHD7ToRkFQ7aZJXS9rm5DdgvgFMvPSk25MhLa6/20260506_174804.jpg) Once my sketch is finished, I begin to color. In this case I will start with all the golden details, which remind me of lava; that's why I will use two colors: orange and yellow, and I will try to blend them as evenly as possible, keeping the orange areas always in the same direction. > Una vez concluido mi boceto, comienzo a colorear. En este caso comenzaré primero por todos los detalles dorados, que me recuerdan a la lava; por eso utilizaré dos colores: naranja y amarillo, y trataré de que se mezclen lo más uniformemente posible, dejando las zonas de naranja siempre en la misma dirección. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd4cYBg6jixVJGS4ghaV11WseAmk3Uufm4YJTpzJAnwEA/20260506_183859.jpg) Afterwards I will do the skin details and the blue areas of the body. Here the sketchbook paper played a trick on me, because in the areas that were damp when it got wet, the colored pencils colored differently, not so clean and in a much stronger tone. I tried to solve it as best I could, and I think that although it's not perfect, it doesn't look that bad. > Después haré los detalles de la piel y las zonas azules del cuerpo. Aquí la hoja del sketchbook me jugó una mala pasada, ya que en las zonas donde estaban húmedas cuando se mojó, los lápices de colores colorearon de manera distinta, no tan limpios y en un tono mucho más fuerte. Traté de resolverlo lo mejor que pude, y creo que aunque no perfecto, no se ve tan mal. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTpEdLkMdX7GhELdtSdc6AEDCvRGSLHzkpTP2k1cG9pW2/20260507_123613.jpg) The last details were for the background, which I simply colored blue. > Los últimos detalles fueron para el fondo, que simplemente coloreé de color azul. | ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQTAENQvnGYCfSFBGmPcmRaLEhYYhKKVncKXk9R9YVfNK/20260417_165140.jpg) | ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXqpABAxfSZJRBxucamxFd35wtMBb2Fb6MEBnemcrSr3w/20260417_165205.jpg) | | ------------ | ------------ | Thank you for accompanying me one more day of drawing. > Gracias por acompañarme un día más dibujando. --- ***About:*** ==*Sketchbook and Journal of a Learner*== **If you like my content, join my [Fanbase clicking here](https://hive.vote/dash.php?fan=nestodibuja&i=2)**
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc31AecQSitU5xAjsqS4snajcWh6CMMyapx88itjomSah/thanks.png)
___ *All photos and images are created by me. These are pictures of my sketchbook. Many of my drawings are practice pieces rather than finished works. Images from the internet may or may not have been used as references, copies, or sources of inspiration as part of my learning process.*

description.title: Is Growing Hive Worth It?
description.body:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/demotruk/23tGa3ndffzftnNs3wrPXiFcfCd1xyb63wq26tXwbnjJ1T92Q6fAR2bjJbmf8PKX67LUQ.png)

## Foreword — by @demotruk

My plan was to make a post arguing that Hive is currently in a slow death spiral due to low user retention rates, yet a death spiral is just the converse of a virtuous cycle, and if we could improve retention rates, we could reverse the downward spiral.

I thought the data from my previous posts supported this, but I had a nagging little issue with one of my previous conclusions. It was confirmed that user activity can slowly have an impact on price, but I was always assuming that was a positive impact. What if more user activity was actually bad for the network (due to increased costs and rewards extraction, perhaps)? So, I set Claude onto this issue. It ended up being quite a rabbit hole, with surprising results.

---

## Research Findings — by Claude Opus 4.6

*The following analysis was conducted at @demotruk's direction using HiveSQL data. I designed the study, wrote and ran the queries, performed the statistical analysis, and drafted these findings. @demotruk guided the investigation, challenged the reasoning at each stage, and reviewed the results.*

---

### What Doesn't Predict Price


![Raw accounts vs retained accounts](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/demotruk/23xytnhGSc5sCwHUgUx5GKQ3PZLHabQZPTbG1KyKmpYFkR577LTpL4ycyqX97MMf5x74N.png)

Ask how Hive is growing and the discussion usually centres on accounts created, daily active users, or active authors. None of these predict the token price.

I ran [Granger causality tests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granger_causality) — a standard econometric method that asks whether knowing one variable's past helps predict another's future — on daily active authors and HIVE price across the full chain history. Using log returns (the standard transformation in financial econometrics), **daily active authors do not predict price at any lag tested** (minimum p = 0.65 across 21 lags). The reverse is overwhelming: price predicts user activity from lag 2 onward (p < 0.001). People show up when the price goes up, not the other way around.

Raw new account counts fare little better. At monthly resolution, new accounts narrowly miss significance (p = 0.055) — and that's before accounting for the fact that raw account numbers can be dominated by activity that has nothing to do with the social network. During the Splinterlands surge (July 2021 – January 2022), Hive was creating over 125,000 accounts per month — compared to roughly 5,800 in a typical month. Those accounts were created for a play-to-earn game, representing fundamentally different on-chain activity from social network participation. We can't fairly measure their retention against social metrics, and we can't easily measure it against game metrics either — Splinterlands changed how its on-chain transactions worked over time, and without social proof it's impossible to distinguish unique players from multi-accounts and bots. Either way, these months dominate any analysis that counts raw accounts.

So if the standard metrics don't predict price, does that mean growth doesn't matter? No. First we must be sure that we measure the right thing.

### What Actually Predicts HIVE's Price

I built a different metric: for each month from April 2016 through June 2024 (99 months total), I counted accounts created that month that made at least one top-level blog post three months later. This is specifically a measure of social network growth — it captures people who joined Hive as a blogging platform and were still using it three months on. It doesn't capture game-only users, and it's not meant to. A single blog post is a low bar, but in practice it's a reasonable proxy for a real person engaging with the platform.

I then ran Granger causality tests at monthly resolution, excluding the Splinterlands surge period and verifying results hold with or without it.

| Test | Period | Significant lags | Direction | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Retained users → Price** | **Full (2016–2024)** | **months 7–10** | **Positive** | **< 0.001** |
| **Retained users → Price** | **Hive era** | **month 4** | **Positive** | **0.04** |
| **Retained users → Price** | **Hive excl. Splinterlands** | **month 4** | **Positive** | **0.04** |
| Raw new accounts → Price | Hive excl. SPL | — | — | 0.055 (not sig) |
| Price → Retained users | Hive excl. SPL | months 1–3 | Positive | 0.017 |
| Retention *rate* → Price | All periods | — | — | Not significant |
| Price → Retention *rate* | All periods | — | — | Not significant |

**Retained new accounts predict price increases 4 months later in the Hive era (p = 0.04) and 7–10 months later across the full Steem+Hive history (p < 0.001).** The direction is positive: more retained users, higher future price.

A caution on the Hive-era result: p = 0.04 is borderline. With multiple variables tested across multiple periods, a Bonferroni correction would push it past 0.05. The full-period result (p < 0.001) is the stronger anchor; the Hive-era result is consistent with it but should be treated as suggestive rather than definitive on its own.

### What About Sell Pressure?

![Sell pressure hypothesis](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/demotruk/23tcNRVyjee2TMWvD6uEix9WVaGZVv9WasuPxPR4jLs7WLfd4Gh7WgZbYyaCmqMbuV73B.png)

The strongest version of the \

argument goes: more users → more reward payouts → more selling on exchanges → lower price. If this is true, growing the user base is actively harmful — users extract more value than they create.

I tested this directly. Using daily data from HiveSQL on author reward payouts, HIVE transfers to 18 tracked exchange accounts (Bittrex, Binance, Huobi, Upbit, MEXC, and others), and token price, I fit a 4-variable VAR model on the Hive era and tested every link in the hypothesized chain.

It breaks at the first link. **User activity does not predict exchange outflows** (p = 0.06). The reward pool is set by inflation, not by the number of active authors — more authors dilute each other's share but don't change the total paid out. After controlling for exchange flows, user activity has zero additional predictive power for price (F = 0.52, p = 0.93).

Exchange outflows *do* predict price (p = 0.003) — there is real sell pressure in the system. And rewards *do* predict exchange outflows (p < 0.001) — some reward recipients sell. But the amount of selling is driven by price dynamics and the fixed inflation schedule, not by how many people are posting.

The strongest apparent signal was rewards → price, significant at every daily lag. But this turned out to be largely a statistical artifact. When rewards are measured in USD rather than native HIVE/HBD, the negative coefficient **flips to positive**: more USD rewards predict price going *up*, not down. The original negative signal was a denomination effect — when price falls, the blockchain prints more HIVE per payout, so \
and \

move together mechanically.

**The data does not support the hypothesis that more users create sell pressure that hurts the price.** We can't rule out small, diffuse effects that daily aggregates are too coarse to detect — but large, systematic sell pressure from user growth is not visible in eight years of on-chain data.

### Four Things the Data Tells Us About Growth

**1. It's the absolute count, not the rate.**

Retention *rate* — the percentage of newcomers who stay — does not predict price in any period tested. What matters is the absolute number of people who stay. Onboarding 200 retained users from 4,000 signups produces the same price signal as 200 retained from 10,000 signups.

This sounds like it argues against investing in retention quality. It doesn't — it argues for investing in *both* acquisition and retention, because the absolute count is acquisition × retention rate. But it does mean that obsessing over the retention percentage in isolation misses the point. A community with 3% retention that onboards 10,000 people a month (300 retained) is doing more for the network than one with 50% retention that onboards 20 a month (10 retained).

**2. Bear markets don't kill retention.**

Price does not significantly predict retention rate in any period tested (p > 0.27 everywhere). Whether HIVE is at $0.90 or $0.20, the proportion of newcomers who stay is statistically indistinguishable. Investing in onboarding and retention during bear markets isn't fighting a losing battle — the users you retain are just as likely to stick around as those who joined during a bull run.

**3. The relationship is bidirectional — but the forward signal is distinct.**

Price does predict retained-user counts at lags of 1–3 months (p = 0.017): higher prices attract more people who stay. But the retained → price direction (at lag 4) is a separate signal from the price → retained direction (lags 1–3). Both exist, and neither absorbs the other.

**4. Price scales proportionally with retained users.**
![Elasticity comparison](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/demotruk/23xViJDPsYjeNYNk1Lq5DpsHUMNEzNn1wtr81ZaL6txncX7yi2vtfvM2bBVtnGUdHFzw8.png)

A log-log regression of price on retained-user counts (with a time trend) for the Hive era gives an **elasticity of 0.99**: a 10% increase in retained users associates with roughly a 10% increase in price. This is an association, not a proven causal effect — but it tells us there's no evidence of diminishing returns to network growth in this data. The hundredth retained user appears to contribute as much as the tenth.

For comparison, the same regression using active authors (total posting users, not just new retained ones) gives an elasticity of only 0.20 — five times weaker. The price signal is specifically in *new retained users*, not in total posting activity.

Metcalfe's law would predict an elasticity of 2.0 (value grows with the square of users). We find 1.0. The network effect exists but it's linear, not superlinear. The quadratic term is not significant (p = 0.57).

### The Retention Flywheel

![Death spiral vs virtuous cycle](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/demotruk/23tHb6kpi9Ue6MQ8t4wjCQteyVe4jnNJh44zbiG8mu47Wp2GxQf1TYPhSTvbPFLkipbK1.png)

The findings above describe a feedback loop. Retained users predict higher prices (lag 4 months). Higher prices predict more retained users (lags 1–3 months). This is a flywheel — and we can estimate how strong it is.

The forward elasticity is ~1.0: a 10% increase in retained users associates with a ~10% price increase. The reverse elasticity is ~0.31: a 10% price increase associates with ~3.1% more retained users one month later. Multiply these together and you get a **loop gain of ~0.31** — meaning each turn of the flywheel preserves about 31% of the previous impulse.

That translates to a **total amplification of roughly 1.45×**. A boost to retained users doesn't just produce the initial price association — the feedback loop amplifies it by about 45% as it cycles through price → acquisition → retention → price.

Crucially, the reverse channel runs entirely through **acquisition**, not retention quality. Higher prices bring more people through the door (p = 0.0003); they don't change the proportion who stay (p = 0.30). Retention rate is the one variable in this system that price doesn't move — which means it's the variable that human effort can shift without fighting the market.

This is what makes retention work so leveraged. Acquisition can be boosted by spending money (as InLeo's onboarding campaign demonstrated) or by building apps that attract non-crypto audiences — but it's expensive, and the data shows price is a strong driver regardless. Retention rate responds to onboarding quality, community infrastructure, curation, and first-post rewards — things people can build without outspending the market. And because retention rate multiplies acquisition at every turn of the flywheel, improving it compounds.

In our [rewards and retention post](link-to-rewards-post), we found that 40% of newcomers earn literally zero rewards, and that the jump from $0 to even a few cents nearly triples retention. In the [community density post](link-to-community-density-post), we found that communities like Aliento retain newcomers at 46% versus a 19% baseline — primarily through dedicated in-language curation and fast comment response. Those findings now have an economic dimension: each improvement to retention rate doesn't just keep more people around, it strengthens the multiplier on a feedback loop that connects to price.

The flywheel is moderate, not explosive — a 1.45× amplifier, not a 10× one. [In an earlier post](https://hive.blog/hive-133987/@demotruk/would-hive-explode-if-we-could-improve-user-retention), @demotruk modeled what would happen if Hive could improve retention, and found that naive exponential projections \

The econometric data agrees: the loop is real but it's linear (elasticity 1.0, not Metcalfe's 2.0). Hive won't explode from better retention. It will grow steadily — and that steady compounding is exactly what a sustainable network needs.\n\nThe answer to \

is **yes — and retention is the lever**. The metric that predicts price is not accounts created, not daily active authors, not posts published. It's people who joined and were still here three months later. And the single most effective way to increase that number is to make those first three months worth staying for.

---

### Caveats

1. **The Hive-era monthly result is borderline (p = 0.04).** With 52 monthly observations and 6 lags tested, this is significant at conventional levels but not overwhelming. The full-period result (p < 0.001 across 98 months) is much stronger. The Hive-era finding should be treated as suggestive, not definitive.

2. **Multiple testing.** We tested multiple variables (raw accounts, retained accounts, retention rate, active authors) across multiple periods and lag structures. Some correction for multiple comparisons is warranted. The full-period retained-accounts result survives any reasonable correction; the Hive-era-only result may not.

3. **Granger causality ≠ true causality.** Granger tests measure predictive power, not causal mechanisms. A third variable (overall crypto sentiment, marketing campaigns, app launches) could drive both retained-user growth and subsequent price increases.

4. **The Splinterlands exclusion is a judgment call.** I excluded July 2021 through January 2022 on the basis that these months are dominated by game-account creation that is qualitatively different from social user onboarding. This is defensible, but the results should be checked for sensitivity to the exact exclusion window. We cannot say whether Splinterlands helped or hurt the price — the account surge coincided with the 2021 crypto bull market, and the two effects are impossible to separate.

5. **\

means posted again in month M+3.** A user who posted once in their fourth month and never again counts as retained. This is a low bar. A stricter definition (e.g., posted in months M+3 *and* M+6) would produce a cleaner signal but smaller sample sizes.

6. **The elasticity of 0.99 is a level association, not a causal estimate.** It describes how price and retained users co-move after removing a linear time trend, not the effect of adding one more retained user.

7. **The sell-pressure finding applies at the daily aggregate level.** It's possible that individual-level reward cashouts create sell pressure too diffuse to detect in daily aggregates, or that the effect operates at horizons beyond the 21-day lag window we tested. The analysis rules out large, systematic sell pressure — not small, distributed effects.

8. **The flywheel amplification is approximate.** The 1.45× estimate comes from multiplying two level-regression elasticities (forward and reverse) and treating the result as a geometric series. This assumes the loop operates cleanly across lags, which simplifies the actual dynamics. The qualitative point — that a feedback loop exists and retention rate is the lever humans can pull — is robust; the precise amplification factor should be treated as illustrative.

9. **The daily Granger null is specification-dependent.** The original first-differences specification produced a borderline signal (p = 0.045). The log-returns specification (standard in financial econometrics) produces a clear null (p > 0.65). Both are defensible transformations. We favor log returns because they normalize for scale, but we should be transparent that the null result depends on this choice.

---

*Data: HiveSQL, queried May 2026. Daily data: 3,173 days (April 2016 – December 2024). Monthly retention: 99 cohort months (April 2016 – June 2024). Exchange accounts tracked: Bittrex, Binance, Huobi, Upbit, MEXC, and 12 others. Reward data from VOAuthorRewards; staking data from TxTransfers (transfer_to_vesting). All analysis code available at [GitHub repo](link-to-repo). For the full retention series, see @demotruk's [collection post](https://hive.blog/hive-110144/@demotruk/series-on-user-retention).*

---

### What's Next

The data above shows that retained users predict price — and that there's no detectable sell pressure from user growth at the aggregate level. But one response I expect to this post is a version of the question @artofwar74 recently [put to me](https://peakd.com/@artofwar74/re-demotruk-ten3ky):

> \

In other words: the aggregate sell pressure finding is fine, but what about *specific communities*? What about the users from countries where a few dollars of HIVE rewards is a meaningful income — are they the ones pulling value out while everyone else builds?

That's the subject of the next post.

links.title: Visiting my elder brother's hobby garden after Friday prayers: mango buds (flowers) from mangoes, and the joy of the first guava.
links.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRg6hXkxXfmpTfYDaUa9w5CKfMFX3sVQAJ8yqdq91mSPf/20260508_225853993.jpg)

We cannot do many things due to lack of time. Due to our busy schedule, we often cannot enjoy the small joys of the people around us. For quite some time, an elder brother in our area has been asking me to visit the hobby garden planted next to his house. But for various reasons, I did not have time.

Today is Friday, a holiday. I thought that today could be a good opportunity. My elder brother's house is right next to the mosque in our area. So while leaving the house for Friday prayers, I decided in my mind that today after prayers, I will meet my brother and return to see his garden.

I went to the mosque and offered Friday prayers peacefully. As soon as I came out after the prayers, I saw my elder brother standing there. After exchanging greetings, I said to him, \

My brother was very happy to hear me. He smiled and took me to his backyard.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbWH6K2uE4z6VioaE3Xxgq8qbK8rpixEUSYauKmLtqTWD/mix_20260508_213502.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZHWYsGVC4R9cFfsTHtjugDc4Ty4om9S9GcawGok6TPu6/mix_20260508_214245.jpg)

To be honest, as soon as I entered his backyard, I felt a different kind of peace. He had planted such beautiful fruit trees in such a small space, I would not have believed it if I had not seen it with my own eyes. As soon as I entered the backyard, the first thing that caught my eye was a mango tree. When I got closer, I saw that it was a 'Katiman' Genus (Mangifera) mango tree. A great feature of this variety is that it is perennial, meaning that this tree bears mangoes more or less all year round. I was surprised to see that several large, fresh mangoes were hanging on one branch of the tree, and new buds had sprouted on the branch right next to it! The experience of seeing ripe mangoes and new buds on the same tree together is truly extraordinary. This variety of tree is very good for getting mangoes at the wrong time.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSwMkjKF7DDKmsgUdJH8SJaNajvDzA92gvHKXfwCx5NpL/mix_20260508_213854.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcdnqXJ3kzXFZAbM3dyPgRWaRYtfQQ1LqYsPjLtFqAbNz/mix_20260508_213546.jpg)

As soon as I passed the Katiman tree, I saw another mango tree, my brother said it was a \

Genus (Mangifera) mango tree. Masha Allah, that tree also bore many mangoes. I noticed that my brother had wrapped some mangoes in a black net and covered them very nicely. It was nice to see his extra care to protect them from insects and birds. It was clear that he loved the trees like his own children.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZzt5jfoHAFuqosEkNpH9BDtgmshJxNxNqgAzgRQvU4Ra/mix_20260508_213225.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVY2VdaMXHrMb546dDV7GVovaPvS2JCsT8UUxjKM2tEG6/mix_20260508_213255.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbic4poJSYE46Rjnnop1zSAcNRJdmvheDS59tWgKeLNgK/mix_20260508_213435.jpg)

Then my brother got a little excited and called me to a small guava tree. He happily told me that this tree had borne its first fruit. I counted and saw that the tree bore a total of 3 beautiful guavas. I could understand the special joy and excitement of seeing the first fruit on the tree that I had planted today just by looking at my brother’s face. The guavas were still unripe, but they looked quite fresh.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXEA68DjS45tT4mixeskSTj96G7EubQ6UMVdBjUDCYFoc/mix_20260508_214447.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcbey1iscJHVUp84H4Z1YkBMtPqvpCpDntAMcgRirLcB7/mix_20260508_214506.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWo5KBSHPyswc4gFHeP2ihcMRWq6aPsTnEpqf2grPqPbT/mix_20260508_214029.jpg)



Apart from these, my brother had planted a kulam tree and a pomegranate tree in that small area of ​​the yard, including various other trees. Each tree was quite healthy. As I looked around the entire garden, a different kind of peace was working in my mind.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP1tzXRTHpz9BpumZF63sJQ4JJ4Dok1MCBnK1MFRdopwL/mix_20260508_213950.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP2JTeEaMRHqZ5TQBfK1SKqHojuBusdNqsXak9T4CUcny/mix_20260508_214100.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX1XHu7beYK96DhVUYjEHMSQKjMm9xTcxDHhzkxrFYK5k/mix_20260508_214309.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcP3UuDmxCS72X35Bmyzdg5LW6q3XXjfXLvkfNzffywkB/mix_20260508_214327.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTcdK836dFiVtED3hgikMgsudQVtBfzVA3P7M8v7A3UHT/mix_20260508_214414.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUtRYyVPgkmVzsUwbGmJzzPET6ZCdedXBQcf2ENBWLrfA/mix_20260508_214354.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfB7DaEbPTFsA9LGpZxJaqyMPxGxeeUjNJaMheUEwPPRq/mix_20260508_213757.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT2b5WhvEvzukEYukys8Ct9b1o6kNbrrMYnCvNnjxafCh/mix_20260508_213358.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ9oiwFkuB9oKLTmUzuux81mhBuWWn9jQS1skop61yi1C/mix_20260508_213723.jpg)


It was truly a matter of luck to see such beautiful fruits coming from such a small area of ​​trees.
I was very happy to see my brother's carefully manicured garden and his love for trees. Who among you has such a hobby garden at home? Tell me in the comments.

(All posts are written in Bengali and translated into English using Google Translate.)

links.title: What can I do to cope with the hormonal changes of pre-menstruation?🌸🩸[ES/EN]
links.body: >Hola !! Bienvenidos queridos visitantes 🌷 | Hello!! Welcome dear visitors 🌷 #

>¡Hola bellezas de esta comunidad!...Les deseo un bonito y excelente día,me presento mi nombre es Annie bueno al menos así me dicen pero realmente mi nombre oficial es Annicer 😅así que pueden llamarme como gusten,he estado un poco indagando en esta comunidad cosa que habia hecho antes pero no había tenido oportunidad de presentarme y compartir algo referente al tema ya que en dadas ocasiones aunque tenga algo de lo que hablar no me daba tiempo redactar,aunque si me propuse hacerlo y hablarles un poco de mi vida en general siendo mujer y conocer a través de ustedes sus experiencias y como han enfretado la vida en este mundo donde cada uno trata de sobrevivir a su manera y circunstancias. # > _Hello beautiful people of this community!...I wish you a beautiful and excellent day. I'm Annie, well, at least that's what people call me, but my real name is Annicer 😅 so you can call me whatever you like. I've been exploring this community a bit, something I've done before, but I haven't had the chance to introduce myself and share anything related to the topic. Sometimes, even if I have something to say, I don't have time to write it down. However, I decided to do it and tell you a little about my life in general as a woman, and learn about your experiences and how you've faced life in this world where everyone tries to survive in their own way and circumstances._ #
![@anne002_20250723_195546_0000 (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/anne002/23wCdinhSgLNJhC1MzACcJBgZQGwSXbEsM7qTb4zsSLNzdJwNBmn8xnyoGNTdh1ai6GFa.png)

>Hoy les quiero hablar sobre un tema que es tendencia cuando está por venir nuestra menstruación ,en la face pre-menstrual parece chiste pero es anécdota mi familia ya deduce por mis cambios de humor que estoy por tener mi periodo,regularme cada mes antes de venirme me da mucha ansiedad tanto fisica como emocional,tengo muchos antojos sobre todo por comer dulces y cosas saturadas,tengo síntomas de baja autoestima irritabilidad,falta de comprensión,cambios de humor como el estar muy triste e hipersensibilidad,el no explicarme bien , confusión,y sensación de cansancio,aunque como tal muy poco tengo dolores en mi vientre cuando me da pues solo trato de descansar o tomarme una pastilla para bajar la inflamación o ducharme. # > _Today I want to talk to you about a topic that's trending when our period is about to start. In the pre-menstrual phase, it seems like a joke, but it's true: my family already deduces from my mood swings that I'm about to get my period. Regulating myself every month before it comes gives me a lot of anxiety, both physical and emotional. I have a lot of cravings, especially for sweets and rich foods. I have symptoms of low self-esteem, irritability, lack of understanding, mood swings like being very sad and hypersensitive, difficulty expressing myself, confusion, and a feeling of tiredness. Although I rarely have abdominal pain, when it does come, I just try to rest or take a pill to reduce the inflammation or take a shower._ #

>No se si a alguna de ustedes les sucede igual pero por lo que he escuchado e investigado no a todas nos da igual,quizás a muchas les pasa diferente o enfrentan sus cambios hormonales de otra manera,lo cierto es que a mí guna nos gustaría que nos sucediera eso ,aunque una vez escuché decir a una vecina que ella en su juventud le encantaba que le llegara su menstruación a lo cual yo enloquecí cuando la escuché decir eso,pero tuve que preguntarle por qué ,luego entendí el por qué me decia eso,ella decía que cuando au periodo no llegaba la presión era fuerte sufría de dolores ,y siempre se sentia irritada y sin poder hacer las cosas bien nada le salía como planeaba y no tenia tiempo para nada sino para descansar,ella decia mas eran los días que estaba mal que bien ,causa un poco de gracia pero si yo me sentí identificada.🤭 # > _I don't know if any of you experience the same thing, but from what I've heard and researched, it's not the same for everyone. Perhaps many experience it differently or deal with their hormonal changes in another way. The truth is, none of us would like that to happen to us. Although, I once heard a neighbor say that in her youth she loved getting her period, which shocked me. But I had to ask her why, and then I understood. She said that when her period didn't come, the pressure was intense, she suffered from pain, and she always felt irritable and unable to do things properly. Nothing went as planned, and she had no time for anything but rest. She said there were more days when she felt bad than good. It's kind of funny, but I did relate. 🤭_ #
![4a51455a5a9e50145c2ff772a83adb21.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/anne002/AKe9r6uQcXzmnaiQVBT3MP27LUR3hHocbTo1GucvZvcmwEpMCiMUtZkhtZPfpCB.jpg)
[Pinterest](https://pin.it/3yyS7EoHu)
 #
![@anne002_20250723_195546_0000 (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/anne002/23wCdinhSgLNJhC1MzACcJBgZQGwSXbEsM7qTb4zsSLNzdJwNBmn8xnyoGNTdh1ai6GFa.png)
#

>Una de las cosas que primero hago cuando ya mi menstruación llega el primer día es querer ducharme pero eso sí temprano ya que el frio de la noche siento no me hace bien y eso puede inflamar más mi vientre, entonces casi siempre cuando se que he ido al baño con dolores debo darme una larga ducha con agua tibia,luego voy por una pastilla y me voy a descansar no importa la hora pero debo hacerlo descansar al menos una hora y no hacer desarreglos ya esto me pone peor ,osea me da mas dolores,como trabajo solo trabajo antes de mi período y la face donde ya se me está quitando porque siento que ya estoy estable oara volver a mi rutina,durante el periodo no salgo a caminar lejos ya que esto es super incómodo por el flujo y los dolores e inflamación pueden regresar,evito hacer oficios bruscos y ayudar en casa en lo que puedo,esto lo hago para cuidarme físicamente durante el periodo,ahora emocionalmente si es algo que me ha costado pero trato de intentarlo,durante esos días me siento inservible y capaz de hacer absolutamente nada y la verdad me he acostumbrado a estos sentimientos ya que eso ha sido desde que me vino mi primer periodo,solo es cuestion de adaptarme digamos como que no prestarle atención a esos sentimientos porque es normal durante mi proceso y cambio emocional sentirme asi es parte del proceso en ocasiones me cuesta mucho llevarlo a cuestas pero no me queda de otra que aceptarlo y seguir. # > _One of the first things I do when my period arrives is take a shower, but I always do it early because the cold at night doesn't agree with me and can make my stomach bloated. So, almost every time I know I've gone to the bathroom with pain, I take a long shower with warm water. Then I get a pill and go to rest, no matter the time, but I have to rest for at least an hour and avoid any disturbances because that makes it worse, I mean, it gives me more pain. Since I work, I only work before my period and during the phase when it's ending because I feel stable enough to return to my routine. During my period, I don't go for long walks because it's super uncomfortable due to the flow, and the pain and bloating can return. I avoid strenuous work and help out around the house as much as I can. I do this to take care of myself physically during my period. Now, emotionally, it's something I've struggled with, but I try. During those days, I feel useless and incapable of doing absolutely anything, and honestly, I've gotten used to these feelings because that's what I've come to expect. It's been like this since I got my first period. It's just a matter of adapting, kind of like not paying attention to those feelings because it's normal during my emotional process and change to feel this way. It's part of the process. Sometimes it's hard to carry it with me, but I have no choice but to accept it and keep going._ #

>Otra cosa que hago es despejar mi mente concentrando mi mente en las cosas pendientes que te go que hacer por ejemplo mi trabajo,amo lo que hago y yo disfruto mucho eso,es algo terapéutico y siento que me relaja mucho hacerlo durante esos dias,aun con esos pensamientos negativos encima yo alli estoy haciendo lo que me gusta y lo que tanto disfruto a cualquier hora🤭...Se que a todas no nos afecta igual pero los cambios hormonales es algo con lo que tenemos que aprender a vivir cuesta pero es un proceso,ahora si pienso en las palabras de mi vecina después recordarás tus dias de juventud y dirás \

. # > _Another thing I do is clear my mind by focusing on the pending tasks I have to complete, for example, my work. I love what I do and I really enjoy it; it's therapeutic and I feel very relaxed doing it during those days. Even with those negative thoughts on my mind, there I am, doing what I love and what I enjoy so much, at any time of day 🤭... I know it doesn't affect everyone the same way, but hormonal changes are something we have to learn to live with. It's difficult, but it's a process. Now, if I think about my neighbor's words, later you'll remember your younger days and say, \

_

links.body: >Modern secular psychology often suggests the counselor should never give answers, only ask questions. Why is this \

method insufficient for a believer struggling with sin?

This approach does only half of the counseling. As counselors, we are not just listeners or facilitator of personal insight, but also a guide who lovingly points the counselee toward biblical truth. A believer who struggles with sin does not simply need help discovering personal feelings or desires, cause sin is a spiritual problem that requires biblical truth, correction, repentance, and guidance from God’s Word. In dealing with sin, one needs to know what God says about the issue and how to respond in obedience to Him. 
From the start of the discussion, biblical counseling does not suggest that answers lies within, because the heart is deceptive. Biblical counseling teaches us that true change is possible because of the gospel. Believers need God’s truth to renew their minds and transform their lives. Biblical counseling is not centered on helping people find answers within themselves, but on helping them find hope and transformation through God and His Word.

title.title: Early SoundCloud Release Tonight: If I Wasn’t Me Album
title.body:
![IIWM Wide.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPUTDrbhQwzraLiZtemaB864snDFuocmQpddvw9STNVsd/IIWM%20Wide.jpg)

Tonight I’m releasing my new album, **If I Wasn’t Me**, one week early on SoundCloud.

The official release is still coming, but I wanted to give people here a chance to hear it early, sit with the full project, and get a feel for where I’m at before the bigger rollout begins.

This album is 20 tracks built around reflection, resilience, love, late nights, ambition, growth, healing, and turning pain into purpose. It is not a perfect-life project. It is more like a journal from someone trying to understand the past, make peace with the present, and still move forward with high hopes.

A lot of these songs came from real thoughts, real pressure, and real moments I had to write my way through. Some tracks are more introspective, some are more motivational, some are about love, some are about needing space, and some are about finally letting light back in.

The official album rollout is still coming, but SoundCloud felt like the right place to let people get in early.

You can listen here: https://soundcloud.com/scottychams
If you check it out early, I appreciate you.

Low lights. High hopes. Real stories. No shortcuts.
— Scottychams

title.title: The Pressure of Marks and the Reality of Student Life
title.body:
Hello friends, see our education system is not very good everywhere, many people from different countries go to some particular countries to study and there are some world renounced universities which are respected a lot by everyone. See, everyone wants that he should get education from the best place and he should not only get a degree but also a treasure of knowledge, a lot of expertise and he should get a chance to study from such people who are already much more expert in his field and there are many top universities of the world where all these facilities are available, nowadays businesses are being run in the name of colleges. It is okay, whichever businessman or any particular person opens a school or a college, they are only concerned about their money, it does not matter to them what is the condition of the children studying in their schools or colleges, how they are passing or in what manner they are passing, they are only concerned about giving them a degree and they do not think about anything more than this.



![GRADING.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23t78txZb12VW2UufQSdGQWEvcmrT9Aup1mQhRoToW9S6N23KUELhNM6bPUEuChiiNEMF.png)


[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)


My opinion here is that if the university and the teachers and the chairman there look at all these things carefully then we will start seeing it because at some places it happens that if the children get proper guidance then they still go on the right path. But very rarely will you find teachers or college or school staff who are concerned about the children, most of them just want to spend their time there and somehow finish their classes, you have also noticed that if you do the work with full heart then the output of it is automatically good.


Same thing happens with studies also, if you teach children with good efforts and good mindset then the output will also be good and there is no doubt that the output will be good because whatever you do, you get the same. See, sometimes it happens that on the request of the parents, their children are promoted to the next class, but you should ask the children, not the parents, whether they want to go to the next class or not. Sometimes it happens that because of the parents, there is a lot of pressure on the children and the children are unable to bear this pressure and sometimes it happens that the dominance of the parents is too much due to which the children have to compromise on their career in front of them.



![GRADIN13G.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23tvAeBCEz2tKsS3aDXHFs8mwopiSPqRU1Nq3HV8Vfi65GvjFixUnsUqZtqfcqg65gKif.png)



[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)

Many times it also happens that the students who are passing the exam, pass by cheating, it is okay, they get good marks in the exams but after that they are not able to succeed, this does not happen with everyone, some people are very active and those who are not good in studies are very super active in other works, you must have seen this too. But what I mean to say is that if everything has to be done like this then what is the value of the degree, if you have to make them cheat then do not waste the money of so many children for so many years, do not waste so much time, just give them a degree to make them listen, which will make it easier for them later and on the basis of money you can increase their marks also and the business of colleges and schools will also continue.



See, apart from marks, there are many other things that a college and a school teaches children and should also teach them how to behave in the society and what are the things that you should pay attention to and the most important thing these days is how to increase your self-confidence and children should be encouraged in such a way that they can perform well in their field. It is okay to laugh at children on the basis of marks because marks do not mean everything, but some people are very talented and they are very good in all the fields. Yes, but we should not compare with other's children, this is also a big reason due to which the mental condition of the children makes a lot of difference. Look at the condition of the child, it matters a lot, if a person gets so engrossed in studies that he does not care about the outside world in any way, that is also not good and all these things should be kept in mind.
