[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1778232655103-237ffbecb4733332.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=hiveargentina/f5f3f820) ▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=hiveargentina/f5f3f820) ---
![Copia de Final Iniciativa.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hiveargentina/23xyNSKdZ2xfcPuHCeYdZGcysaH9VutYLNHenSXwkt68mxMHPbLEF1kHXhoDqMZTiWT1u.png)

     En medio de un mundo en el que la lectura se hace mayormente de forma digital, encontramos muchos lectores que pudiéramos llamar de la \

, pues prefieren las ediciones impresas con toda la magia que conlleva el poder disfrutar no solo de las letras, sino también del pasar las páginas y los olores propios de un libro en físico. Quizás faltaron autores, títulos y experiencias por contar, pero nos quedamos con las de quienes participaron en esta iniciativa, enriqueciendo al ecosistema y compartiendo detalles sobre sus gustos, permitiéndonos así conocerlos un poco más. Vaya, como siempre, nuestro agradecimiento a cada uno de los hivers que se unieron a la iniciativa, así como también el apoyo de los moderadores y curadores de la comunidad que también enriquecieron la experiencia con sus aporte acertados. Igualmente, nuestra inmensa gratitud a todos los proyectos de curación que pasan por la comunidad y apoyan a los autores que hacen vida en la misma, pues pensamos que Hive no se trata solo del crecimiento personal, sino que en el grupal está la clave para hacer un ecosistema mucho más fuerte, dándole importancia tanto a los autores, como a las comunidades y por supuesto, los proyectos de curación.
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

In a world where reading is mostly done digitally, we find many readers we might call “old school,” as they prefer print editions with all the magic that comes from enjoying not only the words, but also the act of turning the pages and the unique scents of a physical book. Perhaps there were authors, titles, and experiences left untold, but we’ll focus on those who participated in this initiative, enriching the community and sharing details about their tastes, allowing us to get to know them a little better. As always, our thanks go out to each of the Hivers who joined the initiative, as well as to the community moderators and curators whose insightful contributions also enriched the experience. Likewise, our immense gratitude goes out to all the curation projects that pass through the community and support the authors who make it thrive, as we believe that Hive is not just about personal growth, but that collective growth is the key to building a much stronger ecosystem, giving importance to authors, communities, and, of course, curation projects alike.

Dentro de muy pocos días, haremos oficial la iniciativa para este mes de mayo, esperando que abunden las participaciones de parte de los miembros asiduos a la comunidad y también de nuevos hivers que aporten sus puntos de vista al respecto, sobre todo por la importancia del tema, y su relación directa con el ecosistema. Cabe destacar que nosotros seguimos apostando por la generación de contenidos, la activación de la creatividad, además de la interacción y el flujo de ideas que permitan generar más bloques en nuestra blockchain, así que los invitamos a estar atentos, para que participen en cada uno de los proyectos que genera nuestra comunidad, como parte de nuestra estrategia para mantener activas nuestras cuentas y todo el ecosistema, aumentando nuestra marca personal, y sobre todo, que la colmena se mantenga generando muchas transacciones cotidianas. Rogamos leer las reglas de la comunidad, así como también de las iniciativas y, por supuesto, entender la filosofía de nuestro ecosistema. En esta comunidad, pregonamos la calidad, ante la cantidad. Y siempre aplaudiremos contenidos originales, con percepciones y/u opiniones personales, sobre el tema tratado. Creemos que todos podemos sumar valor, al ecosistema. También recuerden, que somos humanos y como todos, podemos cometer errores, pero la idea es consensuar y el norte, siempre será primero HIVE.
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

In just a few days, we will officially launch this month’s initiative, hoping for widespread participation from our regular community members as well as new Hivers who can share their perspectives on the matter—especially given the importance of the topic and its direct connection to the ecosystem. It is worth noting that we remain committed to content creation, fostering creativity, as well as interaction and the flow of ideas that allow us to generate more blocks on our blockchain, so we invite you to stay tuned and participate in each of the projects our community generates, as part of our strategy to keep our accounts and the entire ecosystem active, strengthen our personal brand, and, above all, ensure the hive continues to generate many daily transactions. Please read the community rules, as well as those for the initiatives, and, of course, understand the philosophy of our ecosystem. In this community, we prioritize quality over quantity. We will always applaud original content with personal perspectives and/or opinions on the topic at hand. We believe everyone can add value to the ecosystem. Also, remember that we are all human and, like everyone else, we can make mistakes, but the goal is to reach consensus, and our guiding principle will always be \

body.title: The Mountainous Region.
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ9Ro5BXp8AVYzfQyP8cxQ851W9xyqxGVib2nj3r4pGR7/32343.jpg)

Hello Hive Community.

I hope you all are fine. I am also fine here. My favorite subject for posting in the Photography Lovers Community is always natural scenery. In today's post, I have presented the beautiful mountains and natural scenery on the way to reach Pangong Tso Lake in Ladakh. The journey through the mountainous region of Ladakh on the way to Pangong Tso is one of the most beautiful and unforgettable experiences in the world. The road to Pangong Tso passes through high mountains, rocky valleys and snowy peaks that look like dream scenes. Every part of the journey here presents a new view of the beauty of nature. The journey here fills the heart of every traveler with wonder and excitement.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWVjbuZUtiq9ZTXFx2zobYZ4Ug7EDZ4bAajdwZkUL4irK/1_1.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaLBUZuJrB1SNYAQAHfZb4m6nZez4McBAG7s3sEKDnixz/2_2.jpg)

The first photograph presented here is my favorite photograph among all the photographs presented today. This photograph covers every part of nature. The beauty of the blue sky can be seen in this photograph. As can be seen in the photograph, the beauty of the sky is amazing. The air of this area is so clean and fresh that during the day the sky looks dark blue and at night it is full of bright stars. In this area, white clouds slowly roll over the mountains. These clouds create wonderful shadows on the rocky hills. The serene atmosphere of this region makes the tourists feel close to nature.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaiAvoksmccejLQdYqz32erk1Yz29Lq7Nv4ovfaXfv8gW/3_3.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfGmKBhjd5EE9mCuuMeSzEEGWjCpRC18CadhYGkoNgdRj/4_4.jpg)

When we leave Leh city and move towards Pangong Tso, every tourist who visits here is welcomed by endless mountain ranges. The specialty of the mountains of Ladakh is that many places are different from the lush green hills of the mountains. If I talk about the Ladakh region, then this area is a mountainous desert. It can be said that these mountains are mostly dry and rocky. If you look at the photographs above, you will see that these mountains are painted in the colors of brown, gold, gray and white. As can be seen in the photographs above, under the bright blue sky, the mountains look magnificent. Due to the sunlight, the colors of the hills change throughout the day. The changing colors of the mountains make the natural scenery here look magical.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYadrPTXzLbLxCfg2MMAAWRqjYRKeEvXwV8MRS6FTyddZ/5_5.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTcgBANBofHC9TQGUj4636n9fAWsyCoTGg7pEoenzwHrE/6_6.jpg)

As can be seen in the first photograph presented above, the roads here are full of adventure in themselves. These roads pass through steep slopes and curves. Tourists coming here often stop to watch the captivating mountain views around the road. If I count such places, the first name comes from Changla Pass. Achangla Pass is one of the most exciting parts of the journey. Changla Pass is counted among the highest mountain passes in the world. This pass is covered with snow most of the time in winter. The cold wind blowing on this pass provides refreshment. I have talked about one pass but there are many such passes in Ladakh.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfPKQkiBHm5YrEaEK3xroPMcPhxisgyqvXaR83h8nbZxw/7_7.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbpxx7qUATYcXuWB6DHsx3FGG33hvM5Nqaym7iYGqY7s1/8_8.jpg)

In the photograph taken above, the serene and magnificent beauty of the mountainous region can be seen under the bright blue sky. The sky seen in these photographs shows the wonderful connection between the clouds and the mountains. The atmosphere and nature here look pure. In the first photograph above, the dark blue color in the sky is very clearly visible. In this scene, soft white clouds are spread across the sky like floating cotton. These clouds add beauty and balance to the entire scene. The bright sunlight falling on these clouds makes them soft and shiny.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcDHHPgeaQ6Hj8XpF7GYs9f72wtqBvPdXN7x2Y1WA8mkF/9_9.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVmpnsGBW2dCHgVADy9GyShpJ2xZDwbQizrFvhxivDNBT/10_10.jpg)

As seen in the photographs above, the big mountains stand proudly under the sky with their rocky slopes and rough surfaces. In the second photograph above, the sunlight and shadows falling on the mountains create beautiful patterns and make the landscape more attractive. One similarity in the photographs presented here is that the gentle slopes of the mountains seen in each photograph gradually rise towards the sky. Which gives the scene a magnificent look. The solitude and quiet beauty of these mountains gives a feeling of peace and closeness to nature.

body.title: 晚上又去街边吃了一圈
body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![main-1-1778198649-33dfd8b79f54.png](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/engagement-bootstrap/generated/wendyfay/seed-wendyfay-2026-05-08/main-1-1778198649-33dfd8b79f54.png)
</center>
</liketuimages>

今天傍晚没什么事，就一个人逛到了那片商业街。天色刚好，还不完全黑，那种光线最舒服，暖暖的灯亮起来了，整条街都闪闪的。街边的小吃摊子一个接一个，烤串、炒菜、什么都有，人挺多的，都是下班出来吃饭的。

我在几个摊子前停留了一会儿，看着锅里冒出来的热气，食材在铁板上滋滋响，那种现做现吃的感觉真的没办法抗拒。最后还是忍不住坐下来点了些东西，就坐在那些塑料凳子上，边吃边看来来往往的人。旁边有朋友，有独自一个人的，有家庭，每个人好像都在享受这个时刻。

街边小吃的好处就是这样，随意，不用讲究，就是吃得开心。那些冒着热气的菜，香味混在一起，有点混乱但又很真实。吃完了擦擦嘴，继续逛街，或者就在这里坐一会儿看着人群。这样的夜晚，其实就挺够了。

body.title: Trip To Punta Cana
body.body: > My wife and I took an evening walk along the beach in Punta Cana, filled with beauty and tranquility. As we walked hand in hand, I could feel the soft, warm sand caressing my feet and the warm breeze caressing my skin. The sun was slowly setting behind the horizon in the distance. The colors in the sky were incredible, and I took a few photos to share with you. ![Pu (4).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTD7jrPmgpYhJXyQ3NdDunaoHZi8fkMgnLV1XWSAeQMeG/Pu%20(4).jfif) ![Pu (3).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR8UsvhPWgVNNMtYukr7fPwWNUZqSgjwQUaWZvkSWUUz4/Pu%20(3).jfif) I decided to take a few photos to capture these beautiful moments. I positioned my camera so that I could capture the silhouette of my wife as she jumped in the air with joy. After a few unsuccessful shots :) I chose one that I thought was successful. The sunset light created a photo effect, emphasizing her movements and emotions. When we get home, I think I'll print this photo on paper :) ![Pu (2).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNPTF3hZ6R85e642oR9ya9ryPAadfbkS5NdhtKSx3fWAc/Pu%20(2).jfif) When evening came, I decided to experiment with a few more shots. I lay down on the ground and pointed the lens at one of the tall palm trees that towered above us. In the darkness, its leaves looked like bird wings against the starry sky. The stars shone brightly, as if they were diamonds scattered across the endless sky. I felt the magic of the moment take over me and I knew that this photo would be something special for me and for this post. ![Pu (1).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWGh95qYdVNSMjq19RLuyx8ZgRAzEBSjE7m9FKGDAqNPm/Pu%20(1).jfif) As we walked along the beach, we listened to the gentle sound of the waves. The air was saturated with the aroma of salt water and tropical flowers, which made the atmosphere even more romantic :) We talked quietly, sharing our dreams and hopes, enjoying every moment together. That evening walk along the Dominican beach was a pleasant experience, filled with love, beauty and tranquility. The photos I took will be our way of returning to this moment again, when we want to remember how wonderful the simple pleasures in life can be :) [//]:# (!worldmappin 18.55764 lat -68.37631 long d3scr)

body.title: I gave up my dream of studying in medical college due to financial reasons.
body.body: > https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUStiBaYDRmaGGHcjAcVpDD4C2u2ApE4j9zndAJHCX8m9/1000069143.png I hope my friends are doing well. I have achieved a lot in my life and I have left many things that have gone from my life. I wanted many things that I had a lot of hope in my life but I did not get. When we hope for something and when we struggle a lot to get to that stage. Then it seems that the creator must fulfill that hope of mine. And with that goal we keep moving forward. When we realize that we will never get what we hope for, we get very disappointed. We often underestimate life. I have seen people who have taken their own lives for suicide when they could not reach their goal. In fact, when we want something and if we do not get it, we feel very helpless. That time does not want to leave us. However, a person may not get many things in his life, but he must discard those words and those memories. Only then will he be able to move forward. Our life never stops. One of my hopes in life was that I would become a doctor in the future. When I used to pass in front of the medical college hospital in my city. Since childhood, I felt that it would be great if I could become a doctor. I knew that after my Higher School Certificate examination, I would be able to prepare for the medical examination. For this, I worked hard for about six months to prepare myself. I will never forget how I spent six months at this stage of my life. I have awakened my confidence a lot, I have talked a lot to myself. I looked at my family. My family's dream was that I should study medicine. But in the end, my dream of studying in a medical college was no longer possible for me. When I took the medical college examination, I did not get good results, due to which I did not get a chance in a medical college. Then I told my family to study in a private university, but it was very expensive, it required a lot of money. Which my family could never afford. Due to which I deleted it from my life. After that, I calmed myself down and controlled myself. I have explained myself a lot and then I have calmed down a lot. It really hurts when you have to give up your hopes because of your family's financial situation. ![1000019308.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRW9rHroSFBSAKdERxzaNWNAnWKCXRUdrHF4LbDABXrT6/1000019308.png) --- Divce | realmi c67 -|-| [Image source]( https://pixabay.com/photos/class-teaching-health-nurse-9827876/ ) ### Kind Regards @nahid43 ![1000019308.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRW9rHroSFBSAKdERxzaNWNAnWKCXRUdrHF4LbDABXrT6/1000019308.png) Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@nahid43/my-additional-source-of-income-came-from-tutoring-5qe)

body.title: Is marksheet an important factor to judge ourself?
body.body:
Hello, Ram Ram, Namaste, Satriyakaal to all Hive users .Today I'll tell you that marksheet is an important factor to judge ourself. I am not saying this and people also think that this is not fair that a student is judged by his marks but, this is the reality and when your result comes, I am not talking about rest classes but, I am specially talking about the board classes as when your board result will be coming all your relatives, neighbours and all the other people whom do you know, will take you out from your grave to ask your marks in the exams and this is the reality and everytime a student thinks that we are not judged by our marks , but when the result arrives you start understanding that what is the importance of marks and people give more attention to a person with higher marks or percentage. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaf8W53JE7zJEieeQmB6m5ucdJ3o5otH7Qn6YtLSGfryM/ghjiuytrdesxcvbhjiuytfrgh.png)



[img src](chatgpt.com)

And those who have passed 10th, 12th or have passed many much years after passing the 10th or 12th standard they also share this experience that all the people on the result day start searching the one who is a 10th or 12th grader and this is not a lie and next year when my result will come I'll also be experiencing this and this is a bitter truth and it is very hard to face this reality even if our marks are good, it doesn't matter that how much our marks are, but, it also matters. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQiVm3Xcap5BCJAR8YsWuhhK9KVxAL6LBApgdbJMLEV2W/hgtfdcvbnhjuytfrdc.jpg)



[img src](https://www.magnific.com/free-photo/closeup-doctor-checking-patient-daily-report-checklist_2767783.htm#fromView=search&page=1&position=2&uuid=1757826a-9e10-4e98-a9e1-bd797bc88d22&query=marksheet)


And your family on the result day will also say that you have done hardwork, and you have achieved good marks either you have scored high or low marks. At at last your parents would also say that your hardwork didn't did anything and you should do more hardwork whether you would have given your best for the exams. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcJ7jZadJv6hFntgZqqyDEnggHhxsghmJWMrQ46qyXPC3/yuytrf.jpg)



[img src](https://www.magnific.com/free-vector/hand-drawn-report-card-illustration_86770755.htm#fromView=search&page=1&position=1&uuid=1757826a-9e10-4e98-a9e1-bd797bc88d22&query=marksheet)

So, for Today, this much only till further goodbye.

body.title: နွေ အပူနဲ့ အပြိုင်
body.body:
အိုးက မပူ စလောင်းက ပူ စကားရှိသည်။
ထိုစကားအတိုင်းဖြစ်နေသည်။ ယနေ့ အိမ်သို့
မိတ်ဆွေ အမျိုးသမီးတဦးအလည်လာသည်။
သူမက ကျွန်တော်တို့ရုံးမှ အဖွဲ့သားတဦး
ဖြစ်သည်။ သူမက ကျွန်တော့်ထက် ငယ်သည်။
ငယ်ရွယ်သူဖြစ်သည့်အလျှောက် သူမက
ရုံးမှာ ဆက်လုပ်ပါလျှင် ရှေ့ဆက်ပြီး သူမအတွက်
တက်လမ်းများရှိသည်။ လုပ်ငန်းများကို
စိတ်ဝင်စားစွာ လုပ်ကိုင်တတ်သူလည်းဖြစ်သည်။ 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR6Q1XbRAWdZDymskiiXoDvmPVG13TwAnTSrTsh18bFrQ/image_b7da6c62_d230_47e8_8974_f01472f6b9276699103754185317451.jpg)

ယခုတော့ လမ်းတဝက်မှာ လမ်းပျောက်နေရှာသလို။
သူမမှာ ညီမနှင့် တူမလေးတဦးရှိသည်။ ညီမက
သူမထံမှီခိုနေထိုင်သည်။ အမထံမှာ အတူနေပြီး
နေ့ပြန်တိုးလေးများပေးကာ သားအမိနှစ်ယောက်
အဆင်ပြေသလိုနေခဲ့သည်။ ယခုတော့ သမီးလေးက
အရွယ်ရောက်လာပေသည်။ မိတ်ဆွေအမျိုးသမီးလည်း
အပြင်မှာ စီးပွားရေးလုပ်ရန် စဉ်းစားလာသည်မှာ
ငါးနှစ်ပြည့်ပေသည်။ လက်ထဲရှိသော ငွေကလေးကို
မိတ်ဆွေအချို့ထံ အတိုးလေးပေးကာ ထိုအတိုး
ငွေလေးဖြင့် အဆင်ပြေသလိုနေသည်။ 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRz9aaT4zwJuN2FSDkfYRCJBc6bN9gVf7Aty3exZvorpj/image_af701211_41df_4a29_aefb_bf3ea56732f68296952676617540787.jpg)

ထိုးတက်လာသော လူနေမှုစရိတ်များကြောင့်
အတိုးငွေကလေးဖြင့် လူသုံးဦး၏ စရိတ်က
စားဖို့အတွက် စိစစ်သုံးနေရသည်။ အခြားအသုံးစရိတ်
များအတွက် သုံးရန်အဆင်မပြေပေ။ ထိုကြောင့်
ညီမသားအမိကို ပြောရတော့သည်။ တူမကလေးကို
ကျောင်းဆက်တက်မည်ဆိုက တက်ရန်၊ ကျောင်း
မတက်ပါက အလုပ် လုပ်ကိုင်ရန်ပြောမိသည်။
သားအမိနှစ်ဦးအနက် အမေဖြစ်သူက ဘာမျှ
မသိတော့ကြောင့်၊ ဘာဆက်လုပ်ရမည်ကို
သူ မသိကြောင်း စိတ်ဆိုးစွာပြောသည်။ သမီး
လေးကလည်း သူအား ထိုသို့ အဒေါ်ကပြောသဖြင့် 
စိတ်ဆိုးပြီး ငိုယိုကာ အဒေါ်ကို စကားမပြောပေ။ 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUmHiF9Zi6eAF4LApFcfJTPxqpSLCAGUDC3KrfPvFvYRk/image_c774c516_9458_4671_92b8_f709a9a047238158717138842520388.jpg)

ဖော်ပြပါအကြောင်းအရာများကို မိတ်ဆွေက
ကျွန်တော့်အား ပြောပြခြင်းဖြစ်ပါသည်။
သူမ မရှိပါလျှင် ထိုသားအမိအတွက် ရင်လေး
သည်ဟု ပြောသည်။ မိတ်ဆွေကသာ သူ မရှိ
လျှင် မဖြစ်ဟုထင်နေသည်။ သူမ မရှိပါလျှင်လည်း
သူရို့ဟာနဲ့ သူရို့ဖြစ်သွားပေမည်။ လူဆိုသည်က
နေလို့ ရသလောက်နေကြသည်။ နေလို့ မရသည့်
အခါမှာတော့ မနေသာသဖြင့် လုပ်ကိုင်ကြရ
ပေမည်။ 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfXCmCjSnVzp71cjzqqMtsZNiBEVk7n8Ev3Za2mkd7C5p/image_7456b2a8_2266_4eb8_9ced_cf8091cb0a1f1647469310764449112.jpg)

နေသာလို့နေ နေကြသည်ဟုသာ မိတ်ဆွေ
အမျိုးသမီးကို ပြောမိသည်။ သူမကတော့
သူ့ ညီမနှင့် တူမအတွက် ပူပန်နေသည်။ မှန်ပါသည်
သူမ ကတော့ လောလောဆယ် ပူပန်နေရပေအုံးမည်။
လူသုံးယောက်စာ စားစရိတ်နှင့် နေစရိတ်များက
လောလောလတ်လတ် မိတ်ဆွေက တာဝန်ယူ
ထားရသဖြင့် သူမကတော့ ပူပင်နေရပေအုံးမည်။ 

@htwegyi
May 8, 2026

body.title: Moody Shots - Women's Bridge
body.body:
> There are many ways to capture this part of the city through a photographer’s lens, depending on each photographer’s perspective and the editing techniques you apply, it can appear cheerful, sad, warm, surreal, or cinematic. I particularly like the last one. I always aim for that style in my shots, and it’s already part of my aesthetic when I edit. The Woman’s Bridge is a very popular and touristy area where there are so many elements to capture, and it’s also a highly sought-after location for portrait photography. “Moody” is an editing style in which you significantly lower the saturation levels of certain tones to achieve a deeper, more somber aesthetic, so to speak, by eliminating very bright colors or replacing them with darker ones—all without losing the essence of what is being shown or captured. Here are some of these old but interesting shots; I hope you enjoy them. Have a great weekend, everyone. *P.S.: If there’s a photo here that I’ve posted before, it’s not on purpose.*

body.title: Maybe I Just Love Leg Days
body.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1778231427524-ee04cd75ec29f298.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=stevenson7/b6d58804)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=stevenson7/b6d58804)


---

I finally had a proper leg day yesterday, and it felt pretty good. I’d been having stomach issues on Wednesday, which meant I couldn’t make it to the gym, and then I came down with malaria too. Eventually, I got some medication and luckily started feeling much better, so I forced myself to go to the gym yesterday. I tried not to go too hard, but I definitely did. I even hit a PR on lunges.

I started with squats as usual, although I could only manage 10 reps at 100kg, which is far below my normal weight. But at least I showed up. Then I did some leg extensions, followed by Bulgarian deficit split squats, and then lunges. I used a pair of 30kg dumbbells first, then decided to attempt a PR with 40kg, and I got it. After that came hack squats before I closed out with machine ab crunches.

It’s funny how I always get compliments on the size of my legs but never my upper body. Even though I try to push myself every single session, it feels like I give even more during leg days. Maybe it’s because training legs is almost like cardio, and at the same time, it’s a mental battle. Maybe I just need to accept that I genuinely love leg days.

Anyhoo, thank you for reading. Till the next one. God bless.

---

▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=stevenson7/b6d58804)

body.title: 12 Hours in Desert Heat, Callused Hands, Big Dreams | Pakistani Mazdoor in Saudi
body.body:
/>

Hello Hive Community!

My name is Nomikh and I am from Pakistan. I am 28 years old and I work as a construction laborer in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

I moved to Saudi Arabia 2 years ago to support my family back home. Life here is very tough. I work 10-12 hours every day at construction sites under the hot sun. The temperature often reaches 50°C. My hands are full of calluses from hard work. But Alhamdulillah, I am able to send money home every month to my parents, brothers and sisters.

My biggest dream is to save enough money to start a small business in Pakistan one day. I miss my home, my family, Pakistani food, and my friends. But I know this sacrifice and hard work is for my family's better future.

I joined Hive today because I want to share my real daily life and struggles with all of you. I will be posting about:

1.  The daily life of a Pakistani laborer in Saudi Arabia
    
2.  Photos from construction sites, buildings, and the city of Riyadh
    
3.  My personal stories, challenges, and small moments of happiness
    

Your support means the world to me. Even a small upvote of $1 makes a huge difference for me and my family. I promise to reply to every comment and support your posts in return.

Thank you for taking the time to read my first post. God bless you all.

#introduceyourself #pakistan #saudiarabia #labor #construction #life #firstpost

body.title: Art and Creativity Journal: June Gloom in May
body.body: Greetings, from the creative doldrums of my mind!\n\nThe climate around here usually provides us with something we call the *\

* 

![AS121-NewWork2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alchemystones/23zGm6BbHNeV5TEabKSzFxeQJzUg64N8LLujtY2YAaeimahGqUCcaGvvQhohEHY5YD6sR.jpg)

It has something to do with daytime heating, the coldness of the Pacific ocean, mountains and cool nights which means that when we wake up in the morning there is a dense fog and even occasional fine drizzle hanging over us.

That's the sun rises further, the fog gradually burns off and usually it becomes a clear day by noon or early afternoon.

Perhaps because it has been unseasonably warm for the past week or so we are having an early version of the June Gloom this year.

![AS320-Beach3.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alchemystones/242hRqof2JTe1CkmwyZbzZGhfbU3kKhNZ5PFDeWAxG3EGmvfKGxffBBU8UcPKyKUGjNjD.JPG)

Somehow, the gloominess of these mornings seems to match my creative spirit quite well. I just can't *get in the mood* to create anything. While I can get pretty enthusiastic about things like gardening, when I sit down in my creative space and look at my paints I pretty much draw a blank and I get up and walk away after sitting there for about 10 minutes. Sometimes less.

Maybe this holds true for all creatives, but most of my life I have been plagued by this particular pattern of *\
* In a way, it is part of why I have never become a full-time artist. I am not *reliable.*\n\nHowever, that does not mean that I don't enjoy my *\
* when they do happen. I'm very grateful for the times when *\

* does work.

![AS075-KeithChakra3.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alchemystones/241tdLuUBMDkawocwoyhvU9UCWkuKhXco5asQrFkfCx7ahHhvQ9ZM8N4VtSWbegipkGof.JPG)

The thing about it, is it it really affects all aspects of being a creative. It's not just the *creating* part, itself, but the same can then be applied to things like marketing and publicity. I can get very fired up and active on promotions for a short period of time, but I lack whatever it is that's needed to just keep going day in and day out without fail.

With the project of moving all my existing finished stock to my Etsy shop coming to an end, it also means I am about to start in on the part of the project where regular social media marketing has to start. And that requires a high level of dedication.

We'll see how that turns out...

#### *Thank You!*

![AS-0000-Spacer.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alchemystones/23vsNU1LPAccErViMruWQRcJnb8igXk9AXNCkM4iuZXmo1QFHeLEJpbGhK1RG3P9xPE1r)

If you enjoy painted rocks, do check out **[The Hive Rocks Project](https://peakd.com/c/hive-127783/created)** and help spread the word about Hive, while also being creative!

Because I *am* trying to make some semblance of income — a *part time living,* even — I now add this footer to all my posts, in the hope that someone, somewhere, might decide to take a further look at my work, and perhaps consider supporting independent art.

Thank you, in advance, for your consideration and support!

body.title: PHOTO TRIP - Austria - Buildings at Schwarzenbergplatz in Vienna
body.body:
![cover.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/Eo1xLox815VhWgbpWXpSMKjgJzG6PmthahBReW56tHecs9dPmCjNoQeigz8WDpAuus1.jpg)


One of my main goals when I went to Vienna with my friends was to see the architecture of this city in person. Previously, I'd only seen it in photos or videos, and I had high expectations. However, upon arriving in the city, I wasn't disappointed; from the very first moment I stepped foot in, the architecture impressed me. Not everyone may like it, however, for my friend it was too \

.

> <sub>**[ PL ]**</sub>
> Jednym z głównych moich celów wycieczki z przyjaciółmi do Wiednia było zobaczenie na żywo architektury tego miasta. Wcześniej wielokrotnie widziałem ją tylko na zdjęciach lub filmach i miałem spore oczekiwania. Jednak po przybyciu do tego miasta nie zawiodłem się i praktycznie od pierwszych kroków architektura robiła na wrażenie. Nie każdemu jednak musi się podobać, dla mojego kolegi była zbyt \

.



![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1881.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uQk8toXTFonJVC8xSQCyYGPhafqEqx75c6wEzPuVMmmR3kahSJu8FtgACxpHEUmFjAo.jpg)

A small intersection of three streets: Schwarzenbergplatz, Zaunergasse, and Daffingerstraße. I was particularly interested in the visible building here, specifically its roof with a dome and sculptures. The Syrian Embassy is located in the adjacent building.

> Małe skrzyżowanie trzech ulic: Schwarzenbergplatz, Zaunergasse i Daffingerstraße. Mnie zainteresował tutaj szczególnie widoczny budynek, a dokładnie to jego dach z kopułą i rzeźbami. W sąsiednim budynku znajduje się Ambasada Syrii.

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1887.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23wqbqyKmFBSoCtFXDCND4SAz4x9AEs9fNTnQ2TJRyVSTDjqqQiqEZ13yMY2MYcRP3EMN.jpg)

As a tourist with a camera, street lamps posed a significant challenge when taking photos. It was impossible to get a wider shot without them, and I had to be careful not to obscure interesting architectural features.

> Dla mnie jako turysty z aparatem, sporym utrudnieniem przy robieniu zdjęć były lampy uliczne. Niemożliwe było wykonanie szerszego ujęcia bez nich i trzeba było kombinować aby nie zasłaniały ciekawych elementów architektury.

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1880.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23xKkCYvRf158rcBFZm73ymaPcJC6EYHN1SNqRmd9fCCVNBQ4Ho1PEeeqE3mxcoVAUejz.jpg)

Another obstacle is vehicles. This is quite a large intersection, so there is a lot of traffic on the street. However, the architecture itself is impressive and eye-catching.

> Kolejne utrudnienie to pojazdy. Jest to dość duże skrzyżowanie, więc ruch na ulicy jest spory. Jednak sama architektura robi wrażenie i przyciąga wzrok.

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1890.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uFMcJoJ77dReGUrw5yMrzMH9hLTpWQ9J22uXZuyyFijaFJ7ezsgZwPzzphVyEBLAeXW.jpg)

Schwarzenbergplatz is a large square located between Belvedere Palace and the historic city center. There is also a fountain and a large monument here, which I presented in my [first post from Vienna](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@rsphotos/photo-trip-austria-fountain-and-monument-at-schwarzenbergplatz-in-vienna).

> Schwarzenbergplatz to duży plac znajdujący się między Belwederem a zabytkowym centrum miasta. Znajduję się tu również fontanna i duży pomnik, które przedstawiałem w swoim [pierwszym poście z Wiednia](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@rsphotos/photo-trip-austria-fountain-and-monument-at-schwarzenbergplatz-in-vienna).

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1889.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uFMFdanW2byES2smu8tCJHWourSfvj6LUMTQeGt5pENnPzuLGs4j2nVdtcb9tzhwgFz.jpg)

Perhaps the most interesting building in this area, completely different from the others. It was built in the early 20th century in the Art Nouveau style and houses the French Embassy.

> Chyba najciekawszy budynek w tej okolicy, zupełnie inny od pozostałych. Został zbudowany na początku XX wieku w stylu secesyjnym i mieści się w nim Ambasada Francji. 

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1891.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uFU4nPm1YPXDYgSYU7NBPRNcieCjDk22VJYXcPJKE8vdYX3zthcjtHemWKD3kPBydsW.jpg)

From a distance, the golden sculptures located at the top of the building's facade attract attention.

> Z daleka uwagę przyciągają złote rzeźby znajdujące się w górnej części fasady budynku.

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1896.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23w2o886E5kWQBqd2MpMWtyFP5iDQzYqZgmeJxnMgjQctKXFuTYmytdXSqAER8K6KMycw.jpg)

![RSphotos-25-08-13-RSP_1897.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uFKYEgxo7JXr9EAUFpi3KNMzkN7HouUAL1tYe45kZKqK57JmT37pF5MkjvzGrvveWKJ.jpg)

Finally, the building next to the French Embassy building, a return to the architecture of the previous buildings.

> Na koniec budynek znajdujący się obok budynku Ambasady Francji, czyli powrót do architektury poprzednich budynków.

So, remember the pools on beeswap? This is basically almost the same; the difference is that it is against a different token pair.

You add liquidity, HBD and HIVE, for example, to the pool, and every time people swap via that pool, you gain a percentage of the rewards. Obviously, for it to be lucrative, a lot of liquidity has to exist.

Try something small so you can play with it, like cents, for example. And if you have questions, let me know.

You can always remove the liquidity anytime you need/want.

body.body:
<center>![image](https://pixabay.com/get/g7fd19a119bb9f63ba1c22b42207d26bb716177be1a4ed1615a62a751032dd785f09a678111d16a5c146a64a079b4f1a52d78450d5c7e2b6ab92ab0f69b5c5e86_640.jpg)</center>

***

# 自然的美

自然是我們生活中不可或缺的一部分，它不僅提供了生命所需的資源，還以其獨特的美麗和神秘吸引著我們。以下是一些關於自然的精彩部分。

## 1. 自然的多樣性

自然界充滿了各種各樣的生物和生態系統。從壯麗的山脈到廣闊的海洋，每一個角落都蘊藏著獨特的生命形式。

- **植物**：樹木、花卉、草地等各種植物為地球增添了色彩和氧氣。
- **動物**：從微小的昆蟲到巨大的藍鯨，動物們在生態系統中扮演著重要的角色。

## 2. 自然的力量

自然擁有無與倫比的力量，無論是壯觀的火山爆發還是平靜的湖泊，這些都展示了自然的威嚴。

- **氣候變化**：氣候變化影響著全球生態系統，提醒我們保護自然的重要性。
- **自然災害**：地震、颶風等自然災害雖然可怕，但也讓我們更加珍惜生活中的平靜時刻。

## 3. 自然與人類的關係

人類與自然之間的關係是相互依存的。我們從自然中獲取資源，但同時也有責任去保護它。

- **可持續發展**：我們需要尋找與自然和諧共處的方法，以確保未來世代能夠享受這份美好。
- **環保行動**：參加植樹、清理海灘等活動，為保護自然出一份力。

## 4. 自然的啟發

自然不僅是資源的來源，還是藝術和靈感的泉源。

- **藝術**：許多畫家和作家受到自然的啟發，創作出無數動人的作品。
- **心靈的平靜**：大自然的美景能夠讓人感受到心靈的平靜，減輕壓力。

## 結論

自然是我們共同的家，珍惜和保護自然是每一個人的責任。讓我們一起努力，為未來創造一個更加美好的環境。

---

希望這篇關於自然的部能夠激發你對大自然的熱愛和保護意識！

body.body:
![image](https://pixabay.com/get/g01c63be8398e7dceb8d93e9d8987cf897a6b006d34c3452777f339c839769df28e46a6a97035c4d73c512df349af32203e64e7db77332df8724b395a15440ead_640.jpg)
오늘의 산책은 정말 즐거운 시간이었어요. 한적한 공원에서 친구와 우연히 만나서 반가운 인사를 나눴습니다. 우리는 오랜만에 만나서 서로의 근황을 이야기하며 웃음꽃을 피웠습니다. 산책 중에 흥미로운 것은 공원에서 작은 플리마켓이 열리고 있던 것이었어요. 다양한 핸드메이드 제품들과 골동품들이 진열되어 있었고, 특히 한 아저씨가 만든 나무 조각상들이 정말 독특하고 멋졌습니다. 또 인근 카페에서 향긋한 커피를 사서 마시면서 편안한 시간을 보냈답니다. 오늘의 산책은 사람들과의 만남과 작은 발견들로 가득 차서 매우 뜻깊었어요. _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). body.title: A collection of watercolours and memories ❤️ Amonet (EN-ES)
body.body:
> --- ![Carta de acuarelas y dibujos.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23viEGNeSyTZsz3pcUoGeSTDQVwtaPESM8A8dzqj1fYYzqx6MY3AiurDGGztTpc3LeMK6.jpg) ![separador sencillo 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/Eo8UGAXUZoPxi8Ny3bWhw7vRVQywdynrHRhAwwZtRqW9jnyK7CZ42782EyeJ1UKHQuv.png) A few days ago, memories came flooding back of a time when I was a child, a time I associate mainly with school, but also with moments of solitude. It was a time when we had what we called ‘letter cards’. They were sheets of paper, some lined and others unlined; some came with their own coloured envelope, whilst others were plain white, but they all featured some sort of pattern or design, and there was a huge variety. You could buy them and they came in a bag, all the same, but the girls at school had them too and we could swap them. It was a bit like the sticker-collecting craze, but I think this was just for girls. As I said, the motifs varied; many depicted girls as in a drawing, and there were animals, angels and fantasy scenes. My friend Claudia and I were talking about them a few days ago, and it brought back memories. In this design, and perhaps in another one later on, I wanted to bring back this memory but do it digitally. I loved the experience.
SPANISH VERSION (click here!)

Hace varios días vinieron a mi mente recuerdos de una época, cuando era niña, que relaciono más con la escuela, pero también con mis momentos de soledad. Una época en que existían los que llamábamos, las hojas de carta. Eran hojas, algunas con renglones y otras no, algunas traían su sobre respectivo de color o a veces era blanco, pero todas tenían algún motivo o diseño y había mucha variedad. Se podían comprar y venían varías en una misma bolsa, todas iguales, pero las niñas en la escuela también tenían de esas cartas y se podían intercambiar. Era como la época de las figuritas, pero creo que esto era sólo para niñas. Como les digo los motivos variaban, muchas representaban a niñas como en un dibujo, había de animales, ángeles, fantasía. Y con mi amiga Claudia las mencionamos hace unos días, me trajo recuerdos. En este diseño y tal vez en algún otro más adelante, quise traer este recuerdo, pero hacerlo digitalmente. Me encantó la experiencia.

![separador sencillo 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/Eo8UGAXUZoPxi8Ny3bWhw7vRVQywdynrHRhAwwZtRqW9jnyK7CZ42782EyeJ1UKHQuv.png)
Process in pictures - Proceso en imágenes
|![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23t86WE3GGSbbhziwLa1i81bgYB213iADhdHz9pFKSxWsvkJAWwrbTpyZuT9DF6MQmAkX.jpg)|![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23uFrsXQA9eoNazvBaTS5uNkoDNm8AiVe56m6beET7UPgsKHofV4Y7VLSMceRQQcKdRPi.jpg)| |-|-| |![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vsmXb9dJgc4wCoWJPvUtMEWd6PtKcC4dt9Qu7HduXtW15ShqcJWNYA1oaA36XCFFQPB.jpg)|![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23tw1sE6DusUSBDXxAuGkjcQy3tv7aHWzxxhq34wF3qTibfwFC9SkwoyGtqoBKehhCid2.jpg)| ||| |![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMsHSAnoGJoegmQBhxm2PbzfgxGy3DcybRHqNBcDP7EwjK8Uk7UquahZJWP9HASdxCk.jpg)|![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vsfj8x3QrgzxFQzWXQLnAwEKoX6AfZbZHEsNybAqZBbDKbWSrsG9xVBP2wuqunfjz1X.jpg)| ![separador sencillo 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/Eo8UGAXUZoPxi8Ny3bWhw7vRVQywdynrHRhAwwZtRqW9jnyK7CZ42782EyeJ1UKHQuv.png) # Design process The design was created entirely in Photoshop CS6 without the use of AI, using 10 royalty-free images spread across 20 layers. On a white layer, I placed the first watercolour image, over which I added four layers of the lined sheet, in different positions and with a drop shadow layer style to separate them from the background. On top of two of these layers and beneath the other two, I placed the first image of flowers with the darker colour blend, enhancing the outlines with an edge filter. Then, on top of this, I placed the second watercolour image using a soft light blend, and from the image of the green leaves I selected, copied and pasted some of them into the design, placing them on the right-hand side using a darker colour blend. I placed the second image of flowers on the other side of the design, in two layers, using the ‘Darken’ and ‘Normal’ blending modes, but for the latter I left only the part with the flowers. Beneath this image of white flowers, I worked on the two images of the drawings featuring children with cats, using the ‘Darken’ blending mode and erasing certain parts so they matched the edges of the leaves with lines. With the image of the girl, I created two layers using underexpose and normal colour blends. I applied the added edges filter to all of them, as well as to the image of butterflies using the darken blend. The animation is done completely in After Effects, working on the opacity of each layer and adding lights in the form of clouds for better contrast. I send you all a big hello and see you next time. Thanks for watching and reading this far. Amonet - AV Design
SPANISH VERSION (click here!)

# Proceso del diseño El diseño está realizado completamente en el programa Photoshop CS6 sin uso de IA con 10 imágenes sin derechos de autor distribuidas en 20 capas. Sobre una capa blanca dispuse la imagen de la primera acuarela sobre la cual puse en cuatro capas la hoja con renglones, en distintas posiciones y con un estil de capa de sombra paralela para separarlas del fondo. Sobre dos de estas capas y debajo de las otras dos puse la primera imagen de flores con la fusión de color más oscuro, realzando los contornos con un filtro de bordes añadidos. Luego sobre lo anterior puse la segunda imagen de acuarelas con la fusión de luz suave y de la imagen de las hojas verdes fui seleccionando, copiando y pegando algunas de ellas en el diseño, colocándolas en el sector derecho del mismo con la fusión de color más oscuro. La segunda imagen de flores la coloqué al otro lado del diseño, en dos capas, con fusiones de color más oscuro y normal, pero de esta última dejé sólo la parte de las flores. Debajo de esta imagen de las flores blancas trabajé las dos imágenes de los dibujos donde hay niños con gatos, con la fusión de color más oscuro y borrando ciertas partes para que coincidan con los bordes de las hojas con renglones. Con la imagen de la niña hice dos capas con fusiones de subexponer color y normal. En todas ellas puse el filtro de bordes añadidos, como así también en la imagen de mariposas usando la fusión oscurecer. La animación está realizada completamente en After Effects, trabajando la opacidad de cada capa y agregando luces en forma de nubes para un mejor contraste. Les envío un gran saludo a todos y hasta la próxima. Gracias por ver y leer hasta aquí. Amonet - AV Design

Hace varios días vinieron a mi mente recuerdos de una época, cuando era niña, que relaciono más con la escuela, pero también con mis momentos de soledad. Una época en que existían los que llamábamos, las hojas de carta. Eran hojas, algunas con renglones y otras no, algunas traían su sobre respectivo de color o a veces era blanco, pero todas tenían algún motivo o diseño y había mucha variedad. Se podían comprar y venían varías en una misma bolsa, todas iguales, pero las niñas en la escuela también tenían de esas cartas y se podían intercambiar. Era como la época de las figuritas, pero creo que esto era sólo para niñas. Como les digo los motivos variaban, muchas representaban a niñas como en un dibujo, había de animales, ángeles, fantasía. Y con mi amiga Claudia las mencionamos hace unos días, me trajo recuerdos. En este diseño y tal vez en algún otro más adelante, quise traer este recuerdo, pero hacerlo digitalmente. Me encantó la experiencia.

Process in pictures - Proceso en imágenes
|![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23t86WE3GGSbbhziwLa1i81bgYB213iADhdHz9pFKSxWsvkJAWwrbTpyZuT9DF6MQmAkX.jpg)|![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23uFrsXQA9eoNazvBaTS5uNkoDNm8AiVe56m6beET7UPgsKHofV4Y7VLSMceRQQcKdRPi.jpg)| |-|-| |![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vsmXb9dJgc4wCoWJPvUtMEWd6PtKcC4dt9Qu7HduXtW15ShqcJWNYA1oaA36XCFFQPB.jpg)|![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23tw1sE6DusUSBDXxAuGkjcQy3tv7aHWzxxhq34wF3qTibfwFC9SkwoyGtqoBKehhCid2.jpg)| ||| |![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMsHSAnoGJoegmQBhxm2PbzfgxGy3DcybRHqNBcDP7EwjK8Uk7UquahZJWP9HASdxCk.jpg)|![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vsfj8x3QrgzxFQzWXQLnAwEKoX6AfZbZHEsNybAqZBbDKbWSrsG9xVBP2wuqunfjz1X.jpg)| ![separador sencillo 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/Eo8UGAXUZoPxi8Ny3bWhw7vRVQywdynrHRhAwwZtRqW9jnyK7CZ42782EyeJ1UKHQuv.png) # Design process The design was created entirely in Photoshop CS6 without the use of AI, using 10 royalty-free images spread across 20 layers. On a white layer, I placed the first watercolour image, over which I added four layers of the lined sheet, in different positions and with a drop shadow layer style to separate them from the background. On top of two of these layers and beneath the other two, I placed the first image of flowers with the darker colour blend, enhancing the outlines with an edge filter. Then, on top of this, I placed the second watercolour image using a soft light blend, and from the image of the green leaves I selected, copied and pasted some of them into the design, placing them on the right-hand side using a darker colour blend. I placed the second image of flowers on the other side of the design, in two layers, using the ‘Darken’ and ‘Normal’ blending modes, but for the latter I left only the part with the flowers. Beneath this image of white flowers, I worked on the two images of the drawings featuring children with cats, using the ‘Darken’ blending mode and erasing certain parts so they matched the edges of the leaves with lines. With the image of the girl, I created two layers using underexpose and normal colour blends. I applied the added edges filter to all of them, as well as to the image of butterflies using the darken blend. The animation is done completely in After Effects, working on the opacity of each layer and adding lights in the form of clouds for better contrast. I send you all a big hello and see you next time. Thanks for watching and reading this far. Amonet - AV Design
SPANISH VERSION (click here!)

# Proceso del diseño El diseño está realizado completamente en el programa Photoshop CS6 sin uso de IA con 10 imágenes sin derechos de autor distribuidas en 20 capas. Sobre una capa blanca dispuse la imagen de la primera acuarela sobre la cual puse en cuatro capas la hoja con renglones, en distintas posiciones y con un estil de capa de sombra paralela para separarlas del fondo. Sobre dos de estas capas y debajo de las otras dos puse la primera imagen de flores con la fusión de color más oscuro, realzando los contornos con un filtro de bordes añadidos. Luego sobre lo anterior puse la segunda imagen de acuarelas con la fusión de luz suave y de la imagen de las hojas verdes fui seleccionando, copiando y pegando algunas de ellas en el diseño, colocándolas en el sector derecho del mismo con la fusión de color más oscuro. La segunda imagen de flores la coloqué al otro lado del diseño, en dos capas, con fusiones de color más oscuro y normal, pero de esta última dejé sólo la parte de las flores. Debajo de esta imagen de las flores blancas trabajé las dos imágenes de los dibujos donde hay niños con gatos, con la fusión de color más oscuro y borrando ciertas partes para que coincidan con los bordes de las hojas con renglones. Con la imagen de la niña hice dos capas con fusiones de subexponer color y normal. En todas ellas puse el filtro de bordes añadidos, como así también en la imagen de mariposas usando la fusión oscurecer. La animación está realizada completamente en After Effects, trabajando la opacidad de cada capa y agregando luces en forma de nubes para un mejor contraste. Les envío un gran saludo a todos y hasta la próxima. Gracias por ver y leer hasta aquí. Amonet - AV Design

body.title: Film Review: Little Big Man (1970)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/uuich47VwLn44B0gHmhgLt6hTcM.jpg)


Nothing better illustrates the profound cultural and political convulsions that reshaped American society in the late 1960s than the diametrically opposed manner in which Hollywood treated the same historical event—the Battle of the Little Bighorn—and its most infamous participant, George Armstrong Custer, across a span of three decades. In 1941, Raoul Walsh’s *[They Died with Their Boots On](https://peakd.com/hive-121744/@drax/film-review-they-died-with-their-boots-on-1941)*, a quintessential Classic Hollywood epic, swallowed the foundational myth of the Old West hook, line, and sinker. The film transforms Custer into a martyr, sacrificing himself and his men to prevent the Indians from defeating a much larger force, a portrayal that served as potent militaristic propaganda on the eve of America’s entry into the Second World War. Three decades later, Arthur Penn’s *Little Big Man* (1970), steeped in the anti-establishment sentiment and wholesale questioning of the American cultural edifice that defined the era, charts a completely different course. Featuring one of Dustin Hoffman’s most iconic performances, the film stands as one of the most prominent works of the New Hollywood movement and a seminal revisionist take on the entire Western genre, systematically dismantling the heroic myths its predecessor so fervently upheld.

Interestingly, Custer is not the film’s protagonist. The basis is Thomas Berger’s 1964 picaresque novel, and the central figure is Jack Crabb (Dustin Hoffman). The plot is framed by an interview the 121-year-old Crabb—a self-described “Indian fighter” and “the only white survivor of Little Bighorn”—grants to a sceptical historian (William Hickey). This narrative device immediately establishes a subjective, unreliable, and mythic quality to the tale. The story, unspooling from Crabb’s memory, begins in 1859 when the 11-year-old Jack and his older sister Caroline (Carole Androsky) become the sole survivors of a Pawnee attack. Taken to a Cheyenne camp, Caroline escapes, but Jack remains. Raised by the tribe under the wise and kind-hearted chief Old Lodge Skins (Chief Dan George), he is given the name “Little Big Man.” This idyllic period is shattered when, as a teenager, he is captured by the US Cavalry. He is placed in the care of the hypocritical Reverend Silas Pendrake (Thayer David) and his sexually frustrated wife Louise (Faye Dunaway), beginning a picaresque odyssey through the underbelly of white civilisation. He fails as a snake-oil salesman and a gunslinger, marries a Swedish woman named Olga (Kelly Jean Peters), and, after her abduction by Cheyenne, searches for her, reconnecting with Old Lodge Skins and eventually joining the US Cavalry as a “mule skinner.” It is here he first encounters General Custer (Richard Mulligan).

Witnessing the cavalry’s brutal massacre of Indian women and children during a raid, a disgusted Crabb deserts. He saves Sunshine (Aimée Eccles), a pregnant Cheyenne woman, rejoins his adoptive tribe, marries her and her sisters, and finds contentment. This happiness is obliterated in 1868 by Custer’s ruthless raid on the Cheyenne camp at Washita River, which claims Crabb’s family. Consumed by a desire for revenge, he infiltrates Custer’s camp but lacks the courage to kill him, descending into drunkenness and hermitry. The narrative culminates in 1876. Contemplating suicide, Crabb stumbles upon Custer’s 7th Cavalry on its final campaign. Offering his services as a scout, he is hired by a hubristic Custer, who delights in the idea of acting against Crabb’s hostile advice. In a final act of cunning, Crabb deliberately misleads Custer into advancing to the Little Bighorn, where the regiment is annihilated. In the poignant aftermath, Crabb and the ageing Old Lodge Skins discuss a future the chief knows is lost; despite their victory, the Cheyenne have lost the war. Resigned to death, Old Lodge Skins changes his mind when a life-affirming rain begins to fall—a moment of quiet, ambiguous grace.

Like many revisionist Westerns of its time, *Little Big Man* was forged in the crucible of the Vietnam War. By 1970, that conflict had fractured American society, turning a generation against the historical myths cherished by their forebears. The film’s script is palpably informed by contemporary events; the depiction of the US military butchering innocent women and children functions as a direct allegory for atrocities like My Lai. Director Arthur Penn would later draw explicit comparisons between the treatment of Indigenous peoples and the Holocaust, a perspective hinted at within the film itself. The historian character uses the word “genocide,” a term the 121-year-old Crabb does not recognise but whose meaning he instinctively grasps. 

The massacre scenes are depicted with a visceral, explicit brutality, utilising squibs and copious fake blood to convey the horror. They are intentionally unpleasant, yet Penn’s film avoids the exploitative excess of Ralph Nelson’s similarly themed *[Soldier Blue](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-soldier-blue-1970-2af)* (1970). Where *Soldier Blue* was criticised for reducing atrocity to lurid entertainment, *Little Big Man* integrates its violence into a broader, more nuanced tragicomic tapestry. The critique is no less severe, but it is arguably more effective for being part of a richer character study.

Yet, if the film’s intent is to confront America with its bloody past, this effort is partially undermined by its episodic, vignette-like structure—a legacy of the picaresque source material. Jack Crabb becomes a proto-Forrest Gump, tumbling through a revisionist history of the West where he samples various stereotypes: the white captive, the pious ward, the conman, the gunslinger, the cavalryman, the avenger. While this serves to deconstruct the genre’s archetypes, it can also feel disjointed, preventing a deep, sustained emotional engagement with any single episode. The narrative momentum is occasionally sacrificed for satirical breadth.

The film’s tone is a curious and sometimes unstable alloy of dark tragedy and broad humour. In the final scene, this combination works brilliantly, granting the Cheyenne and the audience a hard-won, bittersweet respite. Elsewhere, the jokes are hit-and-miss. The subplot involving Crabb’s tomboyish sister, who reappears as his gunslinging mentor, feels undercooked and tonally awkward. An episode featuring Wild Bill Hickok (Jeff Corey), while amusing, strays from history (Hickok died months after Little Bighorn) and feels like a tangential diversion. Furthermore, the satire of Bible-thumping hypocrisy via the Pendrakes is somewhat undermined by Faye Dunaway’s performance, which, while entertaining, edges into hammy caricature.

The film is notable for its embrace of the more liberal content standards of the New Hollywood, particularly in its treatment of sexuality. The character of Little Horse (Robert Little Star), an effeminate Cheyenne who shows obvious homosexual attraction to Crabb, is a remarkably progressive inclusion for a mainstream 1970 film.

What ultimately holds this sprawling, ambitious project together is Dustin Hoffman’s magnificent, chameleonic performance. He relishes the opportunity to embody Crabb’s immense complexity, transforming from a wide-eyed teenager to a broken old man. The grotesque ageing makeup, which Hoffman later said made him feel authentically old, is a testament to the commitment. Hoffman navigates each incarnation—failed criminal, reluctant husband, grieving widower, would-be avenger—with impeccable skill, providing the emotional anchor the episodic plot requires.

Equally vital is Chief Dan George as Old Lodge Skins. In a performance that made him the first Native American nominated for an Academy Award, George delivers a masterful blend of regal gravitas, weary wisdom, and gentle irony. He is the film’s moral and spiritual centre, and his relationship with Crabb provides its emotional core. His lament, “There is an endless supply of white men, but there has always been a limited number of human beings,” resonates with profound sorrow.

Penn strove for authenticity, filming near the actual battle locations in Montana and collaborating with Native American tribes who provided extras. This lends the Cheyenne camp scenes a palpable texture often absent from earlier Westerns. Casting actresses of Asian background for the roles of Sunshine and her sisters, while a pragmatic decision of the time, is a noticeable flaw in this pursuit of authenticity.

As Custer, Richard Mulligan delivers another key performance, portraying the general not as a misguided hero nor a cold professional, but as a vainglorious, murderous lunatic. His Custer is a preening megalomaniac whose demise is stripped of any martyrdom, rendered as the inevitable culmination of racist hubris. Mulligan would later cleverly reference this role in the 1984 film *[Teachers](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-teachers-1984)*, playing a mentally ill man who impersonates historical figures, including Custer.

A significant artistic flaw is the film’s lack of a proper musical score. While this may have been a deliberate choice to avoid sentimentalising the story, it leaves certain sequences feeling oddly bare, lacking the sonic grandeur or emotional underscoring that a composer like, say, the aforementioned Max Steiner (who scored *They Died with Their Boots On*) could have provided.

Despite these imperfections—the episodic structure, the uneven humour, the absent score—*Little Big Man* remains a very good film. It succeeds as an entertaining, if demanding, hybrid of Western, historical epic, and black comedy. More importantly, it transcended its immediate political context. While *Soldier Blue* succumbed to didacticism and heavy-handedness, *Little Big Man* wielded its critique with greater subtlety and humanity. It served as a direct inspiration for later, more polished treatments of similar material, most notably Kevin Costner’s *[Dances with Wolves](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-dances-with-wolves)* (1990), which would revisit the theme of a white man finding kinship with Native culture, albeit with a more romanticised and less caustic sensibility.

*Little Big Man* is a landmark of cinematic revisionism. It systematically dismantled the jingoistic myths, replacing heroic martyrdom with ambiguous survival, and national destiny with personal and cultural tragedy. Reflecting the disillusionment of the Vietnam era, it holds a dark mirror to American history. Flawed yet formidable, carried by powerhouse performances and unflinching in its vision, it works as a compelling, challenging inquiry into the stories a nation tells itself, and the brutal realities those stories often conceal.



RATING: 7/10 (+++)

body.title: i344 JB200, Drawing step by step /Rising Star
body.body: > Blessings once again, everyone. Today I'm back, as usual, to show you the new drawing I've done. If you're here on my blog, you're probably eager to see it, and don't worry, I'll show it to you in just a moment. But before we begin, I'll tell you a few details about the drawing. This one is inspired by the i344 JB200 card; as you can see, it's a cute green microphone. This microphone is from the common section. But this microphone is special and different from the others I've done before for a very particular reason. This is the newest microphone released in the game in the common section, so I'm sure I'm the first to paint it; no one else has drawn it. And that always excites me—being the first to do something. With that said, let's begin. You already saw a preview of how it turned out on the cover, but now I'll show you the step-by-step process. The first thing I did was the inner frame of the card. This frame has the classic and usual shape you already know from my drawings; it looks like this. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ2xgSwJN1wqiEkcKoePtECu6e7XswiSNGvLBNqdKTmqn/1.jpg) After drawing the frame, I sketched the complete outline of the microphone. I started with what would be the handle and then drew the knob on top. That completed the outline. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfTtCkvESouqXoXLbRtSHPdUytMxwgapxPp3jAXUPdwSy/2.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmatJY9A9AcsxNnqyT3bDixiJypAkvSJFznhkx95eTAhAZ/3.jpg) Once that step was finished, I drew several internal divisions inside the microphone to complete the sketch. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR3VNc9S4qHKwBU3zVdkDpnLRRrP7yxA5E216Dt32hvtk/4.jpg) Now we can move on to painting. As you can see, I used green as the main color; it's the most prominent color, appearing in the background and on the microphone itself. I also used other colors, such as navy blue for the frame and various shades of blue for the background inside the card, among others. You can see the order in which I used them in the following photos. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ6MHZJQgxRG8RJWzzAeT2PHDgGh7rTqLb7KxPymfma57/5.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRffsgLb8Faxh4UwbtuDx3ExW59EXxNpfy5mMoPuNDRCb/6.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZzFwrvgtLD468yXf8tW6Je6JkzA5y6QV3qqZUMy1wQim/7.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZJhQvmtBwhjj1j7vKSG4Mkq2USaw2urUMFNuzWzyvoed/8.jpg) And finally, here's the finished result. Thank you so much for viewing my drawing. See you in the next one. Blessings to all. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYuPo2pp3N53sLjZQdwK8XucQuL7qPJYYmUzCSwp1NsQk/9.jpg)

body.title: WHY DO PEOPLE DIE || MCGI TOPIC REVIEW
body.body:
https://youtu.be/Hfy5sK-Y1gQ?si=UujoAyRtS7dCC8QF
Sin was the main purpose that death came into this world. When Adam and Eve disobeyed God, sin entered human life, and death became part of the human experience. According to the Bible, death is not how God originally wanted life to be, but it became the result of mankind’s separation from Him. 

>Romans 5:12 says, “Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, and in this way death came to all people, because all sinned.”

The bible also teaches us that every human have his or her time to spend on this earth, meaning we will die one day. Death reminds people that this world is not permanent and that we need to seek God while we are alive. Even faithful people in the Bible experienced death, showing that no human can escape it through their own strength or wisdom.

body.title: Topic Review: Forgive and forget — what does the Bible say?
body.body:
https://youtu.be/rI1_UqxSoB4?si=u7XdyO20ACpSVaRv

God desires peace, love, and tranquillity rather than conflict between us. God pardons us for our transgressions. He anticipates that we would also pardon others for their own transgressions and failings. He provided a positive example for us to follow. 

This should be how we model our lives, even though it can be challenging at times. It is not beneficial for us to not forgive. God taught that if we come before Him while harbouring animosity toward others, we should first go and resolve our problems before coming back to Him, which may be the reason why our prayers are occasionally impeded.

We are not following Jesus Christ in the proper manner if we do not provide forgiveness to others. In a sense, we don't care about people around the world because most of them don't think it's immoral to be unforgiving. However, it is completely flawed in the context of Christianity.

Tiramisu is a classic Italian dessert and I’ve tried it on several occasions; they were all different because it depends on who makes it, but when made by an Italian, it’s exquisite, it has to be homemade. I’ve tried it in Italian restaurants where not only do they claim the food is Italian, but the owner and all the staff are Italian too; they have a real tradition. That’s where I tasted the most delicious tiramisu. 

Before that, my cousin used to make it, and I didn’t like hers. The one I see in the photos looks absolutely stunning, and it’s perfect with a cup of coffee, but if you ever get the chance to visit an Italian restaurant… try it again; you’ll be surprised. body.title: My Journey Into Storytelling as a Profitable Skill [ENG/ESP]
body.body:
<div  class=text-justify>

It's been a while for me here in the community but I've been learning a lot while away. One of my main goals for this year 2026 is to grow on a skill that will be pay in the nearest future. I've been working on my entrepreneurial mindset by reading books, mentors and attending webinars.

One of the biggest lessons I've learned in this journey is, ***\

***. I really find that lesson cool because it is how the world has changed so much, where people get things done faster because some people came up with ideas.

![IMG_20241205_125910.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/EoCfknHTn577pHjnGsAVH7p6qvSaAGWtKWvzo68HWUVhGDuAi1Erk7EiEFZc2qVirGq.jpg)

There are so many great ideas today that is making lives easier, I am sure to say it is all the power of entrepreneurship because they thought of a problem and brought solution. It's one thing to see a problem, it's another to be bothered about the problem. So I think entrepreneurs who are making it a point of duty to act on their thoughts are worth being praised for their works.

In that spirit, I have started to take note of problems that I want to solve as an upcoming entrepreneur and the skill that is closest to who I have always been since childhood, is what I'll be using to solve these problems. The world started with a story, people have stories, life is a story.

I want to be able to tell these stories so well and impact lives with them. I've been telling stories since I was a little girl but I didn't know there was a high paying skill called **\

** until I decided to change my life, asked myself questions and figured there's a thing I want to do. This skill will not only solve problems for me *(Finding storyworthy moments in my life that will live in my memory all my life)*, the skill will also solve problems for people *(Those who can not tell their own stories but have stories that should be heard)*. I also plan to use this skill to make sales and grow businesses faster for people. ![IMG_20260127_144528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/EoGxsiVKzztiqTtAVHm431qBJ2x98E1uwvZGHFnEuhftm9TrGvNgnECfnGTHazUVkQ5.jpg) It's a long process, I have to learn from scratch again even though I've always had the skill in me. And this is because I want to do a remarkable job when I finally start to impact lives with my stories. I also want to learn the skill in the professional way because it was casual before. I'm grateful for my guide who has been helping me find the right books to hone my skill, I'm also attending classes that expands my knowledge for when I start writing stories for the most unexpected situations. I'm also keeping conscious track of stories happening in my life. All these are exciting processes for me and I can't wait to be good enough in my storytelling skill to prove to myself and the world that I have something we all need - *That our stories has to be told and these stories happen everyday in life.*
### **Spanish Translation**
> Ha pasado un tiempo desde que estoy aquí en la comunidad, pero he estado aprendiendo mucho mientras estaba ausente. Uno de mis principales objetivos para este año 2026 es crecer en una habilidad que me pague en un futuro cercano. He estado trabajando en mi mentalidad emprendedora leyendo libros, aprendiendo de mentores y asistiendo a seminarios web. > Una de las lecciones más grandes que he aprendido en este camino es: \

. Realmente encuentro esa lección muy interesante porque muestra cómo el mundo ha cambiado tanto, donde las personas logran hacer las cosas más rápido porque algunas personas tuvieron ideas.

![IMG_20241205_125910.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/EoCfknHTn577pHjnGsAVH7p6qvSaAGWtKWvzo68HWUVhGDuAi1Erk7EiEFZc2qVirGq.jpg)

> Hoy en día hay tantas ideas geniales que están haciendo la vida más fácil; estoy segura de que todo es el poder del emprendimiento, porque alguien pensó en un problema y trajo una solución. Es una cosa ver un problema, y otra muy distinta es preocuparse por él. Así que creo que los emprendedores que hacen de ello un deber actuar sobre sus ideas merecen ser reconocidos por su trabajo.

> Con ese espíritu, he comenzado a tomar nota de los problemas que quiero resolver como emprendedora en crecimiento, y la habilidad que está más cercana a quien siempre he sido desde la infancia es la que usaré para resolver estos problemas. El mundo comenzó con una historia, las personas tienen historias, la vida es una historia.

> Quiero ser capaz de contar estas historias de una manera tan buena que impacte vidas. He estado contando historias desde que era una niña, pero no sabía que existía una habilidad bien remunerada llamada \

hasta que decidí cambiar mi vida, hacerme preguntas y descubrir que hay algo que quiero hacer. > Esta habilidad no solo resolverá problemas para mí (encontrar momentos dignos de ser contados en mi vida que vivirán en mi memoria para siempre), sino que también resolverá problemas para otras personas (aquellos que no pueden contar sus propias historias pero tienen historias que deben ser escuchadas). También planeo usar esta habilidad para generar ventas y ayudar a que los negocios crezcan más rápido. ![IMG_20260127_144528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/EoGxsiVKzztiqTtAVHm431qBJ2x98E1uwvZGHFnEuhftm9TrGvNgnECfnGTHazUVkQ5.jpg) > Es un proceso largo; tengo que aprender desde cero nuevamente, aunque siempre he tenido esta habilidad dentro de mí. Y esto es porque quiero hacer un trabajo extraordinario cuando finalmente comience a impactar vidas con mis historias. También quiero aprender la habilidad de manera profesional, porque antes era algo casual. > Estoy agradecida con mi guía, quien me ha estado ayudando a encontrar los libros adecuados para perfeccionar mi habilidad. También estoy asistiendo a clases que amplían mi conocimiento para cuando empiece a escribir historias en las situaciones más inesperadas. Además, estoy llevando un registro consciente de las historias que ocurren en mi vida. > Todos estos procesos son emocionantes para mí y no puedo esperar a ser lo suficientemente buena en mi habilidad de narración para demostrarme a mí misma y al mundo que tengo algo que todos necesitamos: que nuestras historias deben ser contadas y que estas historias suceden cada día en la vida. **Images used are mine.** Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@merit.ahama/my-journey-into-storytelling-as-a-profitable-skill-engesp-7sd)

![voting.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23wWyBwcaXnQTVzb7s8QPCPuVKFqoYRo2V5nZn1d6Rcnu6UftefrfXiqxUpr3MQuKMR6x.jpg)



Woke up this morning to find that as expected Labour have lost seats and councils in this local election. This was to be expected as was Reform gaining seats and 2 councils. At the time of writing the Conservatives have lost 170 seats and 1 local authority.  The Lib Dems gains so far are 247 seats up 39 and the gain of 2 councils.

Not all the counting is done yet and I expect from what I’ve seen that some big cities and some London boroughs will report their result later.  No point in going too much into the numbers at this stage as counts are still going on.

What’s becoming clear though is that Labour are taking a battering in terms of seats lost.  They’ve been afflicted by incumbent party syndrome where voters punish a party in national government at local elections.  This has been compounded by public disgust at the entire Labour leadership class and their perceived contempt for ordinary working Britons.  Whether this will force a change of leadership is difficult to predict but Labour’s problem is that they’ve got a dearth of top talent waiting in the wings.  Unlike in the 60’s and 70’s there are no political titans left in Labour who could take hold of the tiller, now the potential leadership pool is shallow and the public don’t seem to like many of the alternatives to Starmer.

From what I’ve seen of the results so far we may be looking at a situation where Reform become the primary party for working class Britons with the working class abandoning Labour.  That’s to be expected as Labour have for too long been a party of the wealthy, the public sector grifter, the members of the ‘lanyard classes’, the doley and Islam.  If an entire class can be abandoned by the party that was set up expressly for them, then it is to be expected that that class will abandon their former party.

I’ll try and write more if I can during today about the results and I’ll attempt a longer form article on this issue on Sunday morning.

body.title: 5 Forint 1947 Lajos Kossuth
body.body:
Hello, another day, another coin. Today I’d like to show you another half-silver coin, but from a different country – communist Hungary, to be precise. I bought it as part of a batch of coins from a market stall. I plan to go back there tomorrow and see if the gentleman is still there. I’ll try to get his phone number, which might lead to a longer-term collaboration. I like making contacts, even the smallest ones in the world of coin collecting. The photos were taken against a backdrop of Baltic Sea gold – amber. Do take a look!



# <center> Hungary 5 Forint 1947 </center>



This is a Hungarian 5-forint coin from 1947, a very interesting period, as formally we still have the Hungarian Republic here, but the political climate of the region after the Second World War was already being heavily shaped by a brutal new order, which is why such coins fit very well with my theme of post-war half-silver coins from countries that were already falling into the orbit of the communist system at that time. On the obverse we see Lajos Kossuth, one of the most important figures in Hungarian history, a man associated above all with the Hungarian Revolution and the struggle for independence; so the figure on the coin is no accident, as the Hungarians were very keen to invoke such national symbols, and the revolutionary theme was very convenient for the communists. The coin may not be some great rarity, but in my opinion it is very pleasing, as it is a good size, is made of silver, features a simple yet distinct portrait, and comes from a period that has recently been of growing interest to me: post-war silver from Red Central and Eastern Europe.



On the reverse, we see the denomination of 5 forints, the date 1947 and the inscription ‘Magyar Köztársaság’, meaning the Republic of Hungary, and the whole design is executed in a fairly simple, official style, without any excessive embellishment, yet it still looks better than many later aluminium or copper-nickel coins. My specimen is already quite worn, with scratches, scuffs and that characteristic look of old silver that has been in circulation, but having bought it from a market stall at a price close to that of silver, this doesn’t bother me at all, because you buy such coins partly for the metal, partly for the history, and partly because it’s simply nice to have them in your collection. It’s worth mentioning that the 1947 5-forint coin was struck in 500-fine silver, so here we have my favourite ‘half-silver’ coin again – a coin that may not contain a huge amount of pure silver, but is still not just an ordinary modern coin, and you can feel in your hand that you’re dealing with something older and more substantial. I like shopping like this, because sometimes, amongst the usual lot from a market stall, you come across something like this – perhaps not an expensive numismatic item, but one that complements a collection well and showcases a piece of the country’s history, which isn’t collected quite as often in Poland as Germany, Russia or the UK. Another advantage of such coins is the price; you can buy many of them and build a nice silver collection.

Witam, kolejny dzień, to kolejna moneta. Dziś chciałbym przedstawić kolejne półsreberko, ale z innego kraju, a dokładniej z komunistycznych Węgier. Kupiłem ją razem z lotem monet ze straganu. Jutro planuję znowu tam pojechać i zobaczyć czy ten pan dalej tam jest. Spróbuję jeszcze zgarnąć numer telefonu, dzięki czemu może wyniknie jakaś dłuższa współpraca. Lubię robić sobie kontakty, nawet te najmniejsze w świecie zbieractwa monet. Zdjęcia zrobione są w otoczce ze złota Morza Bałtyckiego, czyli bursztynu. Zapraszam!

# <center> Węgry 5 Forintów 1947 </center>

Jest to węgierska moneta o nominale 5 forintów z 1947 roku, czyli z bardzo ciekawego okresu, bo formalnie mamy tutaj jeszcze Republikę Węgierską, ale klimat polityczny tego regionu po II wojnie światowej był już mocno ustawiany przez brutalny nowy porządek, dlatego takie monety bardzo dobrze pasują mi do tematu powojennych półsreberek z krajów, które już wtedy wpadały w orbitę  czerwonego systemu komunistycznego. Na awersie widzimy Lajosa Kossutha, czyli jedną z najważniejszych postaci węgierskiej historii, człowieka kojarzonego przede wszystkim z rewolucją węgierską i walką o niezależność, więc sama postać na monecie nie jest przypadkowa, bo Węgrzy bardzo chętnie odwoływali się do takich symboli narodowych, a temat rewolucyjny był bardzo wygodny dla komuchów. Moneta nie jest może jakimś wielkim rarytasem, ale moim zdaniem jest bardzo przyjemna, ponieważ ma dobry rozmiar, jest srebrna, ma prosty, ale konkretny portret i jest z tego okresu, który ostatnio coraz bardziej mnie interesuje, czyli powojenne srebro z czerwonej Europy Środkowej i Wschodniej.

Na rewersie widzimy nominał 5 forintów, datę 1947 oraz napis Magyar Köztársaság, czyli Republika Węgierska, a całość jest zrobiona w takim dość prostym, państwowym stylu, bez przesadnego kombinowania, ale nadal wygląda to lepiej niż wiele późniejszych monet aluminiowych czy miedzioniklowych. Mój egzemplarz jest już dość mocno zmęczony, ma rysy, przetarcia i ten charakterystyczny wygląd starego srebra po obiegu, ale przy zakupie ze straganu i cenie zbliżonej do srebra kompletnie mi to nie przeszkadza, bo takie krążki kupuje się trochę dla metalu, trochę dla historii, a trochę dlatego, że po prostu fajnie mieć je w kolekcji. Warto wspomnieć, że 5 forintów z 1947 roku było bite w srebrze próby 500, więc znowu mamy tutaj moje ulubione półsreberko, czyli monetę, która może nie ma w sobie ogromnej ilości czystego srebra, ale nadal nie jest zwykłym współczesnym bilonem i w ręce czuć, że mamy do czynienia z czymś starszym oraz konkretniejszym. Lubię takie zakupy, bo czasami wśród zwykłego lotu ze straganu trafi się właśnie coś takiego, co nie jest może drogim numizmatem, ale dobrze uzupełnia kolekcję i pokazuje kawałek historii kraju, który w Polsce nie jest aż tak często zbierany jak Niemcy, Rosja czy Wielka Brytania. Kolejnym plusem takim monet jest cena, można kupić wiele takich monet i zbudować ładną srebrną kolekcję.
