title.title: Health as a Living Practice [En-Sp]
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdKVr1BhvSzETS48qwzMno48pE9ogEzMfhFwASo2NJwaE/1778216003002.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/pata-perro-mano-mascota-amigos-7231300/)

In my work, I’ve come to realize that health isn’t something you can fully capture in lab results or medical charts. It shows itself in how people manage to keep going through the realities of their lives. And that doesn’t always come down to genetics or strict routines. Health is built in the everyday, in the way we relate to ourselves and to others.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZbrPYjBMNFrdqvH2Y12jkeT56BWfxLd5iJLmP4p3ghzj/1778216112911.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/relajarse-centro-de-salud-masaje-686392/)

I’ve met patients who believed their struggles were purely biological. Biology matters, of course. But once we look closer, the real story often emerges. A woman who couldn’t sleep, not because of a neurological disorder, but because she had been carrying the weight of caring for her sick mother alone. A man whose panic attacks didn’t ease with medication until he finally spoke about the crushing pressure at work. What helped them wasn’t just treatment—it was recognizing that emotional balance and social support are part of health itself.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYAAcuduaNEfWKrtTsU7CeKAwR31bBaqhTgwzWGi85MYv/1778216272905.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/autocuidado-priorizaci%C3%B3n-8282075/)

Research backs this up. Chronic stress disrupts the immune system, fuels inflammation, and raises the risk of heart disease. On the other hand, people with strong social ties and safe spaces to share their experiences consistently show better outcomes across almost every medical condition. That’s not a metaphor—it’s data. And I see it reflected in my practice week after week.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYM3htN94okrWJqSHVqQYSjsLzR1HwUReLkyfAdcv9szR/1778216375235.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/granero-cabina-fuego-hoguera-gente-2594975/)

I think of a patient who struggled for years with uncontrolled hypertension. He had tried different medications, but his blood pressure stayed high. The missing piece was his environment: a toxic workplace with endless hours and no rest. When he changed jobs and learned to manage stress, his numbers began to stabilize. That wasn’t luck—it was physiology. Lower cortisol, better sleep, healthier routines.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaTBWPnkUCSUvTj1EELKbwUatjuzp8mrfSuHd7MrkXQzF/1778216426382.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/felices-vacaciones-mujer-perro-3042751/)

Or the young woman with depression who had lost all sense of meaning. Medication was part of her care, but what truly shifted her trajectory was reconnecting with joy: dancing again, listening to music, spending time with friends. Neuroscience explains it—those activities activate reward circuits, release dopamine and serotonin. But beyond the chemistry, what I witnessed was someone reclaiming her will to live.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXRSVn42hPw845y4Hy9MLygxEfisMRytPa3WFadXLiVLc/1778216511553.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/joven-mar-amigo-al-aire-libre-8208513/)

Health isn’t a fixed state or a privilege reserved for those with “good genes.” It’s a dynamic process, shaped by small choices: getting enough rest, moving your body, talking to someone you trust, setting boundaries when you need to. And it’s also shaped by deeper attitudes: accepting what you can’t control, practicing gratitude, holding on to hope even when life feels uncertain.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXbjc3rJhaqndzuXP5KsXGhJUMf9ACArsZfx9Y2rFnuLP/1778216654705.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/paseando-parejas-parque-amigos-3755342)

As a psychiatrist, I know the value of medication and therapy. But I also know that much of the healing happens outside the clinic. In honest conversations with friends, in the pause you allow yourself, in the quiet of a walk outdoors. These aren’t extras—they’re foundations of health. Science supports it, and my experience confirms it.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSnDPUTX3j95QXPaXjVGP3Sktpm5xbF5LYqTP1tuJVxNd/1778216943968.jpg)

[Source[(https://pixabay.com/es/photos/gente-muchachas-mujeres-estudiantes-2557399/)

So my message is straightforward: caring for your health isn’t just about tests and routines. It’s about living with awareness, with connection, with purpose. It’s about recognizing that mind and body are inseparable, that what you feel shapes who you are. And ultimately, health is cultivated in real life, in every gesture that brings you closer to being at peace with yourself and with others.

***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfKffNs5EWqSF7irjaFD2hnahPFPe6aXdXqp15fNrpmXb/1778217015289.jpg)

***

Versión en Español 

\

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdKVr1BhvSzETS48qwzMno48pE9ogEzMfhFwASo2NJwaE/1778216003002.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/pata-perro-mano-mascota-amigos-7231300/)

En mi consulta he aprendido que la salud no se mide únicamente en cifras de laboratorio ni en diagnósticos médicos. Se mide en cómo una persona logra sostenerse en medio de lo que le toca vivir. Y eso, créanme, no siempre depende de los genes ni de la disciplina con la dieta o el ejercicio. La salud se construye en lo cotidiano, en la manera en que nos relacionamos con nosotros mismos y con los demás.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZbrPYjBMNFrdqvH2Y12jkeT56BWfxLd5iJLmP4p3ghzj/1778216112911.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/relajarse-centro-de-salud-masaje-686392/)

He visto pacientes que llegan convencidos de que su problema es puramente biológico. Y claro, la biología importa. Pero cuando empezamos a mirar más allá, aparecen las historias que realmente explican el malestar. Una mujer que no lograba dormir no porque tuviera un trastorno neurológico, sino porque llevaba meses cargando sola con el cuidado de su madre enferma. Un hombre con crisis de pánico que no mejoraba con medicación hasta que se permitió hablar de la presión que sentía en su trabajo. En ambos casos, lo que abrió la puerta a la recuperación fue reconocer que la salud también se sostiene en el equilibrio emocional y en el apoyo social.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYAAcuduaNEfWKrtTsU7CeKAwR31bBaqhTgwzWGi85MYv/1778216272905.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/autocuidado-priorizaci%C3%B3n-8282075/)

La investigación lo confirma: el estrés mantenido altera el sistema inmunológico, aumenta la inflamación y favorece enfermedades cardiovasculares. En cambio, las personas que cuentan con vínculos sólidos y espacios de confianza tienen mejor pronóstico en prácticamente todas las condiciones médicas. No es poesía, es evidencia. Y yo lo veo cada semana en mi práctica.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYM3htN94okrWJqSHVqQYSjsLzR1HwUReLkyfAdcv9szR/1778216375235.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/granero-cabina-fuego-hoguera-gente-2594975/)

Recuerdo a un paciente que llevaba años con hipertensión difícil de controlar. Había probado distintos tratamientos, pero la presión seguía alta. Cuando hablamos de su vida, apareció un detalle que nunca había considerado: trabajaba en un entorno hostil, con jornadas interminables y sin descanso. Al cambiar de empleo y aprender a manejar el estrés, su presión empezó a estabilizarse. No fue magia, fue neurobiología: reducir el cortisol y recuperar rutinas de sueño y alimentación equilibraron su cuerpo.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaTBWPnkUCSUvTj1EELKbwUatjuzp8mrfSuHd7MrkXQzF/1778216426382.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/felices-vacaciones-mujer-perro-3042751/)

También pienso en una joven con depresión que había perdido el sentido de todo. Lo que la ayudó no fue únicamente el tratamiento farmacológico, sino volver a conectar con actividades que le daban alegría: bailar, escuchar música, compartir con sus amigas. La ciencia explica que esas experiencias activan circuitos de recompensa en el cerebro, liberan dopamina y serotonina. Pero más allá de los neurotransmisores, lo que vi fue a alguien que recuperaba ganas de vivir.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXRSVn42hPw845y4Hy9MLygxEfisMRytPa3WFadXLiVLc/1778216511553.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/joven-mar-amigo-al-aire-libre-8208513/)

La salud, entonces, no es un estado fijo ni un privilegio de quienes tienen buena genética. Es un proceso dinámico que se alimenta de decisiones pequeñas: dormir lo suficiente, moverse, hablar con alguien de confianza, poner límites cuando es necesario. Y también de actitudes más profundas: aceptar lo que no podemos controlar, cultivar la gratitud, sostener la esperanza en medio de la incertidumbre.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXbjc3rJhaqndzuXP5KsXGhJUMf9ACArsZfx9Y2rFnuLP/1778216654705.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/paseando-parejas-parque-amigos-3755342/)

Como psiquiatra, sé que los medicamentos y las terapias son herramientas valiosas. Pero también sé que la verdadera medicina muchas veces ocurre fuera del consultorio: en la conversación honesta con un amigo, en el descanso que nos permitimos, en la calma de una caminata al aire libre. No son detalles menores, son pilares de la salud. La ciencia lo respalda, y mi experiencia lo confirma.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSnDPUTX3j95QXPaXjVGP3Sktpm5xbF5LYqTP1tuJVxNd/1778216943968.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/gente-muchachas-mujeres-estudiantes-2557399/)

Por eso mi mensaje es sencillo: cuidar la salud no es solo cumplir con exámenes y rutinas. Es aprender a vivir con conciencia, con vínculos, con propósito. Es reconocer que la mente y el cuerpo no están separados, que lo que sentimos impacta en lo que somos. Y que, al final, la salud se cultiva en la vida real, en cada gesto que nos acerca a estar un poco más en paz con nosotros mismos y con los demás.

***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS8NxVgy4gwzyp6DQhH5bFiDnCC7e3UoZD2sHdkm8NfM4/1778217569544.jpg)

title.body:
QUESTION: How would Steemit's @world-travel-pro spend four days in Bangkok?



![z98.jpg](https://img.blurt.blog/blurtimage/world-travel-pro/08281ec147b54753ef94ef2c3f28743963ec8607.jpg)



ANSWER: Based on his travel philosophy and past recommendations, Steemit's @world-travel-pro would likely spend 4 days in [Bangkok](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/0fn2g) focusing on budget-friendly local experiences, affordable luxuries, and avoiding \

traps.
## Core Travel Philosophy

* Budget Savvy: He often highlights ultra-cheap finds, such as [private AC rooms for $10 USD](https://steemit.com/@world-travel-pro/road-to-steemfest-5-the-thai-life-and-what-to-expect) and massages for under $5.
* Active Exploration: He prefers [walking over taking tuk-tuks](https://steemit.com/@world-travel-pro/world-travel-report-11-vientiane-laos) to truly \

though he acknowledges tuk-tuks for convenience if you haggle well.
* Freedom over Schedules: He typically suggests booking only the first few nights and [keeping the rest open-ended](https://steemit.com/travel/@johnnyfdk/thinking-about-going-to-thailand-travel-tips) to allow for spontaneous changes in plans.

## Likely 4-Day Bangkok Itinerary 

## Day 1: Local Immersion & Street Food

* Morning: Explore the local neighborhood on foot. @world-travel-pro values the \

of a simple walk around the block.
* Afternoon: Visit [Wat Arun](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/05s69t) (Temple of Dawn). Even for repeat visitors, this remains a staple recommendation for its iconic riverfront presence.
* Evening: Street food dinner in Silom Soi 20 or [Chinatown (Yaowarat)](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/g/11t6wxn1ry), focusing on high-quality but low-cost meals.

## Day 2: Parks & Modern Bangkok

* Morning: A run or walk in [Lumphini Park](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/09rxcz). He appreciates free activities and green spaces.
* Afternoon: Explore the Ari neighborhood for artisanal coffee or head to [Siam Square](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/088vqz) for people-watching and window shopping.
* Evening: Visit a rooftop bar like [Octave](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/g/1s049rb_s) or [Above Eleven](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/g/1pzqsvgvy) for a \

at sunset—one of the few areas where he might suggest a splurge. 

## Day 3: Cultural Deep Dive or Day Trip

* Option A (Cultural): Visit the [Bangkok National Museum](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/02vnrfw) or the [Jim Thompson House](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/03hlbr1) to understand Thai history and architecture.
* Option B (Day Trip): Take an early morning trip to [Ayutthaya](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/024tvh) to see the ancient ruins, returning in time for a late afternoon Thai foot massage.
## Day 4: Markets & Last Massages

* Morning: If it’s a weekend, a visit to [Chatuchak Weekend Market](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=/m/015g8y) is essential for unique finds and cheap eats.
* Afternoon: Get a final Thai massage at a local shop (aiming for those $5–$7 deals he enjoys).
* Evening: A riverfront walk near Asiatique or a casual dinner with friends, emphasizing social connection over tourist shows.

## What He Would Avoid

* Overpriced Transport: He warns against tuk-tuks that try to charge double or triple the going rate and suggests haggling firmly.
* Generic Tourist Traps: He generally avoids highly scripted \

or over-commercialized boxing stadiums in favor of authentic street life.
................................................................................................
WTP OPINION: This sounds very accurate. This is very much how I would approach four days in Bangkok. Not into drinking, so the roof top bar would be switched with maybe a high end hotel buffet or something.

   Also I would not be haggling over tuk-tuks in 2026. I would be using metered taxis, grab app, and their modern subway system.

Photo credit- @world-travel-pro!

Just looking at the design and fighting style of this card, it is clear that it is designed to play an aggressive role in the game. Many times this card can put pressure on the opponent at the beginning of the match and help your team move forward. This card is quite effective for those who like fast-paced gameplay. It is especially suitable for those who like to attack quickly and put pressure on the opponent. With the right team combination and planning, this card can greatly increase your chances of winning. I hope this review of mine will be helpful to you and you will be able to perform better using this card.

title.title: No Days Off, Still at the Gym 💪🔥 / Sin Descanso, De Nuevo en el Gym 💪🔥
title.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPfhfmSt8y4wpyiYNCnU5HvrscAUK1fR54ESaPHRxCPT6/IMG_8163.jpg 

Here I am again at the gym, no days off, staying consistent and committed to my goals. Some might say I should rest more, and maybe they’re right sometimes, but today I felt that inner push to keep going. It’s not always about being perfect, it’s about showing up and staying disciplined with myself.

There are days when my body feels tired, when the energy isn’t at its best, but I’ve learned that consistency is built in moments like this. Even if the workout is lighter, even if I don’t give 100%, just being here already means a lot. It’s a reminder that I’m serious about my progress.

I’m proud of myself for not stopping, for choosing effort over excuses again and again. Step by step, I keep building strength, confidence, and a better version of me. And yes… here I am, once again, giving it my all at the gym. 💖✨

>Aquí estoy otra vez en el gym, sin descanso, siendo constante y comprometida con mis metas. Algunos dirán que debería descansar más, y tal vez tienen razón a veces, pero hoy sentí ese impulso interno de seguir. No se trata de ser perfecta, sino de presentarme y mantener mi disciplina.

>Hay días en los que el cuerpo se siente cansado y la energía no es la mejor, pero he aprendido que la constancia se construye justo en momentos como este. Aunque el entrenamiento sea más ligero o no dé el 100%, el simple hecho de estar aquí ya vale mucho. Es una señal de que voy en serio con mi proceso.

>Me siento orgullosa de no parar, de elegir el esfuerzo sobre las excusas una y otra vez. Poco a poco sigo construyendo fuerza, seguridad y una mejor versión de mí. Y sí… aquí estoy de nuevo, dando lo mejor en el gym. 💖✨

title.title: Ramen de pollo con jengibre/ Chicken ramen with ginger 🍜🫚
title.body:
> Feliz noche foodies! Que tal su día? Por estos lados bastante bien, haciendo varias cositas geniales y entre ellas este **ramen con pollo y jengibre** que quedó realmente rico y que por supuesto no podía dejar de compartir con ustedes para que también disfruten de una comidita súper deli.
Good evening, foodies! How’s your day going? Things are going pretty well over here – I’ve been up to all sorts of lovely things, including making this **chicken and ginger ramen**, which turned out absolutely delicious. Of course, I just had to share it with you so you can enjoy a really tasty meal too.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc6Dq9JKWRcnbcsbKWgyP4qCjoAc5hdHZKFnUdVUEHGMA/1778207865056.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) Esta receta me la encontré hace unos días en la web y la pinta que tenía era tan provocativa que tenía que prepararla en casita y en mi caso utilicé los sobrecitos de ramen sabor a pollo de la marca Kaldini que son mis favoritos y añadí diferentes ingredientes como pechuga asada, champiñones, huevo sancochado, y el ingrediente estrella que es el jengibre. Una mezcla de sabores que estoy segura les va a encantar, y lo mejor de todo es que es bastante sencilla de hacer.
I came across this recipe online a few days ago and it looked so tempting that I just had to make it at home. I used Kaldini brand chicken-flavoured ramen packets – they’re my favourites – and added various ingredients such as grilled chicken breast, mushrooms, a soft-boiled egg, and the star ingredient: ginger. A blend of flavours that I’m sure you’ll love, and best of all, it’s quite simple to make.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaZX4UvZRSKenGHmSmyY5kiVdYNWqWSegHvcwFAgi8BNY/1778207865602.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) ## Ingredientes 1 pechuga de pollo 1 cebolla mediana 1 ramita de cebollín 1 ramita de ajoporro 2 dientes de ajo Salsa de soya Repollo Jengibre fresco 1 lata de champiñones 2 huevos Sal y pimienta
## Ingredients 1 chicken breast 1 medium onion 1 sprig of chives 1 sprig of leek 2 cloves of garlic Soy sauce Cabbage Fresh ginger 1 tin of mushrooms 2 eggs Salt and pepper
## Procedimiento/Procedure Para la preparación de este platillo lo primero que haremos será condimentar la pechuga de pollo con sal, pimienta y salsa de soya y la podremos a cocinar a fuego medio hasta que esté bien cocida.
To prepare this dish, the first thing we’ll do is season the chicken breast with salt, pepper and soy sauce, then cook it over a medium heat until it’s thoroughly cooked.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNWqBXDUybXeh78r3gascE1sYxEXwciKuBgYxLkXQBcir/1778208000055.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) Mientras la pechuga se cocina cortamos todos los vegetales que formarán parte de nuestro ramen y ponemos en una olla a hervir 1.5 litros de agua.
Whilst the chicken breast is cooking, chop all the vegetables that will go into our ramen and bring 1.5 litres of water to the boil in a saucepan.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYyRQT5FXrPpnKQ6aSmx5QAqLQsJdxCguveTq7c9RNd17/1778207865985.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaHySThfCubDN2bse1MaoSNrNopgWAgRNWxVkQVsaMyQf/1778207866230.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) Seguidamente retiramos la piel del jengibre y cortamos 6 rodajas y una vez el agua comience a hervir agregamos todos los vegetales y cuatro cucharadas de salsa de soya, y cocinaremos por diez minutos.
Next, peel the ginger and cut it into 6 slices. Once the water starts to boil, add all the vegetables and four tablespoons of soy sauce, and cook for ten minutes.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPe7noK2pyPSaFV5WmiTWDykMU88JH1xP5zJjViAWBTJ3/1778207866477.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeLjDCZGqdDiu1Mp8qCoaRo5kGtZJsysmrWjtkww1q9d4/1778207999821.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) En este punto nos encargamos de sancochar los huevos y saltear los champiñones con una cucharada de salsa de soya. Y reservamos para el momento de servir.
At this stage, we blanch the eggs and sauté the mushrooms in a tablespoon of soy sauce. We set them aside until ready to serve.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeHnTMpHVrutZqUZRL6EegNaLYcvcEXUCFLMERwKqSGk5/1778208000267.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) Transcurridos los diez minutos agregamos el sobre del condimento del ramen junto con los fideos y dejamos cocinar hasta que estén en su punto, lo que toma aproximadamente 8 minutos. Para este momento, ya la pechuga debe estar lista, así que la cortaremos en rebanadas delgadas y reservamos.
After ten minutes, add the packet of ramen seasoning along with the noodles and leave to cook until they are just right, which takes about 8 minutes. By this point, the chicken breast should be ready, so slice it thinly and set aside.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPCqu9ks8DWjZd4iDToNpkwGkgEqJzgpc2DwRynV3VCFu/1778208000485.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) Una vez tenemos listos todos los componentes de nuestro ramen solo nos queda emplatar, y lo primero que agregaremos serán los fideos junto con el caldo. Seguidamente agregamos el pollo, medio huevo y champiñones, finalizando con cebollín fresco por encima.
Once all the ingredients for our ramen are ready, all that remains is to plate it up, and the first things we’ll add are the noodles and the broth. Next, we add the chicken, half an egg and the mushrooms, finishing with a sprinkling of fresh chives on top.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma1QTyCT8LtfKdiTrQVKCy3fTGgKNdTtgou42XtA9Vhgi/1778208000712.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaL2DaCbcY71sqsRmQrzAmX3uPUCUr8kVsYqwbGpqbqQ/1778208114597.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrAtDwCbtQWhspQ3fZXZeAUy9hLt9oKpPonMJbvaGuui/1753392698151.png) El resultado? Uffff demasiado rico, y aunque tiene muchos pasos, vale demasiado la pena porque es simplemente increíble y se ve tan bello que definitivamente es un plato que te invita a disfrutarlo. >The result? Mmm, absolutely delicious! And although there are quite a few steps involved, it’s well worth the effort because it’s simply incredible and looks so beautiful that it’s definitely a dish that invites you to enjoy it.

title.title: [카일의 수다#870]2020년 드라마 도시남녀의 사랑법
title.body:
![IMG_0474.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeAkU78vU3CVeitiwsEj6ruTCUD2nzsYbxyzFYBCJMeLC/IMG_0474.webp)


지창욱, 김지원의 조합이 궁금했던 드라마.
막상 보기 시작하니 생각보다 훨씬 현실적이고 감성적인 작품이었다.

2020년에 공개된 드라마인데도 지금 봐도 전혀 촌스럽지 않다. 오히려 요즘 짧고 자극적인 콘텐츠들 사이에서, 이런 현실 연애 감성이 더 반갑게 느껴졌다.

드라마는 인터뷰 형식으로 진행된다.
등장인물들이 카메라 앞에서 자신의 연애를 털어놓는 방식인데, 처음엔 조금 낯설지만 보다 보면 오히려 그래서 더 현실적으로 느껴진다.
누군가의 연애썰을 옆에서 듣는 기분이랄까.

특히 초반 양양 에피소드 분위기가 정말 좋았다.
서핑, 바다, 여름밤, 즉흥적인 만남들.
젊고 자유로운 공기들이 화면에 가득해서 괜히 나까지 여행 온 기분이었다.

그 여행지에서만 가능한 감정들이 있다.
평소의 나보다 조금 더 솔직해지고, 조금 더 대담해지고,
“지금 이 순간”만 생각하게 되는 그런 분위기.

근데 이 드라마가 좋았던 건, 그 설레는 감정을 그냥 로맨틱하게만 소비하지 않는다는 점이었다.
서울로 돌아오고 현실이 시작되면서 연애 속 불안함, 감정의 온도차, 관계를 이어가는 어려움 같은 것들이 너무 현실적으로 다가온다.

좋아하는 마음만으로는 안 되는 순간들.
연애하면서 누구나 한 번쯤 느껴봤을 감정들이 꽤 디테일하게 나온다.

지창욱과 김지원의 분위기도 정말 잘 어울렸다.
특히 김지원 특유의 자연스러운 감정 연기가 드라마 분위기랑 너무 잘 맞았던 것 같다.

16부작 전통 드라마들처럼 큰 사건이 계속 터지는 스타일은 아닌데, 그래서 오히려 더 현실 연애 느낌이 난다.
잔잔하게 흘러가는데 이상하게 계속 보게되는 드라마.

2020년 작품인데도 여전히 좋았던 이유는 아마 ‘연애 감정’ 자체는 시간이 지나도 크게 변하지 않아서 아닐까.

설레고, 답답하고, 좋아하고, 도망치고, 후회하는 마음들.
도시에서 살아가는 평범한 사람들의 연애 이야기라 더 마음에 와 닿았다.

title.body: I am always impressed by the amount of produce you obtain from such a small space. Even with a huge garden, I've never been able to grow enough of everything we like to eat in order to last an entire year. Especially onions; they don't do well for me. We've had some good potato years, some lousy years. The winter squash rarely last beyond March in our above-ground root cellar. How do you store your carrots? That's another we've always struggled with. One year I tried canning them, but they were big enough to need to be peeled, and boy! did that ever hurt my arthritic thumbs! There has to be a better way.

title.title: La costumbre de resistirlo todo [Esp/Eng]
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXoa5rSqWX2Qnjm4YvWDvBb2jqLR1Yw2NDtU2JhqK2DpE/3938030_woman_1958723_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/woman-solitude-sadness-emotions-1958723/)

---

🇪🇸 En Español

# La costumbre de resistirlo todo

---

A veces no es el problema lo que más pesa… sino la forma en que aprendimos a vivir con él como si fuera normal.

---

Hola querida comunidad @holos-lotus,

Hay escenas que no necesitan ser extraordinarias para quedarse grabadas en la memoria. A veces son justamente las más cotidianas las que dicen más sobre quiénes somos y cómo hemos aprendido a sobrevivir.

Recuerdo una noche cualquiera en Cuba, de esas en las que la corriente se va sin aviso. No hay explicación, no hay hora estimada de regreso, no hay control posible. Simplemente ocurre.

La casa quedó en silencio, como siempre pasa en esos momentos. El calor comenzó a hacerse más presente, los mosquitos también, y la oscuridad dejó de ser solo ausencia de luz para convertirse en una especie de presencia incómoda.

La gente alrededor, como es habitual, empezó a adaptarse. Algunos salieron a la puerta, otros se quedaron sentados en silencio, y otros simplemente aceptaron la situación como parte del día.

Pero lo que más me llamó la atención no fue el apagón en sí.

Fue una frase.

Alguien dijo con naturalidad:

> “Bueno… al menos hoy vino el agua.”

---

Y en ese instante ocurrió algo curioso.

Nadie se sorprendió.

Nadie corrigió la frase.

Nadie la cuestionó.

Solo hubo un pequeño asentimiento colectivo, como si aquello tuviera sentido.

Y fue ahí cuando me di cuenta de algo que con los años he seguido viendo una y otra vez: la capacidad que tenemos de ajustar nuestra percepción de lo normal según lo que vamos perdiendo.

---

## La normalización de lo difícil

Desde mi experiencia como médica, he escuchado frases similares en muchos contextos. Personas que describen síntomas claros de agotamiento, ansiedad o estrés, pero los acompañan siempre con la misma idea:

“pero eso es normal”.

Y esa palabra, “normal”, a veces me deja pensando más que el propio síntoma.

Porque lo que empieza siendo una respuesta puntual a una situación difícil, puede terminar convirtiéndose en una forma de vida.

---

## Resistir como hábito

En contextos como el nuestro, resistir no es una elección ocasional. Es casi un aprendizaje temprano.

Se aprende a:
- esperar  
- resolver  
- improvisar  
- adaptarse  

Y con el tiempo, esa capacidad de adaptación tan valiosa empieza a transformarse en otra cosa: la incapacidad de reconocer cuándo algo ya no debería ser normal.

---

## Lo que el cuerpo no dice en voz alta

Hay algo que también he observado desde lo médico: el cuerpo rara vez se adapta sin costo.

El organismo se acostumbra a la tensión, al estrés, al cansancio sostenido… pero no lo hace sin dejar huella. Lo que se normaliza emocionalmente, muchas veces se acumula físicamente.

Y lo más complejo es que, cuando finalmente aparece el malestar, ya no se percibe como algo nuevo, sino como “parte de la vida”.

---

## La pregunta que queda

Esa noche del apagón, con aquella frase aparentemente simple, entendí algo que no he dejado de pensar desde entonces:

> ¿en qué momento dejamos de notar lo que realmente nos está costando vivir así?

---

Tal vez la verdadera reflexión no sea solo sobre la falta de luz o de recursos, sino sobre cómo, poco a poco, aprendemos a sobrevivir tanto… que olvidamos cómo se siente simplemente vivir en equilibrio.

Y quizás el primer paso no sea dejar de resistir.

Sino volver a preguntarnos si todo lo que estamos resistiendo debería seguir siendo normal.

---

Gracias por leerme.

Las imágenes son de Pixabay y la traducción al inglés fue hecha en DeepL Translate.

----

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXoa5rSqWX2Qnjm4YvWDvBb2jqLR1Yw2NDtU2JhqK2DpE/3938030_woman_1958723_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/woman-solitude-sadness-emotions-1958723/)

---

🇬🇧 In English

# The Habit of Enduring Everything

---

Sometimes it is not the problem itself that weighs the most… but the way we learn to live with it as if it were normal.

---

Hello dear @holos-lotus community,

There are scenes that do not need to be extraordinary to remain in memory. Sometimes it is precisely the most ordinary moments that reveal the most about who we are and how we have learned to survive.

I remember a regular night in Cuba, one of those when the electricity goes out without warning. There is no explanation, no estimated time of return, no control. It simply happens.

The house fell silent, as it always does in those moments. The heat became more noticeable, the mosquitoes as well, and darkness stopped being just the absence of light and became something almost tangible and uncomfortable.

People around, as usual, began to adapt. Some stepped outside, others remained quietly seated, and others simply accepted the situation as part of the day.

But what caught my attention was not the blackout itself.

It was a sentence.

Someone said naturally:

> “Well… at least we have water today.”

---

And in that instant, something happened.

No one was surprised.

No one corrected it.

No one questioned it.

Only a subtle collective acceptance, as if it made sense.

And that was when I realized something I have kept seeing over the years: our ability to adjust what we consider normal depending on what we are gradually losing.

---

## The normalization of difficulty

From my experience as a physician, I have heard similar expressions in many contexts. People describing clear symptoms of exhaustion, anxiety, or stress, always accompanied by the same idea:

“but this is normal.”

And that word, “normal,” sometimes makes me think more than the symptom itself.

Because what begins as a response to a difficult situation can slowly turn into a way of life.

---

## Endurance as a habit

In contexts like ours, endurance is not an occasional choice. It is almost an early learned behavior.

We learn to:
- wait  
- solve  
- improvise  
- adapt  

And over time, this valuable adaptability begins to turn into something else: the inability to recognize when something should no longer be normal.

---

## What the body does not say out loud

There is something I have also observed medically: the body rarely adapts without cost.

The human system adjusts to stress and exhaustion, but not without consequences. What is normalized emotionally often accumulates physically.

And the most complex part is that, when symptoms finally appear, they are no longer perceived as something new, but as “part of life.”

---

## The question that remains

That night of the blackout, with that seemingly simple sentence, I understood something I have not stopped thinking about:

> when did we stop noticing what it is truly costing us to live this way?

---

Perhaps the real reflection is not only about the lack of electricity or resources, but about how, little by little, we learn to survive so much that we forget what it feels like to simply live in balance.

And perhaps the first step is not to stop enduring.

But to start asking ourselves whether everything we are enduring should still be considered normal.

---

title.title: Squid and Apple Salad\\Tintenfisch-Apfel-Salat
title.body:
Hello,my friends!
Today we're cooking a salad with boiled squid, fresh apples, and boiled eggs in mayonnaise sauce. A real protein bomb! Squid, sorry, is delicious in any form, but squid is especially good in salads. The recipe is simple; you just need to have quality squid on hand. Blue, rotten squid is never quality! Let's go, it'll be delicious!


![1.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW46rZxJMBaEsuwALa5iPymhy2vE8GYL3GBLPLutVTqC7/1.jpg)


Ingredients:
● 6 frozen squid (palm-sized squid)
● 2 fresh apples
● 3 eggs
● 1 tbsp sesame seeds
● 250g or more mayonnaise
● 2 tbsp 6% wine vinegar
● Black pepper - a pinch
● Salt - a pinch
● Sugar - 1 tsp
● Mustard - 1 tsp (to taste)
● Fish sauce (optional) - 2 tbsp
● Hot pepper, green onions, and herbs - to taste

1.Cook the squid. I used Far Eastern squid with the skin on. Some people defrost them first, but I don't bother. Place the squid in the sink and rinse them briefly with warm water to remove the ice and soften the body. Then I cut off the tail, cut it in half, and cut the body in half lengthwise. I clean out the entrails, spine, and membrane from the inside. Using my hands and water, I remove the skin. If there's any skin left, don't worry; the remaining skin will peel off when boiled in water. Bring the water to a boil and drop in the squid pieces. Cook for 1-2 minutes; the squid will begin to curl into tubes, indicating it's ready. Good squid will be a creamy white or slightly pink color. Now you can transfer the squid pieces to cold water; this will make the remaining skin easier to peel off.


![2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQAqtMZVPAFgdpwXx8Wm44w7D2sXxJgzp2vZV6YGs2ek9/2.jpg)


2.Dice the squid. There's a lot of squid, which is good. You could cut it into strips, but we have apples in the salad, and dicing them is easiest.



![3.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWSirdonWtjT3gzLxhzSicdUY1D2gW9K8KES4cZbz94uz/3.jpg)


3.Add the squid to the pan and immediately add some mayonnaise. Peel and core the apples and dice them. Add the apple cubes to the salad.



![4.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQx85KvjA9RWac1sBQQeQhftmdooo78UBuFyjaXnzj9Kn/4.jpg)


4.Peel the hard-boiled eggs and cut them into pieces. Add the eggs to the salad.



![5.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUktDgRnxdb5RHgpxsDY5n7ojnRJuiuFGw9k2XvTJ44RR/5.jpg)


5.Now add the remaining mayonnaise, a spoonful of sesame seeds, 2 tablespoons of wine or apple cider vinegar, a pinch of hot pepper, salt, and sugar, a spoonful of mustard, green onion rings, and, if desired, a couple of tablespoons of fish or Worcestershire sauce for a piquant flavor. Toss the salad and refrigerate. 30 minutes is plenty of time.



![6.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbjMHgFsavfBVfqQB83L6229rE5g2vsQ2oY7UKKE4Dcpt/6.jpg)


6.Serve the squid and apple salad. It has a very delicate and pleasant flavor. The apples add a wonderfully refreshing touch!




![7.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXPCQ6yt8GyjyMN2wbKpYREjex9QT8qN31W3k58VSZmCJ/7.jpg)

Shall we make it?

![3-poloska-1.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyhhAydYCgxXo6MZeZ3YC526qwyBdU2NCdMXtyoJGAXB/3-poloska-1.png)

Heute machen wir einen Salat mit gekochtem Tintenfisch, frischen Äpfeln und gekochten Eiern in Mayonnaise. Eine echte Proteinbombe! Tintenfisch ist einfach in jeder Form lecker, aber in Salaten schmeckt er besonders gut. Das Rezept ist simpel; man braucht nur hochwertigen Tintenfisch. Blauer, fauler Tintenfisch ist nie gut! Los geht's, es wird köstlich!

Zutaten:
● 6 gefrorene Tintenfische (handflächengroß)
● 2 frische Äpfel
● 3 Eier
● 1 EL Sesamsamen
● 250 g oder mehr Mayonnaise
● 2 EL 6%iger Weinessig
● Schwarzer Pfeffer – eine Prise
● Salz – eine Prise
● Zucker – 1 TL
● Senf – 1 TL (nach Geschmack)
● Fischsauce (optional) – 2 EL
● Chili, Frühlingszwiebeln und Kräuter – nach Geschmack

1.Die Tintenfische zubereiten. Ich habe Tintenfische aus Fernost mit Haut verwendet. Manche tauen sie vorher auf, aber ich mache mir die Mühe nicht. Die Tintenfische in die Spüle geben und kurz mit warmem Wasser abspülen, um das Eis zu entfernen und sie weicher zu machen. Dann schneide ich den Schwanz ab, halbiere den Körper und halbiere ihn der Länge nach. Ich entferne die Innereien, die Wirbelsäule und die Haut. Mit den Händen und Wasser ziehe ich die Haut ab. Falls Hautreste zurückbleiben, ist das kein Problem; die restliche Haut lässt sich beim Kochen leicht abziehen. Ich bringe das Wasser zum Kochen und gebe die Tintenfischstücke hinein. Nach 1–2 Minuten Kochzeit rollt sich der Tintenfisch zu Röhren zusammen und ist dann gar. Guter Tintenfisch ist cremeweiß oder leicht rosa. Nun können Sie die Tintenfischstücke in kaltes Wasser geben; dadurch lässt sich die restliche Haut leichter abziehen.

2.Den Tintenfisch würfeln. Es ist eine große Menge, was gut ist. Man könnte ihn auch in Streifen schneiden, aber da wir Äpfel im Salat haben, ist das Würfeln am einfachsten.

3.Den Tintenfisch in die Pfanne geben und sofort etwas Mayonnaise hinzufügen. Die Äpfel schälen, entkernen und würfeln. Die Apfelwürfel zum Salat geben.

4.Die hartgekochten Eier schälen und in Stücke schneiden. Die Eier ebenfalls zum Salat geben.

5.Nun die restliche Mayonnaise, einen Löffel Sesamsamen, 2 Esslöffel Wein oder Apfelessig, eine Prise Chiliflocken, Salz und Zucker, einen Löffel Senf, Frühlingszwiebelringe und nach Belieben ein paar Esslöffel Fischsauce oder Worcestershiresauce für eine pikante Note hinzufügen. Den Salat vermengen und 30 Minuten im Kühlschrank ziehen lassen.

6.Den Tintenfisch-Apfel-Salat servieren. Er hat einen sehr feinen und angenehmen Geschmack. Die Äpfel verleihen ihm eine wunderbar erfrischende Note!

Wollen wir ihn zubereiten?

![3-poloska-1.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyhhAydYCgxXo6MZeZ3YC526qwyBdU2NCdMXtyoJGAXB/3-poloska-1.png)



![U5duDCNw2pr2jpJvE8CRni125dys5tM_1680x8400.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXaogGpoD7LJkEufiNxjF52VcPhQZJYsJet34fDwJyYUV/U5duDCNw2pr2jpJvE8CRni125dys5tM_1680x8400.png)![U5dr1BuE8ejAxctktpDvrzGctPnaMgF_1680x8400.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVmydUTmF1ECe7u87FkCoJYcxT6Xo9spqJBWGi8G3ntXH/U5dr1BuE8ejAxctktpDvrzGctPnaMgF_1680x8400.jpg)

title.title: How Geelong Windows Quietly Improved Insulation, Comfort, and Daily Living
title.body: The original idea was small paint a few rooms, clean up the outdoor area, and finally deal with a couple of annoying maintenance issues we had ignored for too long. But once I started spending more time at home during the renovation, I noticed the windows constantly. One didn’t close properly anymore. Another made a soft rattling noise whenever the wind picked up late at night. Small things, really. But once you notice them, they somehow become impossible to ignore. That’s basically how I ended up researching [**geelong windows**](https://www.avistawindows.com.au/) and realising there’s a lot more involved than I first thought.

>Why I Started Looking Into Geelong Windows At first, I assumed window upgrades were mostly cosmetic. But after paying attention for a few days, it became obvious the older windows were affecting comfort too. Rooms felt colder early in the mornings Outside traffic noise seemed louder than before Some frames looked worn after years of weather exposure A few windows felt stiff and difficult to open properly My research about double glazed windows and aluminium frame windows and custom window solutions for Geelong and Melbourne areas started when I began my reading. The more I studied contemporary systems I discovered that our existing windows were actually more outdated than I had originally thought. It wasn’t just about appearance anymore. It was about insulation, airflow, and daily comfort.

>First Impressions During the Showroom Visit I visited a showroom connected with Avista Windows after someone casually mentioned them during a conversation. The first thing I noticed was how calm everything felt. No aggressive sales talk. No overwhelming technical explanations. Just different window systems displayed in a way that made comparison easy. Seeing modern geelong windows in person was honestly different from looking at photos online. The aluminium frames looked slimmer, cleaner, and much more modern than older timber windows. One staff member demonstrated a double glazed window by shutting it while noise from outside was coming through the open display area. The difference was immediate. That small demonstration probably explained more than twenty minutes of technical talk could have.

>Understanding the Process Felt Easier Than Expected I originally assumed replacing windows would become stressful and confusing. But the process itself felt surprisingly manageable. Measurements discussed room by room Frame styles explained in simple language Window designs matched to home layout Installation timelines outlined clearly I also learned that many homeowners upgrading geelong windows don’t wait until windows completely fail. They replace them when comfort and efficiency start becoming noticeable issues. That honestly made a lot of sense.

>Actual Benefits I Started Noticing Even before making final decisions, I could already understand why people invest in modern windows during renovations. Better insulation during colder weather Reduced outside noise entering the home Cleaner and more modern appearance Easier maintenance compared to timber frames Better natural lighting and airflow indoors I didn’t expect windows to affect daily living this much, but they really do. Modern home window solutions are clearly designed around energy efficiency and comfort now, not just appearance.

>A Small Interaction That Felt Genuine There was one small interaction during the visit that actually stayed with me. I asked whether replacing all windows at once was necessary because I was worried about budget and disruption. The reply was simple: “Most people do it gradually. There’s no need to rush everything together.” It sounds minor, but that instantly made the process feel less overwhelming. No pressure. No hard sales approach. Just practical advice. Sometimes that alone makes you feel more comfortable dealing with a company.

>Why Geelong Windows Started Making Sense What began as a simple renovation project slowly turned into something more practical. Looking into geelong windows made me realise how much older windows quietly affect everyday comfort without people fully noticing. Small drafts during colder nights Noise levels you slowly get used to Older frames affecting overall appearance Reduced insulation impacting room temperature Once you start noticing those things, it becomes difficult to ignore them again.

>Why More Homeowners Prefer Modern Window Solutions What stood out most during the experience wasn’t just the products themselves—it was how practical modern systems have become. Today’s window designs focus on: Energy efficiency Noise reduction Low maintenance materials Cleaner modern aesthetics Long-term durability And honestly, that combination makes a lot of sense for modern homes.

>Final Thoughts I didn’t expect window upgrades to become something I’d spend so much time thinking about. But after seeing the difference modern aluminium and double glazed systems can make, it became clear why so many homeowners upgrade windows during renovations instead of waiting for major problems. The whole experience felt less about replacing frames and more about improving how the home actually feels every day. In the end, exploring geelong windows turned out to be one of those small renovation decisions that quietly improves comfort, insulation, and everyday living far more than you initially expect.

***
This report documents the activities, contributions, and progress of our group during our project mandate. 

23rd November 
As a commencement to our project,  our first meeting held in the common room (by 9:30pm) on how to proceed with our project. A recording was made for those who weren’t present

24th November 
Mmesoma and Ejiro created a google form revolving around the appeal and opinions of the vendor Grandpas Chips.  This for, was distributed amongst platforms to students so we can assess feedback as marketing promoters and strategise what our next move would be.

25th November  
Suggestions by group members were made regarding the form and corrections were made to make up for any inaccuracies or mistakes in the google form. After corrections were made, the form was once again disseminated across platforms.


26th November. 
Victoria, oyindamola and Faaz had a meeting with the store owner of Grandpa chips (Victor Chukwuwujindu). We informed the owner about our plans and mandate issued by our lecturer and we came to an agreement to further discuss our execution plans with his permit at a later date.

28th November 
An extensive interview transcript simplified and created by Faaz was given on our group chat on telegram. The interview outline provided an insight on Grandpa chips business and gave us an idea of how to properly combat its flaws and provide resolutions as marketing/sales promoters. 

30th November 
Another meeting was held. All members attended. A survey dashboard comprising of customer feedback and responses to Grandpa chips services and food was provided by Victoria. Together the team analysed the database and sought ways to improve and regulate customer satisfaction and expectations and at the same time improve the standards of Grandpa chips holistically.

2nd December 
The group leader Victoria provided an execution plan. It was a composition of agreements and analysis made at hour previous meeting. IMC tools were highlighted as the  foundational framework in which  we’d properly implement our ideas and apply them appropriately.

4th December 
A final meeting with us and Mr. Chukwuwujindu  was organised before our departure for Christmas holiday in order to present the ideas and concepts developed by our team and gain his approval. The discussion held at the meeting was particularly positive and we decided to execute our plans after resumption as agreed by Mr Chukwuwujindu.

title.title: The Storm and a little damage to our last Sets of Dry Season Corn Stalks
title.body:
# Hello Hive 



![5137.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23zRreYGycJ2nwqZYo7irY1R6zAFe2Bicpiqf2T8gPF43SxAtfYiHPP2qtY4u4rz7dcPX.jpg)



Happy new day to us all. I hope that we have had a wonderful night rest and in good health. 

As I am just recuperating I haven't really done any stressful work recently. Two day ago I was at home and took out time to plant some water leaf veggies. 


Yesterday I finally visited the farm to check in how well the roos are doing only to be meet with some damages to our corn farm here.


![5119.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23uFPgj2GRJencYTQUqWV5kSW344ojVjoUrAnA8PcoD3LxvCLW5btHoimAFEjpRyBVsp9.jpg)

Each time there is a heavy storm like as it is this morning tall plants tends to fall and if they are yet to produce their food as at the time they can get poorly affected. 
This corn has already borne it's cobs and is at its maturing stage. I'm not so sure if these corns are matured enough within. 


Some of the corn roots were completely uprooted from the ground and the can no longer continue growing but other are still rooted even in this position and hopefully they will do well too

![5137.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23zRreYGycJ2nwqZYo7irY1R6zAFe2Bicpiqf2T8gPF43SxAtfYiHPP2qtY4u4rz7dcPX.jpg)


The rains are usually aggressive here whenever it starts failing. It's comes with heavy breeze and storm removing people's roof and flooding the whole stress. Nothing happens in moderation anymore and it's so worrisome. Hopefully we won't have more damages here before these finally gets harvested.

![5125.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23xKrGb49F5S5fNF7iR6QwPhVathGGwYFx1i6xt2sQ7omar9ARG9xBesYb7gKpJTJQV3d.jpg)

Even till now we are yet to commence farming for this year. 
The land has been cleared for tillage. There are no portable tractors here to do the job and being a hard labour we are yet to get labourers. Alot of people are now shying away from hoeing the land. Those are olden days methods of farming. Life has improved so well that I wished that some of these development will reach our ends here to ease us of much stress and burden. There are portable tillage machines I have seen over the internet but I wonder how long it will take for us to get hold of similar technology for farming.

title.title: 「Vicky's Life」短剧｜《惊鸿一瞥》（陈添祥x刘念）
title.body:
![IMG_0170.jpeg](https://s2.loli.net/2025/08/11/AihYzKqpnWCx4U8.jpg)

要我说看剧还得是看一线合作的剧，流量身份摆在那里强强联手的本子和资源自然不会差。我还是第一次看陈添祥的现代剧，没想到同刘念同台搭戏的感觉还蛮不错。

从剧情的角度来说，我觉得这是个男女双强又相互救赎的故事。女主同闺蜜的生意需要一匹宋锦布料而料子在男主手上，她为了得到料子故意接近他，起初闹了很多乌龙。

随着了解的加深，我们发现男主事业有成但原生家庭也有问题。他早年在US的时候，别墅里塞买了想要把他养废的人和物件。他那些年没睡过一个安稳觉，非常之脆弱。

从人设的角度来说，我非常喜欢女主敢爱敢恨的性格。她既可以在事业上拼尽全力又能很好的爱人，面对重男轻女的家长不亢不卑。有点像赫本feel的妆造，也非常吸睛。

男主的人设我觉得是那种内心有点创伤但能很好控制自己，控制欲很强有些霸道总裁的感觉。很难想象陈添祥年纪那么小居然可以将这个角色诠释好，禁欲系感觉拉满。

从拍摄和服化道的角度来说，这部剧总体来说画面很精致。总体的色调完全不是糖水短剧的廉价感，不管是主角还是配角的妆造都在线的，看得出剧组很花心思和钱。

总的来说，特别好看的剧，推荐啦！


（本篇完）

title.title: Film Review: Hot Girls Wanted (2015)
title.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/6xBGfuKg20WXtqdWokrwBMM0hAH.jpg)



In the contemporary digital landscape, where recent estimates suggest that approximately ten percent of all American women between the ages of 18 and 24 earn their primary income as content creators on platforms like OnlyFans, it is increasingly difficult to recall a time when such work resided firmly in the shadows. Not so long ago, participation in the sex industry—even its newer, internet-adjacent forms—was considered a subject not for polite conversation, let alone serious cinematic examination. When the film industry did deign to address it, the approach typically vacillated between cheap sensationalism and predictable moralising, often combining the worst aspects of both in a prurient package disguised as social commentary. This tradition is evident even in projects that purported to offer a more nuanced perspective, such as the 2015 documentary *Hot Girls Wanted*, directed by journalists Jill Bauer and Ronna Gradus. The film reveals a work caught between a genuine desire to understand a burgeoning subculture and an ingrained tendency to frame its subjects through a lens of implicit judgement, ultimately compromising its potential as a definitive study of the amateur pornographic milieu.

Bauer and Gradus, who had previously touched upon the intersection of technology and sexuality in their 2012 film *Sexy Baby*, initially conceived *Hot Girls Wanted* as an investigation into the predominantly male consumers of online pornography. However, the cultural landscape shifted dramatically in 2014 with the public outing of Miriam Elizabeth Weeks, a Duke University student who performed under the pseudonym “Belle Knox”. The ensuing media circus, which focused relentlessly on the scandal of a so-called “porn star” at an elite institution, provided Bauer and Gradus with a new, more commercially viable angle. They pivoted their focus to the young women entering the industry, a decision that simultaneously granted the film its relevance and planted the seeds for its conflicted perspective. The documentary narrows its gaze specifically to the world of “pro-am” pornography, a genre designed to simulate amateur authenticity while being produced by professional outfits. It is a sphere populated overwhelmingly by very young women, often lured by the twin promises of easy money and a thrilling escape from mundane provincial lives.

The film’s narrative engine is the experiences of six such women, aged 18 to 21, who responded to an advertisement posted by Riley, a Miami-based agent and part-time performer. In exchange for ten percent of their earnings, Riley provides them with accommodation in his home and schedules their shoots. The central arc follows Tressa, known professionally as Stella May, a 19-year-old high school graduate from Arlington, Texas, who moves to Miami to pursue this career instead of attending college as her family expected. The documentary traces a familiar trajectory: initial euphoria and excitement, fuelled by growing social media followings and a sense of newfound autonomy, followed by a rapid disillusionment. As the market’s appetite for fresh faces proves fickle, Tressa is pressured into accepting increasingly niche and extreme performances. The film documents her physical and emotional strain, culminating in health issues and the eventual intervention of her mother and initially supportive boyfriend, Kendall. Her decision to quit, erase her online presence, and return home to work as a restaurant manager is presented not merely as a personal choice but as the logical, morally correct conclusion to her story.

*Hot Girls Wanted* premiered at the Sundance Film Festival, garnering attention not only for its provocative subject matter but also for its association with producer Rashida Jones, whose involvement lent it a veneer of Hollywood legitimacy. Its subsequent distribution on Netflix guaranteed it a wide audience. On the surface, the film avoids the trappings of a simplistic, radical feminist critique. Bauer and Gradus largely refrain from portraying their subjects as helpless victims coerced by economic desperation or physical force. Instead, the women are presented as individuals with distinct, sometimes defiant, personalities—young adults who may be guilty of poor judgement or self-delusion but who occasionally offer sharp, perceptive commentary on their circumstances. The film even includes a fascinating segment on Belle Knox, whom the subjects view with a mixture of resentment and recognition, noting she began in similarly extreme content and has merely been more adept at leveraging her notoriety. Riley, the agent, is afforded moments of brutal honesty about the fleeting shelf-life of the performers, complicating any straightforward reading of him as a mere predator. By the documentary’s end, the attrition rate speaks volumes: of the six women followed, only two remain in the industry, with the others having quit or moved to other sectors of the sex trade.

Yet, this apparent nuance is systematically undermined by the film’s formal and editorial choices. Throughout, stark intertitles flash statistics about the prevalence of violent pornography, the youth of performers, and the alleged psychological harms of consumption. These inserts, devoid of contextual analysis or sourcing, echo the language of anti-pornography moral panics and implicitly frame the entire enterprise as a social pathology. This creates a profound dissonance: while the footage shows complex individuals making active choices, the textual commentary insists on a narrative of corruption and victimhood. Tressa’s exit is thus edited and scored to feel like a triumphant escape, a redemption arc that validates the filmmakers’ unspoken bias. The objectivity promised by the vérité style is ultimately sacrificed to a more traditional, cautionary tale structure.

This compromised stance drew mixed criticism upon release. Some praised its unflinching access, while others, particularly those within or sympathetic to the sex industry, accused it of being manipulative and inherently hostile. The criticism evidently resonated with Bauer and Gradus, who addressed it indirectly with their 2017 sequel series, *Hot Girls Wanted: Turned On*, which broadened the scope to explore technology’s impact on dating and intimacy. The shift suggests an awareness of the original film’s limitations.

In the end, *Hot Girls Wanted* is a document of a specific moment in the evolution of internet-era sex work, valuable for its raw footage and intimate access. However, its critical failure lies in its inability to fully commit to its own most interesting insights. It glimpses the nuanced reality of its subjects—their ambition, their naivety, their resilience—but repeatedly retreats into the comforting, editorialising framework of a social problem film. A decade on, as the mainstreaming of content creation has forced a more pragmatic, less hysterical public conversation, the documentary feels increasingly like a product of an older, more anxious morality. It captures the dawn of a revolution in adult entertainment but views it through the tinted lens of a past that could not quite imagine, or accept, the complex professional landscape these women were inadvertently helping to build.


RATING: 5/10 (++)

title.title: El amor es inherente al éxito. ❤️‍🩹🏆[Esp-Eng]
title.body:
>

<center>![InShot_20260508_001301674.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRvPMtd6JuebnL7FGLMe2sbo737EZnht4jLfwiy6mFLx8/InShot_20260508_001301674.jpg)</center>

Vivimos en un mundo donde el éxito económico, donde trabajar hasta alcanzar metas materiales y escalar lugares de poder, como ascensos laborales, títulos y sobresalir por logros no está bien visto, pues socialmente se cree que quién trabaja tanto para alcanzar esos objetivos lo hace desligado a los sentimientos de amor. 

Cuando la verdad es todo lo contrario, el camino al éxito no es fácil, así que mantenerse en ese camino es un acto de amor, amor personal, amor a lo que haces, amor a tus sueños, amor al éxito y además tener un entorno saludable que te impulse. 

Cuándo nos rodeamos de personas motivadoras, cuando tenemos un entorno saludable y amoroso, lograr nuestros objetivos y alcanzar el éxito es mucho más fácil además que serán logros compartidos, porque si bien es cierto que existen personas que alcanzan sus objetivos desde una posición fría, calculadora y amargada, también es cierto que ese éxito no es perdurable en el tiempo. 

Porque el éxito de la vida tiene muchos factores que influyen tanto positivamente como negativamente, y lo que hace la diferencia en el viaje son los sentimientos de la persona.

Una persona inteligente, mentalmente saludable, que tiene planes de éxitos trata de tener un entorno sano, motivador, donde pueda sentir apoyo y bienestar, porque gran parte del éxito de una persona comienza en las bases de sus relaciones. 

Cuando tenemos un entorno amoroso, el objetivo para alcanzar el éxito es mucho más motivador, porque no es simplemente tener un trofeo, un título o un puesto, es un logro compartido, es bienestar económico, es paz personal, familiar, de pareja y de amistad... Éxitos sin propósitos son frágiles, son vacíos y a veces ni siquiera se tiene un entorno para sustentarse, no hay con quién celebrar los logros, ni comentar las victorias. 

Así pues que sin duda alguna el amor es inherente al éxito, quien diga lo contrario es porque sencillamente no está enfocado realmente en surgir, ni tiene claro el camino y además le teme al tiempo, porque el camino al éxito no es fácil y socialmente se nos ha vendido que \

cuando en realidad el amor es un agente que impulsa. 

Una persona enamorada de sus objetivos, no se detiene en el tiempo, en los tropiezos, en los días grises... Ya que su corazón está blindado por la energía necesaria para seguir, es un corazón resiliente, con suficiente bienestar para poder mantenerse en el camino. 

Claro está también hay personas que sin sentimientos de amor se mantienen firmes hasta lograr lo que desean, pero estas personas tienden amargarse cuando hay un día difícil, cuando el tiempo es más largo o cuando los logros no son tal como lo desean. 

<div class=\

> ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQme3m6SkU94kYBdeK7fCzrMmEwoJZ4AMjGi4rKWH9iGrjX/image.png)[2] Así pues que cada uno de nosotros tiene en sus manos la posibilidad de decidir cómo quiere que sea su éxito, como un camino plano, en frialdad y soledad o tomar las riendas de su vida y caminar al éxito en paz, con amor y en compañía. ______ ###

We live in a world where economic success, working hard to achieve material goals and climb the ladder of power—with promotions, titles, and outstanding accomplishments—is frowned upon. Society often believes that those who work so hard to reach these objectives are detached from feelings of love. However, the truth is quite the opposite. The path to success is not easy, so staying on it is an act of love: self-love, love for what you do, love for your dreams, love for success, and also having a healthy environment that supports you. When we have a loving environment, the goal of achieving success is much more motivating, because it's not simply about having a trophy, a title, or a position; it's a shared achievement, it's financial well-being, it's personal, familial, romantic, and platonic peace... Successes without purpose are fragile, they are empty, and sometimes there isn't even a support system to sustain them, no one with whom to celebrate achievements or share victories. Therefore, without a doubt, love is inherent to success. Anyone who says otherwise is simply not truly focused on rising to the top, doesn't have a clear path, and is also afraid of time, because the road to success is not easy, and society has sold us the idea that \

when in reality, love is a driving force.

A person in love with their goals doesn't let time, setbacks, or gray days stop them... Because their heart is fortified with the energy needed to keep going; it's a resilient heart, with enough well-being to stay on the path.

Of course, there are also people who, without feelings of love, remain steadfast until they achieve what they want, but these people tend to become bitter when there is a difficult day, when time is longer, or when the achievements are not as they wish.

title.title: The Silverblogger Chronicles-Prompt #45.Black beans, family, and everything they carried. [EN/ES]
title.body:
Hello SilverBloggers community!

This week I’m joining the **Chronicles weekly prompt (Week 45)**, and instead of thinking about a single extraordinary meal, my memory keeps returning to something much simpler… something that was always there.

---

## The Taste That Never Left  
### *Black beans, family, and everything they carried*

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbUqwk8J5KoyTEuBhf3neB6zmRUUPNA7dik2WfojoN8VL/dioncerqueira_a_dish_made_of_5160472_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/a-dish-made-of-food-eat-kitchen-5160472/)

---

When I was a child, I grew up in a small rural town. I used to travel to the city often, but no matter where I went during the day, I always returned home.

And at home, there was something constant.

The table.

Back then, meals were not like today. Food wasn’t just served on a plate. The table had to be prepared. Different dishes placed in the center — rice, meat, root vegetables, sometimes soup… and always beans.

Black beans.

They were my favorite.

---

At home, my mother was the one who cooked. Maybe it was tradition, maybe it was circumstance, maybe simply because she was the one who spent more time there.

But what I know is this:

I loved her cooking.

We also visited other relatives often, and the scene repeated itself — a full table, beans at the center, family gathered around.

But no matter where we went…

> *none of them tasted like my mother’s.*

---

As a child, there are many things you take for granted.

You sit at the table, you eat, you enjoy… but you don’t stop to think about what it means.

I didn’t know then that those meals would stay with me the way they did.

---

I grew older.

Boarding school came, then university. Life moved forward, as it always does.

And somewhere along the way, without even realizing it at first… I began to miss those meals.

Not just the food.

The feeling of them.

And especially those beans.

---

Today, for me, a meal without beans feels incomplete, no matter what else is on the plate.

Life changed. I moved out. Built my own home, my own family.

My wife now takes on most of the cooking. She doesn’t even eat beans… and yet, she still prepares them for me.

And sometimes, half joking, whenever we visited my mother, I would say:

“Today I’m finally going to eat real beans.”

---

My mother passed away two years and eight months ago.

I’ve mentioned her before. I’ve mentioned the beans too.

But the truth is… they are not just food.

They are something bigger.

---

I remember working the land.

Planting. Clearing. Harvesting. Processing.

And then cooking what came from that effort.

When you eat something that has passed through your own hands like that, the taste is different.

Not because of the recipe.

But because it carries something else.

Work.  
Time.  
Family.  
Care.

---

That’s what those beans really were.

Not just a dish.

But a way love was present at the table, every single day, without needing to be said.

---

> *Some meals are remembered for how they tasted. Others… for what they meant.*

---

*Images: Pixabay*  
*Translation: DeepL / Google Translate*

---

Thank you for reading.
Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

---

👉 Daily Hive Journal 🚀

There I share progress, mistakes, and results with no filter.

---

## En Español

Hola comunidad de SilverBloggers!

Esta semana me uno al **prompt semanal Chronicles (Semana 45)**, y en lugar de pensar en una comida extraordinaria, mi memoria regresa a algo mucho más simple… algo que siempre estuvo ahí.

---

## El sabor que nunca se fue  
### *Frijoles negros, familia y todo lo que llevaban dentro*

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbUqwk8J5KoyTEuBhf3neB6zmRUUPNA7dik2WfojoN8VL/dioncerqueira_a_dish_made_of_5160472_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/a-dish-made-of-food-eat-kitchen-5160472/)

---

Desde pequeño crecí en un pueblo de campo. Viajaba con frecuencia a la ciudad, pero al final del día siempre regresaba a casa.

Y en casa, había algo constante.

La mesa.

En aquellos tiempos, la comida no era como hoy. No era solo servir un plato. Había que preparar la mesa, poner varias fuentes — arroz, carne, viandas, a veces sopa… y siempre frijoles.

Frijoles negros.

Mis preferidos.

---

En casa, quien cocinaba era mi mamá. Tal vez por costumbre, por la dinámica familiar o porque pasaba más tiempo allí.

Lo cierto es que me encantaba cómo cocinaba.

Visitábamos también a otros familiares y todo era parecido — la mesa servida, los frijoles en el centro, la familia reunida.

Pero, sin importar dónde fuera…

> *como los de mi mamá, ninguno.*

---

De niño, hay muchas cosas que uno da por sentado.

Te sientas, comes, disfrutas… pero no te detienes a pensar en lo que significa.

En ese momento no lo sabía.

---

Fui creciendo.

Vinieron las becas, luego la universidad. La vida siguió avanzando.

Y en algún punto, casi sin darme cuenta… empecé a extrañar aquellas comidas.

No solo la comida.

La sensación.

Y especialmente aquellos frijoles.

---

Hoy, para mí, un plato de comida sin frijoles está incompleto, tenga lo que tenga.

La vida cambió. Me fui a vivir solo, formé mi familia.

Mi esposa asume en gran medida la cocina. Ella no come frijoles… y aun así me los prepara.

Y en tono de broma, cada vez que visitábamos a mi mamá, yo decía:

“Hoy sí voy a comer frijoles de verdad.”

---

Mi mamá falleció hace ya dos años y ocho meses.

En otros posts la he mencionado. También a los frijoles.

Pero en realidad… no son solo comida.

Son algo más grande.

---

Recuerdo incluso haber trabajado la tierra.

Sembrar. Chapear. Recoger. Procesar.

Y luego cocinar lo que salía de ahí.

Cuando comes algo que pasó por tus propias manos, el sabor es distinto.

No por la receta.

Sino por lo que lleva dentro.

Trabajo.  
Tiempo.  
Familia.  
Cariño.

---

Eso eran realmente aquellos frijoles.

No solo un plato.

Sino una forma en que el amor estaba presente en la mesa todos los días, sin necesidad de decirlo.

---

> *Hay comidas que se recuerdan por su sabor. Otras… por lo que significaron.*

title.title: Do Kids Really Need Allowance?
title.body: As much as I know, parenting differs for every parent. People adopt what they think will be okay for their kid's upbringing, and when it comes to giving kids allowance when they still live on the same roof with their parents and you still provide their meals and pay their bills, the idea differs from each parent's. While some parents only adopt the idea of giving their kids pocket money, others embrace allowance, as it teaches money management and responsibility. ![17782150938838926506407488169304.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nkemakonam89/48WDMGjQr1Ew3rTQNheYV2FBAEafWCQUjuz86PoVSs62UQJSZBFBcmuJ146FUacChp.png) ***** Personally as a parent, I already have a stretched budget; it's a whole lot already with the kind of country I live in that wouldn't allow its citizens to breathe fresh air. I carry a lot of responsibilities for my kids already; the likes of feeding, clothing, medicals, roof, school fees, etc., so adding allowance for them again at least by this stage of their lives seems like an overburden to me. I feel like they need the money for nothing. ***** Maybe it's something I will do when they are of age anyways, but for now, I don't even give them even pocket money, not to talk of allowance. The only money I started allowing them to handle for the sake of learning savings and more is the cash gift their uncles and aunties usually dash them occasionally; otherwise, I make sure to provide every basic need they really need as growing kids. ***** One thing I noticed from the little cash gift under their custody is that they are always taking permission to spend the money on snacks even when their locally constructed piggy bank, where they claim they have learned the importance of savings, is there glaring at them. It's all about what to buy every now and then, and when I give the permission and the money gets exhausted, they will start requesting money from me. Can you imagine, lol. ***** So this way, I feel they are far from learning about money usage. This is why I think that introducing allowance for them when they are of age will be a good idea, where they will have to brainstorm on managing the fixed amount of allowance either weekly or monthly they may receive . I think the main idea of allowance for kids should be teaching them responsibilities; otherwise, they shouldn't start receiving money without proper guidance. If not, it might turn to a total mess along the line. ***** So yeah, I think giving kids allowance is okay when we intentionally use it as a tool for financial education, especially at their early stage in life. No doubt, it will help to prepare them for the real world. A world where earning money isn't so easy and learning money management is a must to survive, so yeah, it makes more sense to raise kids who understand value rather than be on the receiving side. title.title: ¡Presentación en Costa Azul - Danza la tierra! 🌍 [ESP/ENG]
title.body:
>
Bienvenidos! 🙋🏻‍♀️
¡Hola amigos!! ¿Como están?? Espero que muy bien, como siempre les deseo lo mejor, buena salud y prosperidad, por mi parte me encuentro bien gracias a Dios, con poco tiempo para escribir, pero sin dejar este pasatiempo tan bonito al que le tengo un cariño grande y aprecio, hoy les comparto algunas fotos de muchísimas jajaja que tome el día de nuestra presentación en el centro comercial costa azul en celebración del día de la danza!. Nuestra categoría fue infantil, pues en la academia tenemos a niñas pequeñas, fueron tres días de diferentes categorías y estilos de danza, el primero, sería infantil, así que todas las academias de la Isla con pequeñas y pequeños artistas nos unimos para mostrar este hermoso arte, nosotras en ABAMS llevamos una propuesta que sentíamos era justa y necesaria, pues los niños son el futuro, y desde ya es bueno enseñarles sobre lo que está pasando en el mundo, lo que le hemos hecho a la tierra como humanos, y las consecuencias de eso, más, si el futuro es más consiente y ecológico, las cosas podrían mejorar!! En cuanto a los vestuarios y baile en sí, cada niña represento un elemento de la tierra, con un baile lírico -contemporáneo que demostró como la tierra sufría y luego todo mejoro, la idea es crear historia, impacto y conciencia a través de la danza, creo que se logró, se vio hermoso y al público le gusto!. Casi siempre solemos ser los primeros en bailar por nuestras temáticas, esta vez no fue la excepción, abrimos el evento y eso fue magnífico, como ya lo mencione aquí les comparto solo algunas fotos, pues yo normalmente estoy detrás de cámara, grabando videos y tomando fotos en cada presentación, me encanto este día y lo lindo que bailaron las niñas, me despido deseándoles nuevamente lo mejor y que tengan un exitoso día.
ENGLISH

Welcome! 🙋🏻‍♀️
Hello friends!! How are you?? I hope you're all doing well. As always, I wish you the best, good health, and prosperity. I'm doing well, thank God, though I haven't had much time to write, but I haven't abandoned this wonderful hobby that I love and appreciate so much. Today I'm sharing some photos—of the many, haha—that I took on the day of our performance at the Costa Azul shopping center in celebration of International Dance Day! Our category was children's, since we have young girls at the academy. It was a three-day event with different categories and dance styles. The first day was for children, so all the academies on the island with their little artists came together to showcase this beautiful art. We at ABAMS presented a proposal that we felt was fair and necessary, because children are the future, and it's good to start teaching them now about what's happening in the world, what we humans have done to the Earth, and the consequences of that. Furthermore, if the future is more conscious and environmentally friendly, things could improve! Regarding the costumes and the dance itself, each girl represented an element of the earth, with a lyrical-contemporary dance that showed how the earth suffered and then everything improved. The idea is to create a story, an impact, and awareness through dance. I think we achieved that; it looked beautiful, and the audience loved it! We're almost always the first to dance because of our themes, and this time was no exception. We opened the event, and that was magnificent. As I mentioned, I'm only sharing a few photos here, since I'm usually behind the camera, recording videos and taking photos at each performance. I loved this day and how beautifully the girls danced. I'll say goodbye now, wishing you all the best and a successful day.

Days when sales are slow.  
Days when I question myself.

Sometimes growth is simply not giving up.

And honestly, I’m proud of the woman I’m becoming through this process.

More patient.  
More independent.  
More focused on building a better life.

As common as this flower of wetlands or wet soil looks, its artistic composition is just as captivating. The five white petals of this flower in the picture and the yellow color spreading like a sun halo right in the middle are like a perfect work of nature. title.title: Chicken sautéed with garlic and red onion
title.body: >Saludos a todos. Hoy les quiero compartir mi almuerzo de hoy, preparando pechuga de pollo salteada con mucho ajo y cebolla morada, el ajo es un ingrediente bastante fuerte, pero a mi personalmente me encanta su sabor y me encanta agregarle muchísimo ajo, casi siempre me gusta acompañar este pollo con un poco de arroz y tambien puré de papas, pero tambien he probado mezclándolo con salsa bechamel y pasta y queda exquisito. Es una preparación sencilla pero deliciosa. > Hello, everyone. Today I want to share what I had for lunch: sautéed chicken breast with plenty of garlic and red onion. Garlic is a pretty strong ingredient, but I personally love its flavor and I love adding a lot of it. I almost always like to serve this chicken with a little rice and mashed potatoes, but I’ve also tried mixing it with béchamel sauce and pasta, and it turns out delicious. It’s a simple but delicious dish. ![Corazón banner (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alexa.art/23uFgAbHNHepcyH3o8wH15M4pR8K7Jsf3tw4TsSj65zyY1UyQpKRK2L9tGpjABj48Qxzb.png)

>Empecé fileteando las pechugas de pollo para luego picarlas en cuadritos y agregarlas a un sartén con un poco de aceite, tambien al mismo tiempo voy agregando sal y pimienta. > I started by slicing the chicken breasts, then diced them and added them to a skillet with a little oil, seasoning them with salt and pepper as I went. ![primer.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alexa.art/23vi1zqnC9vk6fcvJ1VEYhEzqNZXdRuakUega9TPX6i16tVLTp1wJowqowqdUb8xhQzqU.png)

>Tambien agregue otros condimentos, salsa de soya y salsa inglesa, también me gusta agregarle salsa de ajo pero en ese momento ya no me quedaba y adobo que para mi es algo que nunca puede faltar le da un sabor mas delicioso a todo. Vamos a sofreír el pollo por unos minutos hasta que cambie un poco de color y mientras tanto podemos ir picando el ajo y la cebolla, en este caso use 4 cabezas de ajo y media cebolla morada. > I also added other seasonings, like soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce. I like to add garlic sauce too, but I didn’t have any left at the time. And adobo—which, for me, is an absolute must—gives everything a more delicious flavor. Let’s sauté the chicken for a few minutes until it changes color a bit, and in the meantime, we can chop the garlic and onion. In this case, I used 4 heads of garlic and half a red onion. ![segunda.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alexa.art/23u67B59w4HdJGkRwF9nUxuX9b5MR4YVfNdrH4HuP7aR3HZTcrTzd5qqpHMdC9vm6sQFS.png)

>Despues de picar el ajo y la cebolla, esperare unos minutos para dejar que el pollo se cocine bien y a mi me gusta colocarle un poco de agua y dejarlo secar, cuando ya este secándose, le comienzo a añadir la cebolla y el ajo y dejo sofreír hasta que la cebolla y el ajo estén dorados, una vez listo servir con un delicioso puré de papas y arroz. > After chopping the garlic and onion, I’ll wait a few minutes to let the chicken cook through. I like to add a little water and let it reduce; once it’s starting to thicken, I’ll add the onion and garlic and sauté until they’re golden brown. Once ready, serve with delicious mashed potatoes and rice. ![tercera.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alexa.art/23u6BUiu6fXm7cgPGDTvQTLvTCW3UFWoCAxykrJK5vyXWZiYv65gea34RbHB7zNC8JLHv.png) ![Corazón banner (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alexa.art/23uFgAbHNHepcyH3o8wH15M4pR8K7Jsf3tw4TsSj65zyY1UyQpKRK2L9tGpjABj48Qxzb.png)

>Quedo bastante bueno, lo malo es que se fue la luz mientras cocinaba y no llego nunca, eso me bajo los ánimos un poco cuando ya era la hora de comer porque siempre me gusta acompañar mis comidas viendo algo en la tv jaja.
